export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Shopify client secret for HMAC-SHA256 verification (env: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET) */
  shopifyClientSecret: string
  /** Airtable API key for Bearer authentication (env: AIRTABLE_API_KEY) */
  airtableApiKey: string
  /** Airtable base ID (e.g., appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX) */
  airtableBaseId: string
  /** Airtable table name or ID */
  airtableTableNameOrId: string
  /** Deduplication store for order_id + hmac pairs */
  dedupStore: DedupStore
  /** Injected fetch for testing (defaults to global fetch) */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
  /** Maximum retry attempts after initial request (default: 3) */
  maxRetries?: number
  /** Base retry delay in ms (default: 1000) */
  baseRetryDelayMs?: number
  /** Optional HMAC verification function (defaults to Web Crypto API) */
  verifyHmac?: (rawBody: string, hmacHeader: string, secret: string) => Promise<boolean>
}

export interface DedupStore {
  /** Check if a deduplication key has been seen */
  has(key: string): Promise<boolean>
  /** Record a deduplication key as seen */
  add(key: string): Promise<void>
}

/** Shopify orders/paid webhook payload (UCP format) */
export interface ShopifyOrderPaidPayload {
  id: string
  label: string
  currency: string
  totals: Array<{ type: string; display_text: string; amount: number }>
  line_items: unknown[]
  fulfillment: unknown
  adjustments?: unknown[]
  ucp: unknown
  /** Raw request body for HMAC verification (added by webhook handler) */
  _rawBody?: string
  /** Request headers for HMAC and webhook ID (added by webhook handler) */
  _headers?: Record<string, string>
}

export interface HandleResult {
  /** Airtable record IDs returned by upsert */
  airtableRecordIds: string[]
  /** True if at least one record was created */
  created: boolean
  /** True if at least one record was updated */
  updated: boolean
  /** True if the webhook was deduplicated and not processed */
  deduplicated: boolean
}

interface AirtableUpsertResponse {
  records: Array<{ id: string; createdTime: string; fields: Record<string, unknown> }>
  updatedRecords: string[][]
  createdRecords: string[]
}

function findTotalAmount(payload: ShopifyOrderPaidPayload, type: string): number | null {
  const total = payload.totals.find(t => t.type === type)
  return total ? total.amount : null
}

function extractCustomerEmail(payload: ShopifyOrderPaidPayload): string {
  const fulfillment = payload.fulfillment as Record<string, unknown> | undefined
  const expectations = fulfillment?.expectations as unknown[] | undefined
  if (expectations?.[0]) {
    const dest = (expectations[0] as Record<string, unknown>).destination as Record<string, unknown> | undefined
    if (dest?.email) return String(dest.email)
  }
  return ''
}

async function defaultVerifyHmac(rawBody: string, hmacHeader: string, secret: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const crypto = globalThis.crypto
  if (!crypto?.subtle) {
    throw new Error('Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle) not available; provide verifyHmac in config')
  }
  const encoder = new TextEncoder()
  const keyData = encoder.encode(secret)
  const messageData = encoder.encode(rawBody)
  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', keyData, { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' }, false, ['sign'])
  const signature = await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', key, messageData)
  const signatureHex = Array.from(new Uint8Array(signature))
    .map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0'))
    .join('')
  return signatureHex === hmacHeader.toLowerCase()
}

function parseRetryAfter(header: string | null): number | null {
  if (!header) return null
  const seconds = parseInt(header, 10)
  if (!isNaN(seconds)) return seconds * 1000
  const date = new Date(header)
  if (!isNaN(date.getTime())) {
    const diff = date.getTime() - Date.now()
    return diff > 0 ? diff : null
  }
  return null
}

function isRetryableStatus(status: number): boolean {
  return status === 429 || status >= 500
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ShopifyOrderPaidPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.id) throw new Error('Missing required field: id')
  if (!payload.label) throw new Error('Missing required field: label')
  if (!payload.currency) throw new Error('Missing required field: currency')
  if (!payload.totals || !Array.isArray(payload.totals)) throw new Error('Missing required field: totals')

  const orderId = payload.id
  const orderNumber = payload.label
  const currency = payload.currency

  const totalAmountCents = findTotalAmount(payload, 'total')
  if (totalAmountCents === null) throw new Error('Missing total amount in totals')
  const totalAmount = (totalAmountCents / 100).toFixed(2)

  const customerEmail = extractCustomerEmail(payload)

  const headers = payload._headers ?? {}
  const hmacHeader = headers['x-shopify-hmac-sha256'] ?? headers['X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256'] ?? ''
  const webhookId = headers['x-shopify-webhook-id'] ?? headers['X-Shopify-Webhook-Id'] ?? ''

  // HMAC verification
  let hmacVerified = false
  const verifyHmac = config.verifyHmac ?? defaultVerifyHmac
  if (payload._rawBody && hmacHeader) {
    hmacVerified = await verifyHmac(payload._rawBody, hmacHeader, config.shopifyClientSecret)
    if (!hmacVerified) throw new Error('HMAC verification failed')
  }

  // Deduplication key: orderId + hmac (fallback to webhookId, then orderId alone)
  const dedupKey = hmacHeader ? `${orderId}:${hmacHeader}` : webhookId ? `${orderId}:${webhookId}` : orderId

  const isDuplicate = await config.dedupStore.has(dedupKey)
  if (isDuplicate) {
    return { airtableRecordIds: [], created: false, updated: false, deduplicated: true }
  }

  // Map fields for Airtable upsert
  const fields = {
    'Order Number': orderNumber,
    'Customer Email': customerEmail,
    'Total': totalAmount,
    'HMAC Digest': hmacHeader,
    'Dedup Order ID': orderId
  }

  const url = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${config.airtableBaseId}/${config.airtableTableNameOrId}`
  const body = {
    performUpsert: { fieldsToMergeOn: ['Order Number'] },
    records: [{ fields }]
  }

  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const maxRetries = config.maxRetries ?? 3
  const baseRetryDelayMs = config.baseRetryDelayMs ?? 1000

  let lastError: Error | null = null
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) {
    try {
      const response = await fetch(url, {
        method: 'PATCH',
        headers: {
          'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.airtableApiKey}`,
          'Content-Type': 'application/json'
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(body)
      })

      if (response.status >= 200 && response.status < 300) {
        const data = await response.json() as AirtableUpsertResponse
        await config.dedupStore.add(dedupKey)

        const recordIds = data.records?.map(r => r.id) ?? []
        const updated = data.updatedRecords?.flat() ?? []
        const created = data.createdRecords ?? []

        return {
          airtableRecordIds: recordIds,
          created: created.length > 0,
          updated: updated.length > 0,
          deduplicated: false
        }
      }

      const errorText = await response.text()
      const retryable = isRetryableStatus(response.status)
      if (!retryable || attempt === maxRetries) {
        throw new Error(`Airtable upsert failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} - ${errorText}`)
      }

      const retryAfterMs = parseRetryAfter(response.headers.get('Retry-After'))
      const exponentialMs = baseRetryDelayMs * Math.pow(2, attempt)
      const delayMs = retryAfterMs !== null ? Math.max(retryAfterMs, exponentialMs) : exponentialMs
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs))
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error as Error
      if (attempt === maxRetries) break
      // If it was a non-retryable error, we already threw above
      // Only reach here for retryable errors that we caught
      const retryAfterMs = 0 // Will be recalculated in next iteration if needed
      const exponentialMs = baseRetryDelayMs * Math.pow(2, attempt)
      const delayMs = exponentialMs
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs))
    }
  }

  throw lastError ?? new Error('Airtable upsert failed after retries')
}

# Shopify Orders/Paid → Airtable Upsert Connector

This connector processes Shopify `orders/paid` webhook deliveries, verifies their HMAC-SHA256 signature, deduplicates against prior deliveries, and upserts the order data into Airtable keyed on the **Order Number** field.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a Shopify webhook payload (UCP format) with headers `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` and `X-Shopify-Webhook-Id`.
2. **Verifies** the HMAC-SHA256 signature using the raw request body and the Shopify client secret.
3. **Deduplicates** using a composite key of `order_id + hmac` (falling back to `webhook_id` or `order_id` alone) via a provided `DedupStore`.
4. **Maps** fields to Airtable:
   - `order.id` → `Order Number` (merge key)
   - `order.customer.email` → `Customer Email`
   - `order.total_price` (cents) → `Total` (dollars, two decimals)
   - HMAC header → `HMAC Digest`
   - `order.id` → `Dedup Order ID`
5. **Upserts** to Airtable via `PATCH /v0/{baseId}/{tableNameOrId}` with `performUpsert: { fieldsToMergeOn: ["Order Number"] }`.
6. **Returns** the Airtable record IDs and whether records were created/updated.

## Configuration / Environment Variables

| Config Property | Env Var | Description |
|-----------------|---------|-------------|
| `shopifyClientSecret` | `SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` | Secret used to verify HMAC-SHA256 signatures. |
| `airtableApiKey` | `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` | Bearer token for Airtable API authentication. |
| `airtableBaseId` | — | Airtable base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`). |
| `airtableTableNameOrId` | — | Airtable table name or ID. |
| `dedupStore` | — | Object implementing `has(key)` and `add(key)` for deduplication. |
| `fetch` | — | Optional injected `fetch` (for testing). |
| `maxRetries` | — | Max retry attempts after initial request (default: 3). |
| `baseRetryDelayMs` | — | Base delay for exponential backoff (default: 1000ms). |
| `verifyHmac` | — | Optional custom HMAC verification function. |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, DedupStore } from './connector'

// In-memory deduplication store (replace with Redis, DB, etc. in production)
const dedupStore: DedupStore = {
  store: new Set<string>(),
  async has(key) { return this.store.has(key) },
  async add(key) { this.store.add(key) }
}

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  shopifyClientSecret: process.env.SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET!,
  airtableApiKey: process.env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY!,
  airtableBaseId: 'appYourBaseId',
  airtableTableNameOrId: 'tblYourTableId',
  dedupStore,
  maxRetries: 3,
  baseRetryDelayMs: 1000
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Cloudflare Worker, Express, etc.):
export default {
  async fetch(req: Request) {
    const rawBody = await req.text()
    const payload = JSON.parse(rawBody)
    const headers: Record<string, string> = {}
    req.headers.forEach((v, k) => { headers[k.toLowerCase()] = v })

    const result = await handle({
      ...payload,
      _rawBody: rawBody,
      _headers: headers
    }, config)

    return Response.json(result)
  }
}
```

## Assumptions

- The webhook payload is the full UCP order object as documented by Shopify (see `SOURCE_EXAMPLE` in fixtures).
- HMAC-SHA256 signature is delivered in the `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header; the raw request body is required for verification.
- Deduplication uses a composite key `order_id:hmac` (or `order_id:webhook_id` / `order_id`).
- Airtable table already has a field named **Order Number** that uniquely identifies records.
- Airtable upsert endpoint (`PATCH /v0/{baseId}/{tableNameOrId}`) supports `performUpsert` with `fieldsToMergeOn`.
- The connector runs in an environment with the Web Crypto API (`crypto.subtle`) available for HMAC verification, or a custom `verifyHmac` function is provided.
- Retryable HTTP statuses: 429, 500, 502, 503. Retry-After header may be seconds or HTTP-date.
- Pagination is not needed for the Airtable upsert endpoint (single request).

export function fakeFetch(

): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Salesforce instance URL, e.g. https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com */
  instanceUrl: string;
  /** Salesforce access token (from SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN env var) */
  accessToken: string;
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface HubSpotDealWebhookPayload {
  dealId: string;
  properties: {
    dealname: string;
    amount: string;
    dealstage: string;
    company_name: string;
    domain: string;
    hs_object_id: string;
    [key: string]: unknown;
  };
  eventType: string;
  subscriptionId: string;
  portalId: string;
  occurredAt: number;
}

export interface UpsertResult {
  id: string;
  created: boolean;
}

export interface CreateResult {
  id: string;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  upsert: UpsertResult;
  create?: CreateResult;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: HubSpotDealWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.dealId) throw new Error('Missing required field: dealId');
  if (!payload.properties) throw new Error('Missing required field: properties');
  const { properties } = payload;
  if (!properties.company_name) throw new Error('Missing required field: properties.company_name');
  if (!properties.domain) throw new Error('Missing required field: properties.domain');
  if (!properties.dealname) throw new Error('Missing required field: properties.dealname');
  if (!properties.amount) throw new Error('Missing required field: properties.amount');
  if (!properties.dealstage) throw new Error('Missing required field: properties.dealstage');

  const domain = properties.domain;
  const accountData = {
    Name: properties.company_name,
    Website: domain,
    Account_Name__c: properties.dealname,
    Annual_Revenue: Number(properties.amount),
    StageName: properties.dealstage,
  };

  const upsertUrl = `${config.instanceUrl}/services/data/v68.0/sobjects/Account/Website__c/${encodeURIComponent(domain)}`;
  const headers = {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${config.accessToken}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  };

  // Attempt upsert
  const upsertResponse = await fetchImpl(upsertUrl, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(accountData),
  });

  if (upsertResponse.status === 300) {
    // Multiple matches - fallback to create
    const createUrl = `${config.instanceUrl}/services/data/v68.0/sobjects/Account/`;
    const createResponse = await fetchImpl(createUrl, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers,
      body: JSON.stringify(accountData),
    });
    if (createResponse.status !== 201) {
      const text = await createResponse.text().catch(() => '');
      throw new Error(
        `Salesforce create failed: ${createResponse.status} ${createResponse.statusText} for POST ${createUrl}${text ? ` - ${text}` : ''}`,
      );
    }
    const createJson = (await createResponse.json()) as { id: string; success: boolean; errors: unknown[] };
    if (!createJson.success) {
      throw new Error(`Salesforce create failed: ${JSON.stringify(createJson.errors)}`);
    }
    return {
      upsert: { id: '', created: false },
      create: { id: createJson.id },
    };
  }

  if (upsertResponse.status < 200 || upsertResponse.status >= 300) {
    const text = await upsertResponse.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(
      `Salesforce upsert failed: ${upsertResponse.status} ${upsertResponse.statusText} for PATCH ${upsertUrl}${text ? ` - ${text}` : ''}`,
    );
  }

  const upsertJson = (await upsertResponse.json()) as { id: string; created: boolean; success: boolean; errors: unknown[] };
  if (!upsertJson.success) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce upsert failed: ${JSON.stringify(upsertJson.errors)}`);
  }

  return {
    upsert: { id: upsertJson.id, created: upsertJson.created },
  };
}

# HubSpot Deal Updated → Salesforce Account Upsert

This connector synchronizes HubSpot deal updates to Salesforce Accounts. When a HubSpot deal is updated, it searches Salesforce for an Account by website domain (using the `Website__c` external ID field). If a single match is found, the Account is updated; if no match is found, a new Account is created (via Salesforce upsert behavior). If multiple matches are found (HTTP 300), the connector falls back to creating a new Account via the standard create endpoint.

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration parameters (typically sourced from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|----------------------|-------------|
| `instanceUrl`   | `SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL` | Salesforce instance URL (e.g., `https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com`) |
| `accessToken`   | `SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN` | OAuth access token for Salesforce REST API (Bearer token) |
| `fetch`         | (injected)           | Optional fetch implementation for testing |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, HubSpotDealWebhookPayload } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  instanceUrl: process.env.SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL!,
  accessToken: process.env.SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
};

// In a webhook handler (e.g., Express, AWS Lambda, etc.):
app.post('/hubspot/deal-updated', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const payload = req.body as HubSpotDealWebhookPayload;
    const result = await handle(payload, config);
    res.json({ success: true, result });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Sync failed:', err);
    res.status(500).json({ success: false, error: err.message });
  }
});
```

## Field Mapping

| HubSpot Deal Property | Salesforce Account Field |
|-----------------------|--------------------------|
| `properties.company_name` | `Name` |
| `properties.domain` | `Website` (also used as external ID `Website__c` in upsert URL) |
| `properties.dealname` | `Account_Name__c` |
| `properties.amount` | `Annual_Revenue` (converted to number) |
| `properties.dealstage` | `StageName` |

## Assumptions

1. HubSpot deal properties include `company_name`, `domain`, `dealname`, `amount`, and `dealstage`.
2. Salesforce Account has an External ID field `Website__c` mapped to HubSpot's `domain` property for upsert matching.
3. If no matching Account exists, Salesforce upsert creates a new Account automatically (HTTP 201 with `created: true`).
4. If multiple Accounts match the external ID (HTTP 300), the connector falls back to creating a new Account via the standard create endpoint (`POST /services/data/v68.0/sobjects/Account/`).
5. The integration runs in the order: upsert → if 300 (multiple matches) → create.
6. The webhook payload is delivered via POST with JSON content-type; no authentication is required on the source side.
7. Salesforce API version used is v68.0 (adjust `instanceUrl` if using a different version).
8. The `amount` field from HubSpot is a string representing a number; it is converted to a number for `Annual_Revenue`.
9. The connector validates all required fields and throws descriptive errors if any are missing.
10. Non-2xx responses from Salesforce throw errors including the status code and endpoint for debugging.

 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  hubspotAccessToken: string
  googleSheetsAccessToken: string
  spreadsheetId: string
  sheetRange: string
  hubspotOwnerId: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface CalendlyWebhookPayload {
  event: string
  invitee: {
    email: string
  }
  start_time: string
  cancellation_reason: string
  status: string
  canceled: boolean
  rescheduled: boolean
}

export interface HandleResult {
  hubspotEngagementId: string | null
  deleted: boolean
  googleSheetsAppended: boolean
}

async function searchHubSpotEngagement(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  startTime: string,
  ownerId: string
): Promise<{ id: string; properties: Record<string, string> } | null> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = 'https://api.hubspot.com/crm/v3/objects/communications/search'
  const body = {
    filterGroups: [
      {
        filters: [
          { propertyName: 'hs_timestamp', operator: 'EQ', value: startTime },
          { propertyName: 'hubspot_owner_id', operator: 'EQ', value: ownerId }
        ]
      }
    ],
    properties: ['hs_timestamp', 'hs_communication_body', 'hubspot_owner_id'],
    limit: 10
  }

  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.hubspotAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`HubSpot search failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = await response.json() as { results: Array<{ id: string; properties: Record<string, string> }>; total: number }
  return data.results[0] ?? null
}

async function deleteHubSpotEngagement(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  engagementId: string
): Promise<void> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://api.hubspot.com/engagements/v1/engagements/${engagementId}`

  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'DELETE',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.hubspotAccessToken}`
    }
  })

  if (!response.ok && response.status !== 204) {
    throw new Error(`HubSpot delete failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
}

async function appendToGoogleSheets(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  row: string[]
): Promise<void> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/${config.spreadsheetId}/values/${encodeURIComponent(config.sheetRange)}:append`
  const body = {
    majorDimension: 'ROWS',
    values: [row]
  }

  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.googleSheetsAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Google Sheets append failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: CalendlyWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.event || payload.event !== 'invitee.canceled') {
    throw new Error('Only invitee.canceled events are supported')
  }
  if (!payload.invitee?.email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: invitee.email')
  }
  if (!payload.start_time) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: start_time')
  }
  if (payload.cancellation_reason === undefined) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: cancellation_reason')
  }

  const email = payload.invitee.email
  const startTime = payload.start_time
  const cancellationReason = payload.cancellation_reason
  const logTimestamp = new Date().toISOString()

  let hubspotEngagementId: string | null = null
  let deleted = false

  const engagement = await searchHubSpotEngagement(config, startTime, config.hubspotOwnerId)
  if (engagement) {
    hubspotEngagementId = engagement.id
    await deleteHubSpotEngagement(config, engagement.id)
    deleted = true
  }

  await appendToGoogleSheets(config, [email, startTime, cancellationReason, logTimestamp])

  return {
    hubspotEngagementId,
    deleted,
    googleSheetsAppended: true
  }
}

# Calendly Meeting Cancellation → HubSpot Engagement Deletion + Google Sheets Audit Log

This connector processes Calendly `invitee.canceled` webhooks, finds and deletes the matching HubSpot engagement using the invitee email and meeting start time as a composite key, then appends an audit row to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a Calendly webhook payload (POST to your configured receiver URL)
2. **Validates** the event is `invitee.canceled` and required fields are present
3. **Searches** HubSpot Communications API for an engagement matching the `start_time` and configured `hubspotOwnerId`
4. **Deletes** the found engagement via HubSpot Engagements API
5. **Logs** the cancellation (email, start time, reason, log timestamp) to Google Sheets

## Configuration

All secrets are provided via the `ConnectorConfig` object at runtime. Typical environment variable mapping:

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `hubspotAccessToken` | `HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN` | HubSpot private app access token (Bearer) |
| `googleSheetsAccessToken` | `GOOGLE_SHEETS_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Google OAuth2 access token with Sheets scope (Bearer) |
| `spreadsheetId` | `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID` | The Google Sheets spreadsheet ID (from URL) |
| `sheetRange` | `GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGE` | A1 notation range for the table header, e.g. `Sheet1!A1` |
| `hubspotOwnerId` | `HUBSPOT_OWNER_ID` | The HubSpot owner ID used to scope the engagement search |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  hubspotAccessToken: process.env.HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  googleSheetsAccessToken: process.env.GOOGLE_SHEETS_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  spreadsheetId: process.env.GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID!,
  sheetRange: process.env.GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGE!,
  hubspotOwnerId: process.env.HUBSPOT_OWNER_ID!
}

// In your webhook handler (Express, Fastify, etc.):
app.post('/webhook/receiver', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ success: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err)
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions & Limitations

- **Calendly payload** must include `invitee.email`, `start_time` (ISO 8601), and `cancellation_reason` (may be empty string).
- **HubSpot search** uses the Communications search endpoint with `hs_timestamp` (exact match) and `hubspot_owner_id`. There is no direct email filter; the connector assumes the timestamp + owner context uniquely identifies the engagement.
- **HubSpot delete** uses the Engagements v1 API (`/engagements/v1/engagements/{id}`) which returns 204 No Content on success.
- **Google Sheets** expects a sheet with columns: Email, Start Time, Cancellation Reason, Log Timestamp (in that order). The `sheetRange` should point to the header row (e.g., `Sheet1!A1`).
- **Authentication**: All three APIs use Bearer tokens. Tokens must be valid and have appropriate scopes.
- **Error handling**: Non-2xx responses from any target throw descriptive errors including status code and endpoint. The webhook handler should return 4xx/5xx accordingly so Calendly can retry per its policy.
- **Idempotency**: The connector does not implement idempotency keys; duplicate webhook deliveries will attempt duplicate deletes (HubSpot returns 404 on second delete) and duplicate sheet rows.

export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload {
  id: string;
  customer: {
    email: string;
  };
  lines: {
    data: Array<{
      description: string;
      amount: number; // cents
      quantity?: number;
    }>;
  };
  hosted_invoice_url: string;
  status: string;
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  realmId: string;
  accessToken: string;
  customerEmailToId: Record<string, string>;
  customFieldDefinitionId: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  invoiceId: string;
  attachmentId?: string;
}

async function postJson<T>(
  url: string,
  body: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  endpointName: string
): Promise<T> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const res = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.accessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(`${endpointName} failed with ${res.status}: ${text}`);
  }

  return res.json() as Promise<T>;
}

function centsToDollars(cents: number): number {
  return Math.round(cents / 100 * 100) / 100; // avoid floating point issues
}

function generateSimplePdf(text: string): string {
  // Minimal PDF with one page, Helvetica font, text at (72,720)
  const escaped = text.replace(/[\\()\r]/g, (c) => `\\${c.charCodeAt(0).toString(8).padStart(3, '0')}`);
  const content = `BT /F1 12 Tf 72 720 Td (${escaped}) Tj ET`;
  const length = content.length;
  const pdf = `%PDF-1.4
1 0 obj
<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>
endobj
2 0 obj
<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>
endobj
3 0 obj
<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] /Contents 4 0 R /Resources << /Font << /F1 5 0 R >> >> >>
endobj
4 0 obj
<< /Length ${length} >>
stream
${content}
endstream
endobj
5 0 obj
<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>
endobj
xref
0 6
0000000000 65535 f
0000000010 00000 n
0000000060 00000 n
0000000117 00000 n
0000000230 00000 n
0000000330 00000 n
trailer
<< /Size 6 /Root 1 0 R >>
startxref
${400 + length}
%%EOF`;
  // base64 encode
  const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(pdf);
  const chars = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/';
  let result = '';
  let i = 0;
  while (i < bytes.length) {
    const chunk = (bytes[i++] << 16) | ((bytes[i++] ?? 0) << 8) | (bytes[i++] ?? 0);
    result += chars[(chunk >> 18) & 63];
    result += chars[(chunk >> 12) & 63];
    result += chars[(chunk >> 6) & 63] || '=';
    result += chars[chunk & 63] || '=';
  }
  return result;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.id) throw new Error('Missing required field: id');
  if (!payload.customer?.email) throw new Error('Missing required field: customer.email');
  if (!payload.lines?.data?.length) throw new Error('Missing required field: lines.data (must be non-empty array)');
  if (!payload.hosted_invoice_url) throw new Error('Missing required field: hosted_invoice_url');

  const customerId = config.customerEmailToId[payload.customer.email];
  if (!customerId) {
    throw new Error(`No QuickBooks customer ID mapped for email: ${payload.customer.email}`);
  }

  // Build line items
  const lineItems = payload.lines.data.map((line) => {
    const amountDollars = centsToDollars(line.amount);
    const qty = line.quantity ?? 1;
    const unitPrice = qty > 0 ? Math.round((amountDollars / qty) * 100) / 100 : 0;
    return {
      Description: line.description,
      Amount: amountDollars,
      DetailType: 'SalesItemLineDetail',
      SalesItemLineDetail: {
        Qty: qty,
        UnitPrice: unitPrice,
      },
    };
  });

  // Create invoice
  const invoiceUrl = `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/${config.realmId}/invoice`;
  const invoiceBody = {
    DocNumber: payload.id,
    CustomerRef: {
      value: customerId,
      name: payload.customer.email,
    },
    Line: lineItems,
    CustomField: [
      {
        DefinitionId: config.customFieldDefinitionId,
        StringValue: payload.hosted_invoice_url,
      },
    ],
  };

  interface InvoiceResponse {
    Invoice: {
      Id: string;
      DocNumber: string;
      TxnDate: string;
      Balance: number;
    };
  }

  const invoiceRes = await postJson<InvoiceResponse>(invoiceUrl, invoiceBody, config, 'Create Invoice');
  const invoiceId = invoiceRes.Invoice.Id;

  // Attach document (PDF with Stripe invoice URL)
  const attachmentUrl = `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/${config.realmId}/attachment`;
  const pdfBase64 = generateSimplePdf(`Stripe Invoice URL: ${payload.hosted_invoice_url}`);
  const attachmentBody = {
    AttachableRef: [
      {
        EntityRef: {
          type: 'Invoice',
          value: invoiceId,
        },
      },
    ],
    FileName: 'stripe-invoice.pdf',
    ContentType: 'application/pdf',
    Body: pdfBase64,
  };

  interface AttachmentResponse {
    Attachment: {
      Id: string;
      FileName: string;
      ContentType: string;
    };
  }

  const attachmentRes = await postJson<AttachmentResponse>(attachmentUrl, attachmentBody, config, 'Attach Document');
  const attachmentId = attachmentRes.Attachment.Id;

  return { invoiceId, attachmentId };
}

# Stripe Invoice to QuickBooks Connector

This connector processes Stripe `invoice.finalized` webhook events and creates corresponding invoices in QuickBooks Online, including line items and an attachment referencing the original Stripe invoice URL.

## What it does

1. Receives a Stripe `invoice.finalized` webhook payload.
2. Validates required fields (invoice ID, customer email, line items, hosted invoice URL).
3. Maps the Stripe customer email to a QuickBooks customer ID using a provided mapping.
4. Creates a QuickBooks invoice via the QuickBooks Accounting API:
   - Uses the Stripe invoice ID as `DocNumber`.
   - References the QuickBooks customer via `CustomerRef`.
   - Converts each Stripe line item (amount in cents, optional quantity) to QuickBooks line items with `Amount` in dollars, `Qty`, and `UnitPrice`.
   - Stores the Stripe `hosted_invoice_url` in a QuickBooks custom field (requires a known `DefinitionId`).
5. Attaches a generated PDF document to the created QuickBooks invoice containing the Stripe invoice URL.

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration (provided via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Property | Description | Environment Variable |
|----------|-------------|----------------------|
| `realmId` | QuickBooks company realm ID (found in company settings or OAuth callback) | `QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID` |
| `accessToken` | OAuth 2.0 access token for QuickBooks API | `QUICKBOOKS_ACCESS_TOKEN` |
| `customerEmailToId` | Object mapping Stripe customer emails to QuickBooks customer IDs (e.g., `{"jenny@example.com": "123"}`) | — (provide at runtime) |
| `customFieldDefinitionId` | QuickBooks custom field definition ID used to store the Stripe invoice URL | — (provide at runtime) |
| `fetch` | Optional injected `fetch` implementation (for testing or non-standard environments) | — |

**Secrets**: Never hard‑code `accessToken` or `realmId`. Load them from environment variables or a secret manager at runtime.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload } from './connector';

// Example webhook payload (from Stripe)
const payload: StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload = {
  id: 'in_1MtHbELkdIwHu7ixl4OzzPMv',
  customer: { email: 'jennyrosen@example.com' },
  lines: {
    data: [
      { description: 'Consulting services', amount: 10000, quantity: 2 },
      { description: 'Software license', amount: 5000, quantity: 1 },
    ],
  },
  hosted_invoice_url: 'https://pay.stripe.com/invoice/in_1MtHbELkdIwHu7ixl4OzzPMv',
  status: 'open',
};

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  realmId: process.env.QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID!,
  accessToken: process.env.QUICKBOOKS_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  customerEmailToId: { 'jennyrosen@example.com': '123' },
  customFieldDefinitionId: '1',
};

const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log('Created QuickBooks invoice:', result.invoiceId);
console.log('Attached document:', result.attachmentId);
```

## Assumptions & Notes

- **Stripe webhook signature verification** is not performed by this connector; implement it upstream (e.g., in your webhook handler) using the Stripe signing secret.
- **QuickBooks customer must exist** before invoice creation. The connector does not create customers; it only maps emails to existing QuickBooks customer IDs via `customerEmailToId`.
- **Custom field definition** (`customFieldDefinitionId`) must be created in QuickBooks beforehand (via the UI or the Custom Field API) and its ID known at configuration time.
- **Amount conversion**: Stripe line item amounts are in cents (integer). The connector converts to dollars (decimal) for QuickBooks. `UnitPrice` is derived as `Amount / Qty`.
- **Quantity default**: If a Stripe line item lacks `quantity`, it defaults to `1`.
- **PDF attachment**: A minimal PDF containing the Stripe invoice URL is generated and attached. For production use, consider replacing the PDF generator with a proper rendering of the Stripe invoice page.
- **Error handling**: The connector throws descriptive errors for missing fields, missing customer mappings, and non‑2xx API responses (including status code and endpoint name).
- **Retry logic**: Not implemented. If you need retries for 429/5xx responses, wrap the `handle` call with your own retry policy.
- **Pagination**: Not applicable (single invoice creation + single attachment).

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  asanaAccessToken: string
  workspaceGid: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface JotformSubmissionPayload {
  formTitle: string
  field_answers: Record<string, string>
}

export interface AsanaTaskResponse {
  gid: string
  name: string
  description: string
  resource_type: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  taskId: string
  taskName: string
}

export async function handle(
  payload: JotformSubmissionPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.formTitle || typeof payload.formTitle !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: formTitle')
  }
  if (!payload.field_answers || typeof payload.field_answers !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: field_answers')
  }

  const description = JSON.stringify(payload.field_answers, null, 2)

  const requestBody = {
    data: {
      name: payload.formTitle,
      description,
      workspace: config.workspaceGid,
    },
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.asanaAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(requestBody),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      `Asana API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks`,
    )
  }

  const result = (await response.json()) as { data: AsanaTaskResponse }
  return {
    taskId: result.data.gid,
    taskName: result.data.name,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Jotform to Asana Task Connector

Creates an Asana task from a Jotform submission webhook. The form title becomes the task name, and all field answers are serialized as a JSON string in the task description.

## Configuration

| Config Key | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `asanaAccessToken` | `ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | Personal access token from Asana Developer Console |
| `workspaceGid` | (none) | Yes | Asana workspace GID (obtain via `/workspaces` endpoint) |

## Usage

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  asanaAccessToken: process.env.ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  workspaceGid: '1234567890123456',
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(jotformPayload, config)
console.log(`Created task ${result.taskId}: ${result.taskName}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Jotform webhook payload has already been parsed from multipart/form-data, with the JSON content extracted from the `rawRequest` field. The connector receives a plain object with `formTitle` and `field_answers`.
- The Asana API accepts `name` (string) and `description` (string) in the `data` object, plus a required `workspace` GID.
- Field answers are serialized to a pretty-printed JSON string for the description field.
- Authentication uses a Bearer token via the `Authorization` header.
- No project ID or additional Asana metadata is required beyond the workspace GID.

  method: string

  url: string
  response: unknown

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',

}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Notion integration token with write access to the target database. */
  notionToken: string;
  /** Notion database ID for the 'Signed' database. */
  notionDatabaseId: string;
  /** Pipedrive API token for fetching user details. */
  pipedriveApiToken: string;
  /** Base URL for Pipedrive API v2. Defaults to https://api.pipedrive.com/v2. */
  pipedriveApiBaseUrl?: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface PipedriveWebhookPayload {
  data: {
    id: number;
    title: string;
    value: number;
    owner_id: number;
    won_time: string;
    status: string;
    close_time: string | null;
    [key: string]: unknown;
  };
  previous: unknown;
  meta: {
    event: string;
    entity: string;
    action: string;
    timestamp: string;
    [key: string]: unknown;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  notionPageId: string;
  dealId: number;
}

async function fetchOwnerName(
  ownerId: number,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<string> {
  const baseUrl = config.pipedriveApiBaseUrl ?? 'https://api.pipedrive.com/v2';
  const url = `${baseUrl}/users/${ownerId}`;
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.pipedriveApiToken}`,
      'Accept': 'application/json',
    },
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Pipedrive API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for GET ${url}`);
  }
  const data = await response.json() as { data?: { name?: string } };
  if (!data.data?.name) {
    throw new Error(`Pipedrive user ${ownerId} has no name field`);
  }
  return data.data.name;
}

function formatDateForNotion(isoString: string): string {
  return isoString.split('T')[0];
}

export async function handle(
  payload: PipedriveWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  if (!payload.data?.title) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.title');
  if (payload.data.value === undefined || payload.data.value === null) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.value');
  if (!payload.data.owner_id) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.owner_id');
  if (!payload.data.won_time) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.won_time');
  if (payload.data.status !== 'won') throw new Error('Deal status is not won');

  const ownerName = await fetchOwnerName(payload.data.owner_id, config);
  const closeDate = formatDateForNotion(payload.data.won_time);

  const notionBody = {
    parent: { database_id: config.notionDatabaseId },
    properties: {
      Title: {
        title: [{ text: { content: payload.data.title } }],
      },
      'Deal Value': {
        number: payload.data.value,
      },
      Owner: {
        rich_text: [{ text: { content: ownerName } }],
      },
      'Close Date': {
        date: { start: closeDate },
      },
    },
  };

  const response = await fetchFn('https://api.notion.com/v1/pages', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.notionToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Notion-Version': '2022-06-28',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(notionBody),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text();
    throw new Error(`Notion API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://api.notion.com/v1/pages - ${errorText}`);
  }

  const result = await response.json() as { id: string };
  return { notionPageId: result.id, dealId: payload.data.id };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Pipedrive Won Deal to Notion Page Connector

Creates a Notion page in the "Signed" database when a Pipedrive deal is moved to the Won stage.

## What it does

Listens for Pipedrive `deal.won` webhook events. When triggered:
1. Validates the deal has status `won` and required fields (title, value, owner_id, won_time)
2. Fetches the owner's display name from Pipedrive API using the `owner_id`
3. Creates a page in the configured Notion database with:
   - **Title** (title property) → deal title
   - **Deal Value** (number property) → deal value
   - **Owner** (rich_text property) → owner's full name
   - **Close Date** (date property) → won_time date portion (YYYY-MM-DD)

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `notionToken` | `NOTION_TOKEN` | Yes | Notion integration token with write access to the target database |
| `notionDatabaseId` | `NOTION_DATABASE_ID` | Yes | The Notion database ID for the "Signed" database |
| `pipedriveApiToken` | `PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN` | Yes | Pipedrive API token (personal or OAuth) for fetching user details |
| `pipedriveApiBaseUrl` | `PIPEDRIVE_API_BASE_URL` | No | Base URL for Pipedrive API v2 (default: `https://api.pipedrive.com/v2`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  notionToken: process.env.NOTION_TOKEN!,
  notionDatabaseId: process.env.NOTION_DATABASE_ID!,
  pipedriveApiToken: process.env.PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN!,
};

const payload = await req.json(); // Pipedrive webhook payload
const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log(`Created Notion page ${result.notionPageId} for deal ${result.dealId}`);
```

## Assumptions

- The Notion database "Signed" already exists and has properties named exactly:
  - **Title** (type: title)
  - **Deal Value** (type: number)
  - **Owner** (type: rich_text)
  - **Close Date** (type: date)
- The Pipedrive webhook payload includes `data.title`, `data.value`, `data.owner_id`, `data.won_time`, and `data.status === 'won'`
- The Pipedrive API token has permission to read users (`GET /api/v2/users/{id}`)
- The Notion integration token has permission to create pages in the target database
- The webhook is configured in Pipedrive to fire on `deal.won` events

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  githubOwner: string
  githubRepo: string
  githubToken: string
  zendeskSubdomain: string
  zendeskAccessToken: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ZendeskWebhookPayload {
  type: string
  account_id: number
  id: string
  time: string
  zendesk_event_version: string
  subject: string
  detail: {
    id: string
    subject: string
    description: string
    requester_id: string
    submitter_id: string
    assignee_id: string | null
    status: string
    priority: string
    group_id: number | null
    organization_id: number | null
    brand_id: number | null
    tags: string[]
    created_at: string
    updated_at: string
    type: string
    via: {
      channel: string
    }
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  githubIssueUrl: string
  zendeskCommentId: number
}

async function postJson<T>(
  url: string,
  body: unknown,
  token: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-GitHub-Api-Version': '2022-11-28',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GitHub API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${url}`)
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<T>
}

async function putJson<T>(
  url: string,
  body: unknown,
  token: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'PUT',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Zendesk API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${url}`)
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<T>
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ZendeskWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.detail?.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.id (ticket ID)')
  }
  if (!payload.detail?.subject) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.subject (ticket subject)')
  }
  if (!payload.detail?.description) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.description (ticket description)')
  }

  const ticketId = payload.detail.id
  const title = payload.detail.subject
  const body = payload.detail.description

  const githubUrl = `https://api.github.com/repos/${config.githubOwner}/${config.githubRepo}/issues`
  const githubResponse = await postJson<{ html_url: string }>(githubUrl, { title, body }, config.githubToken, fetchFn)

  const commentBody = `GitHub issue created: ${githubResponse.html_url}`
  const zendeskUrl = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/${ticketId}.json`
  const zendeskResponse = await putJson<{
    ticket: {
      id: number
      comment: {
        id: number
        body: string
        public: boolean
        created_at: string
      }
    }
  }>(zendeskUrl, { ticket: { comment: { body: commentBody, public: true } } }, config.zendeskAccessToken, fetchFn)

  return {
    githubIssueUrl: githubResponse.html_url,
    zendeskCommentId: zendeskResponse.ticket.comment.id,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Zendesk to GitHub Issue Connector

This connector bridges Zendesk ticket creation events to GitHub issue creation, then posts the GitHub issue URL back to the originating Zendesk ticket as a public comment.

## What it does

1. Receives a `ticket.created` webhook payload from Zendesk
2. Creates a GitHub issue in the configured repository using the ticket subject as the issue title and the ticket description as the issue body
3. Posts a comment on the original Zendesk ticket with the GitHub issue URL

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration values, typically sourced from environment variables:

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `githubOwner` | `GITHUB_OWNER` | GitHub repository owner (user or organization) |
| `githubRepo` | `GITHUB_REPO` | GitHub repository name |
| `githubToken` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub personal access token or GitHub App token with `issues:write` permission |
| `zendeskSubdomain` | `ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN` | Your Zendesk account subdomain (e.g., `mycompany` for `mycompany.zendesk.com`) |
| `zendeskAccessToken` | `ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Zendesk API token with `ticket:write` scope |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  githubOwner: process.env.GITHUB_OWNER!,
  githubRepo: process.env.GITHUB_REPO!,
  githubToken: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN!,
  zendeskSubdomain: process.env.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN!,
  zendeskAccessToken: process.env.ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(zendeskWebhookPayload, config)
console.log(`Created GitHub issue: ${result.githubIssueUrl}`)
console.log(`Posted Zendesk comment: ${result.zendeskCommentId}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Zendesk account has a webhook configured for `ticket.created` events, delivering payloads to this connector's endpoint
- The GitHub repository exists and the provided token has permission to create issues in it
- The Zendesk ticket description contains sufficient context to serve as the GitHub issue body
- The final comment is posted as a public comment visible to the ticket requester
- The webhook payload includes `detail.id`, `detail.subject`, and `detail.description` fields
- No authentication is performed on the incoming webhook; securing the webhook URL is the responsibility of the receiver

  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [

        }

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
