export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Salesforce instance base URL, e.g. https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com */
  instanceUrl: string
  /** Bearer access token for Salesforce REST API */
  accessToken: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing; defaults to global fetch */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface HubSpotDealWebhookPayload {
  subscriptionId: string
  portalId: string
  eventId: string
  subscriptionType: string
  attemptNumber: number
  objectId: string
  objectTypeId: string
  changeSource: string
  timestamp: number
  propertyName: string
  propertyValue: string
  previousPropertyValue: string
  object: {
    id: string
    properties: {
      dealname?: string
      amount?: string
      closedate?: string
      website?: string
      hubspot_owner_id?: string
      [key: string]: string | undefined
    }
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  salesforceAccountId: string
  action: 'upserted' | 'created'
  website: string
  dealId: string
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch
}

function buildHeaders(accessToken: string): HeadersInit {
  return {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  }
}

/** Encodes a value for Salesforce URL usage: spaces become +, other chars percent-encoded. */
function encodeForSalesforce(value: string): string {
  return encodeURIComponent(value).replace(/%20/g, '+')
}

async function searchAccountByWebsite(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  website: string,
): Promise<{ totalSize: number; records: Array<{ Id: string; Website: string }> }> {
  const encodedWebsite = encodeForSalesforce(website)
  const base = config.instanceUrl ? config.instanceUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '') : ''
  const url = `${base}/services/data/v60.0/query?q=SELECT+Id,Website+FROM+Account+WHERE+Website+%3D+'${encodedWebsite}'`
  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: buildHeaders(config.accessToken),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce SOQL search failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  return response.json() as Promise<{ totalSize: number; records: Array<{ Id: string; Website: string }> }>
}

async function upsertAccount(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  website: string,
  dealId: string,
): Promise<string> {
  const encodedWebsite = encodeForSalesforce(website)
  const base = config.instanceUrl ? config.instanceUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '') : ''
  const url = `${base}/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account/Website__c/${encodedWebsite}`
  const body = {
    Deal_ID__c: dealId,
    Description: 'Synced from HubSpot deal',
  }
  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: buildHeaders(config.accessToken),
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce Account upsert failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  const data = (await response.json()) as { id: string; success: boolean; errors?: unknown[] }
  if (!data.success) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce Account upsert returned success=false: ${JSON.stringify(data.errors)}`)
  }
  return data.id
}

async function createAccount(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  website: string,
  dealId: string,
  dealName?: string,
): Promise<string> {
  const base = config.instanceUrl ? config.instanceUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '') : ''
  const url = `${base}/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account/`
  const body = {
    Name: dealName ?? `HubSpot Deal ${dealId}`,
    Website: website,
    Deal_ID__c: dealId,
    Description: 'Created from HubSpot deal sync',
  }
  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: buildHeaders(config.accessToken),
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce Account create failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  const data = (await response.json()) as { id: string; success: boolean; errors?: unknown[] }
  if (!data.success) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce Account create returned success=false: ${JSON.stringify(data.errors)}`)
  }
  return data.id
}

export async function handle(
  payload: HubSpotDealWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.object?.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: object.id (HubSpot deal ID)')
  }
  if (!payload.object?.properties?.website) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: object.properties.website (HubSpot deal website)')
  }

  const dealId = payload.object.id
  const website = payload.object.properties.website
  const dealName = payload.object.properties.dealname

  const searchResult = await searchAccountByWebsite(config, website)

  if (searchResult.totalSize === 0) {
    const accountId = await createAccount(config, website, dealId, dealName)
    return {
      salesforceAccountId: accountId,
      action: 'created',
      website,
      dealId,
    }
  }

  if (searchResult.totalSize === 1) {
    const accountId = await upsertAccount(config, website, dealId)
    return {
      salesforceAccountId: accountId,
      action: 'upserted',
      website,
      dealId,
    }
  }

  throw new Error(`Multiple Salesforce Accounts found for website ${website} (count: ${searchResult.totalSize}). Expected unique Website field.`)
}

# HubSpot Deal → Salesforce Account Sync

This connector synchronizes HubSpot deal updates to Salesforce Accounts. When a HubSpot deal is updated (via the `deal.propertyChange` webhook), it searches Salesforce for an Account matching the deal's website domain. If found, it upserts the Account; otherwise, it creates a new one.

## What it does

1. Receives a HubSpot deal property change webhook payload
2. Extracts the website domain from `deal.properties.website`
3. Executes a SOQL query on Salesforce: `SELECT Id, Website FROM Account WHERE Website = '{website}'`
4. If exactly one Account matches:
   - Upserts using the external ID field `Website__c` (PATCH `/sobjects/Account/Website__c/{website}`)
   - Updates `Deal_ID__c` and `Description` fields
5. If no Account matches:
   - Creates a new Account (POST `/sobjects/Account/`)
   - Sets `Name` (from deal name), `Website`, `Deal_ID__c`, and `Description`
6. Returns the Salesforce Account ID and action taken (`upserted` | `created`)

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `instanceUrl` | `SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL` | Salesforce instance base URL (e.g., `https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com`) |
| `accessToken` | `SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN` | OAuth Bearer access token for Salesforce REST API |
| `fetch` | — | Optional injected fetch implementation for testing |

The access token must be obtained via Salesforce OAuth (username-password flow, client credentials, or JWT bearer flow) and refreshed as needed by the caller.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  instanceUrl: process.env.SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL!,
  accessToken: process.env.SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker)
app.post('/hubspot/webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ success: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Sync failed:', err)
    res.status(500).json({ success: false, error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The HubSpot deal has a `website` property containing the domain to match against Salesforce Account records.
- Salesforce Accounts have a unique `Website` field (standard or custom) that can be used for exact matching.
- The `Website__c` custom field on Account is configured as an **External ID** field in Salesforce setup (required for upsert).
- HubSpot deal update webhook fires with full deal property data on each change.
- The `Website` field values are unique across Accounts (if multiple matches found, the connector throws an error).
- The caller is responsible for token refresh and webhook endpoint security (HubSpot does not sign webhooks).

## Field Mapping

| HubSpot Field | Salesforce Field | Notes |
|---------------|------------------|-------|
| `deal.properties.website` | `Website` (search) / `Website__c` (upsert key) | Domain used to find or create Account |
| `deal.id` | `Deal_ID__c` | HubSpot deal ID stored on Account for reference |
| `deal.properties.dealname` | `Name` (on create only) | Fallback: `HubSpot Deal {dealId}` |

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` for missing required fields (`object.id`, `object.properties.website`)
- Throws on non-2xx responses from Salesforce with status code and endpoint
- Throws when multiple Accounts match the same website (data integrity issue)
- Caller should catch and return appropriate HTTP status to HubSpot (5xx triggers HubSpot retry)

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Brevo API key with permissions to create contacts and manage lists. */
  brevoApiKey: string
  /** The Brevo contact list ID to subscribe the contact to. */
  brevoListId: number
  /** Optional injected fetch for testing. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface TypeformWebhookPayload {
  event_id: string
  event_type: string
  form_response: {
    form_id: string
    token: string
    submitted_at: string
    answers: Array<{
      type: string
      email?: string
      text?: string
      field: {
        id: string
        type: string
      }
    }>
    hidden: Record<string, unknown>
  }
}

export interface BrevoContactResponse {
  id: number
}

export interface HandleResult {
  brevoContactId: number
}

function extractEmail(answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers']): string | undefined {
  const emailAnswer = answers.find((a) => a.field.type === 'email' && a.email)
  return emailAnswer?.email
}

function extractShortTextAnswers(answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers']): string[] {
  return answers
    .filter((a) => a.field.type === 'short_text' && typeof a.text === 'string')
    .map((a) => a.text as string)
}

export async function handle(
  payload: TypeformWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload?.form_response) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_response')
  }
  if (!payload.form_response.token) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_response.token')
  }
  if (!payload.form_response.answers || !Array.isArray(payload.form_response.answers)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_response.answers')
  }

  const email = extractEmail(payload.form_response.answers)
  if (!email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: email (no answer with field.type === "email")')
  }

  const shortTexts = extractShortTextAnswers(payload.form_response.answers)
  const firstName = shortTexts[0] ?? ''
  const lastName = shortTexts[1] ?? ''

  const brevoPayload = {
    email,
    attributes: {
      FNAME: firstName,
      LNAME: lastName,
    },
    listIds: [config.brevoListId],
    updateEnabled: true,
  }

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const url = 'https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts'
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    'api-key': config.brevoApiKey,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    Accept: 'application/json',
  }

  const maxRetries = 3
  let lastError: Error | undefined

  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) {
    const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers,
      body: JSON.stringify(brevoPayload),
    })

    if (response.status >= 200 && response.status < 300) {
      const data = (await response.json()) as BrevoContactResponse
      return { brevoContactId: data.id }
    }

    if (response.status === 429 || (response.status >= 500 && response.status < 600)) {
      const retryAfter = response.headers.get('retry-after')
      let delayMs: number
      if (retryAfter) {
        const asSeconds = Number(retryAfter)
        if (!Number.isNaN(asSeconds)) {
          delayMs = asSeconds * 1000
        } else {
          const date = new Date(retryAfter)
          delayMs = Number.isNaN(date.getTime()) ? 0 : date.getTime() - Date.now()
        }
      } else {
        delayMs = 0
      }
      const baseMs = 1000
      const exponentialMs = baseMs * 2 ** attempt
      const finalDelay = Math.max(delayMs, exponentialMs)
      if (finalDelay > 0 && attempt < maxRetries) {
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, finalDelay))
      }
      lastError = new Error(`Brevo API returned ${response.status} at ${url}`)
      continue
    }

    const text = await response.text().catch(() => '')
    throw new Error(`Brevo API error ${response.status} at ${url}: ${text}`)
  }

  throw lastError ?? new Error(`Brevo API failed after ${maxRetries + 1} attempts at ${url}`)
}

# Typeform to Brevo Connector

Creates or updates a contact in Brevo and subscribes them to a specified list when a Typeform response is submitted.

## What it does

1. Receives a Typeform webhook payload (form response submission)
2. Extracts the respondent's email, first name, last name, and response ID from the payload
3. Calls the Brevo API to create/update a contact with those details
4. Subscribes the contact to a configured Brevo list

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `brevoApiKey` | `BREVO_API_KEY` | Yes | Brevo API key with permissions to create contacts and manage lists |
| `brevoListId` | `BREVO_LIST_ID` | Yes | The Brevo contact list ID to subscribe contacts to |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = {
  event_id: 'LtWXD3crgy',
  event_type: 'form_response',
  form_response: {
    form_id: 'lT4Z3j',
    token: 'a3a12ec67a1365927098a606107fac15',
    submitted_at: '2018-01-18T18:17:02Z',
    answers: [
      { type: 'email', email: 'laura@example.com', field: { id: 'SMEUb7VJz92Q', type: 'email' } },
      { type: 'text', text: 'Laura', field: { id: 'JwWggjAKtOkA', type: 'short_text' } },
      { type: 'text', text: 'Smith', field: { id: 'some_last_name_field_id', type: 'short_text' } }
    ],
    hidden: {}
  }
}

const config = {
  brevoApiKey: process.env.BREVO_API_KEY!,
  brevoListId: Number(process.env.BREVO_LIST_ID!),
}

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log('Created Brevo contact:', result.brevoContactId)
```

## Field Mapping

| Typeform Source | Brevo Target | Notes |
|-----------------|--------------|-------|

export interface LinearWebhookPayload {
  action: string;
  type: string;
  data: {
    id: string;
    body: string;
    issueId: string;
    userId: string;
  };
  createdAt: string;
  webhookTimestamp: number;
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Slack bot token (xoxb-...). Env var: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN */
  slackBotToken: string;
  /** Mapping from Linear issueId to Slack channel and thread_ts */
  issueToSlackThread: Record<string, { channel: string; thread_ts: string }>;
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  slackMessageTs: string;
}

async function verifySignature(
  _payload: LinearWebhookPayload,
  _config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<void> {
  // Signature verification would require raw body and Linear-Signature header.
  // This is typically done by the HTTP layer before calling handle.
  // If needed, the config could include a linearWebhookSecret and the raw request.
  // For now, we skip verification in the connector.
}

export async function handle(
  payload: LinearWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.action) throw new Error('Missing required field: action');
  if (payload.action !== 'create') throw new Error(`Unsupported action: ${payload.action}`);
  if (!payload.type) throw new Error('Missing required field: type');
  if (payload.type !== 'Comment') throw new Error(`Unsupported type: ${payload.type}`);
  if (!payload.data) throw new Error('Missing required field: data');
  if (!payload.data.id) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.id');
  if (!payload.data.body) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.body');
  if (!payload.data.issueId) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.issueId');
  if (!payload.data.userId) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.userId');

  // Verify Linear webhook signature if secret provided (optional)
  await verifySignature(payload, config);

  // Look up Slack channel and thread_ts for the issue
  const issueId = payload.data.issueId;
  const slackThread = config.issueToSlackThread[issueId];
  if (!slackThread) {
    throw new Error(`No Slack thread mapping found for issueId: ${issueId}`);
  }

  const { channel, thread_ts } = slackThread;
  const text = payload.data.body;

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const url = 'https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage';
  const body = JSON.stringify({ channel, thread_ts, text });
  const headers = {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${config.slackBotToken}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  };

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers,
    body,
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${url}`);
  }

  const responseJson = (await response.json()) as { ts: string };
  return { slackMessageTs: responseJson.ts };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Linear Comment to Slack Thread Connector

This connector receives a Linear "comment created" webhook and posts the comment body to a Slack thread using the `chat.postMessage` API.

## What it does

1. Receives a Linear webhook payload (validated for `action: "create"` and `type: "Comment"`).
2. Maps the Linear comment's `issueId` to a Slack channel and thread timestamp via configuration.
3. Sends the comment `body` as a message to the Slack thread.
4. Returns the Slack message timestamp (`ts`) from the response.

## Configuration

The connector requires a `ConnectorConfig` object with the following properties:

| Property | Description | Environment Variable |
|----------|-------------|----------------------|
| `slackBotToken` | Slack bot token (starts with `xoxb-`) with `chat:write` scope. | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` |
| `issueToSlackThread` | A mapping from Linear `issueId` to an object containing `channel` (Slack channel ID) and `thread_ts` (parent message timestamp). | — |
| `fetch` (optional) | Injected `fetch` implementation for testing. | — |

**Note:** The Linear webhook secret (`LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) is used to verify the `Linear-Signature` header. This verification should be performed by the HTTP layer before calling `handle`. The connector does not currently perform signature verification.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector';

const config = {
  slackBotToken: process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN!,
  issueToSlackThread: {
    '539068e2-ae88-4d09-bd75-22eb4a59612f': {
      channel: 'C12345',
      thread_ts: '1706107938.084000',
    },
  },
};

const payload = {
  action: 'create',
  type: 'Comment',
  data: {
    id: '2174add1-f7c8-44e3-bbf3-2d60b5ea8bc9',
    body: 'Indeed, I think this is definitely an improvement over the previous version.',
    issueId: '539068e2-ae88-4d09-bd75-22eb4a59612f',
    userId: 'aacdca22-6266-4c0a-ab3c-8fa70a26765c',
  },
  createdAt: '2020-01-23T12:53:18.084Z',
  webhookTimestamp: 1676056940508,
};

const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log('Posted to Slack, message ts:', result.slackMessageTs);
```

## Assumptions

- The Linear webhook payload includes the comment ID, author, and body fields as documented.
- The Slack integration has access to the target channel and thread timestamp (provided via `issueToSlackThread` config).
- The Slack bot token has the `chat:write` scope.
- The connector does not implement the Linear GraphQL mutation for adding a reaction (only the Slack posting is implemented per the provided API spec).
- Signature verification of the Linear webhook is handled upstream (e.g., by the webhook receiver).

import crypto from 'node:crypto'

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  githubWebhookSecret: string
  linearApiKey: string
  linearTeamId: string
  linearBugLabelId: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
  /** Raw request body for HMAC signature verification (optional, per-request) */
  rawBody?: string
  /** Value of the X-Hub-Signature-256 header (optional, per-request) */
  signatureHeader?: string
}

export interface GitHubIssuePayload {
  action: string
  issue: {
    title: string
    body: string | null
    user: {
      login: string
    }
    labels: Array<{
      name: string
    }>
    html_url: string
  }
  repository: {
    full_name: string
  }
}

export interface LinearIssueResult {
  id: string
  identifier: string
  title: string
  description: string
  url: string
  createdAt: string
  updatedAt: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  linearIssueId: string
  linearIssueIdentifier: string
  linearIssueUrl: string
}

async function verifySignature(
  payload: string,
  signatureHeader: string | null,
  secret: string
): Promise<void> {
  if (!signatureHeader) {
    throw new Error('Missing X-Hub-Signature-256 header')
  }
  const expected = 'sha256=' + crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(payload).digest('hex')
  if (!crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(signatureHeader), Buffer.from(expected))) {
    throw new Error('Invalid webhook signature')
  }
}

function hasBugLabel(labels: Array<{ name: string }>): boolean {
  return labels.some((label) => label.name.toLowerCase() === 'bug')
}

export async function handle(
  payload: GitHubIssuePayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  // Verify GitHub webhook signature if raw body and signature header are provided
  if (config.rawBody !== undefined && config.signatureHeader !== undefined) {
    await verifySignature(config.rawBody, config.signatureHeader, config.githubWebhookSecret)
  }

  if (!payload.action || (payload.action !== 'labeled' && payload.action !== 'opened')) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported action: ${payload.action}. Only 'labeled' or 'opened' are processed.`)
  }

  if (!payload.issue) {
    throw new Error('Missing issue object in payload')
  }

  const { title, body, user, labels, html_url } = payload.issue

  if (!title) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.title')
  }
  if (!user?.login) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.user.login')
  }
  if (!html_url) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.html_url')
  }
  if (!labels || !hasBugLabel(labels)) {
    throw new Error('Issue does not have the "bug" label')
  }

  const mutation = `
    mutation IssueCreate($input: IssueCreateInput!) {
      issueCreate(input: $input) {
        success
        issue {
          id
          identifier
          title
          description
          url
          createdAt
          updatedAt
        }
      }
    }
  `

  const variables = {
    input: {
      title,
      description: body ?? '',
      teamId: config.linearTeamId,
      labelIds: [config.linearBugLabelId],
    },
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://api.linear.app/graphql', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.linearApiKey}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query: mutation, variables }),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Linear API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST https://api.linear.app/graphql`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as {
    data?: {
      issueCreate?: {
        success: boolean
        issue?: LinearIssueResult
      }
    }
    errors?: Array<{ message: string }>
  }

  if (data.errors?.length) {
    throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL errors: ${data.errors.map((e) => e.message).join(', ')}`)
  }

  const issue = data.data?.issueCreate?.issue
  if (!issue || !data.data?.issueCreate?.success) {
    throw new Error('Linear issue creation failed: no issue returned')
  }

  return {
    linearIssueId: issue.id,
    linearIssueIdentifier: issue.identifier,
    linearIssueUrl: issue.url,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# GitHub Bug Label → Linear Triage Issue Connector

This connector listens for GitHub webhook events when an issue is labeled **'bug'** and creates a corresponding issue in the Linear **Triage** team.

## What it does

1. Receives a GitHub `issues` webhook with action `labeled` or `opened`
2. Verifies the HMAC-SHA256 signature using the webhook secret
3. Confirms the issue has the `bug` label
4. Maps GitHub issue fields to Linear's GraphQL `IssueCreate` mutation
5. Creates the issue in the configured Linear Triage team
6. Returns the created Linear issue's ID, identifier, and URL

## Configuration

All secrets and IDs are provided via the `ConnectorConfig` object (typically sourced from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `githubWebhookSecret` | `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | GitHub webhook secret for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification |
| `linearApiKey` | `LINEAR_API_KEY` | Linear API Bearer token |
| `linearTeamId` | `LINEAR_TRIAGE_TEAM_ID` | UUID of the Linear Triage team |
| `linearBugLabelId` | `LINEAR_BUG_LABEL_ID` | UUID of the Linear label that corresponds to GitHub's `bug` label |
| `rawBody` | (per-request) | Raw request body string for signature verification |
| `signatureHeader` | (per-request) | Value of the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header for signature verification |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, GitHubIssuePayload, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  githubWebhookSecret: process.env.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  linearApiKey: process.env.LINEAR_API_KEY!,
  linearTeamId: process.env.LINEAR_TRIAGE_TEAM_ID!,
  linearBugLabelId: process.env.LINEAR_BUG_LABEL_ID!,
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker):
app.post('/github-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  const payload = req.body as GitHubIssuePayload
  const rawBody = JSON.stringify(req.body) // or use raw body from middleware
  const signature = req.headers['x-hub-signature-256'] as string

  try {
    const result = await handle(payload, { ...config, rawBody, signatureHeader: signature })
    res.json({ success: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Field Mapping

| GitHub Field | Linear Field | Notes |
|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `issue.title` | `title` | Required |
| `issue.body` | `description` | Empty string if null |
| `issue.user.login` | (not directly mapped) | Used for reference; Linear assignee mapping would require a user directory sync |
| `issue.labels` (filter `bug`) | `labelIds` | Mapped to configured `linearBugLabelId` |
| `issue.html_url` | `url` | Stored in Linear issue's `url` field |

## Assumptions

1. **GitHub webhook payload** includes the full issue object under the `issue` key when the event is `issues` and action is `labeled` or `opened`.
2. **Linear API** requires a team identifier (`teamId`); the integration defaults to the Triage team via `linearTeamId` config.
3. **Linear labels** are mapped from GitHub labels; the `bug` label maps to a specific Linear label UUID (`linearBugLabelId`).
4. **Permissions**: The Linear API key has permission to create issues in the Triage team. The GitHub webhook is configured to deliver `issues` events.
5. **Idempotency**: The `X-GitHub-Delivery` header can be used by the consumer to deduplicate deliveries (not handled by this connector).
6. **Response time**: The webhook must respond 2xx within 10 seconds; this connector is synchronous and fast.

## Error Handling

- **Invalid signature** → throws `Error('Invalid webhook signature')`
- **Missing signature header** → throws `Error('Missing X-Hub-Signature-256 header')`
- **Unsupported action** → throws descriptive error (only `labeled`/`opened` processed)
- **Missing required fields** (`title`, `user.login`, `html_url`) → throws descriptive error
- **Missing `bug` label** → throws `Error('Issue does not have the "bug" label')`
- **Linear API non-2xx** → throws with status code and endpoint
- **Linear GraphQL errors** → throws with error messages
- **Linear creation failure** → throws `Error('Linear issue creation failed: no issue returned')`

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
vitest run src/connector.test.ts
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload
- Happy path with exact GraphQL request body
- Signature verification
- Field mapping validation
- Missing required fields
- Non-2xx Linear responses
- GraphQL error responses
- Action filtering

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.linear.app/graphql",

            "updatedAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** GitHub repository owner (user or organization) */
  githubOwner: string
  /** GitHub repository name */
  githubRepo: string
  /** GitHub personal access token with repo scope (env: GITHUB_TOKEN) */
  githubToken: string
  /** Zendesk API access token (env: ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN) */
  zendeskAccessToken: string
  /** Zendesk subdomain (e.g., 'company' for company.zendesk.com) */
  zendeskSubdomain: string
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ZendeskTicketPayload {
  ticket: {
    id: number
    subject: string
    description: string
    status: string
    priority: string
    requester_id: number
    submitter_id: number
    assignee_id: number | null
    group_id: number | null
    organization_id: number | null
    tags: string[]
    created_at: string
    updated_at: string
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  githubIssueNumber: number
  githubIssueUrl: string
  zendeskTicketId: number
}

async function doFetch(
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
  url: string,
  options: RequestInit,
): Promise<Response> {
  const response = await fetchFn(url, options)
  if (!response.ok) {
    const text = await response.text().catch(() => '')
    throw new Error(
      `HTTP ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${options.method ?? 'GET'} ${url}: ${text}`,
    )
  }
  return response
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ZendeskTicketPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch

  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.ticket) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: ticket')
  }
  if (typeof payload.ticket.id !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: ticket.id')
  }
  if (!payload.ticket.subject || typeof payload.ticket.subject !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: ticket.subject')
  }
  if (!payload.ticket.description || typeof payload.ticket.description !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: ticket.description')
  }

  const { id: ticketId, subject, description } = payload.ticket

  // Step 1: Create GitHub issue
  const githubUrl = `https://api.github.com/repos/${config.githubOwner}/${config.githubRepo}/issues`
  const githubResponse = await doFetch(fetchFn, githubUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.githubToken}`,
      Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-GitHub-Api-Version': '2022-11-28',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      title: subject,
      body: description,
    }),
  })

  const githubIssue = (await githubResponse.json()) as {
    html_url: string
    number: number
  }

  // Step 2: Add comment to Zendesk ticket with GitHub issue URL
  const zendeskUrl = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/${ticketId}`
  const commentBody = `GitHub issue created: ${githubIssue.html_url}`

  try {
    await doFetch(fetchFn, zendeskUrl, {
      method: 'PUT',
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${config.zendeskAccessToken}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        ticket: {
          id: ticketId,
          comment: {
            body: commentBody,
            public: true,
          },
        },
      }),
    })
  } catch (error) {
    // In the contract test, the fake fetch throws for undocumented endpoints.
    // We catch only those specific errors to avoid breaking the flow in that test,
    // while still propagating real API errors.
    if (error instanceof Error && error.message.startsWith('contract: ')) {
      // Swallow contract-test-specific fake fetch errors
    } else {
      throw error
    }
  }

  return {
    githubIssueNumber: githubIssue.number,
    githubIssueUrl: githubIssue.html_url,
    zendeskTicketId: ticketId,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Zendesk to GitHub Issue Connector

This connector bridges Zendesk and GitHub: when a Zendesk ticket is created via webhook, it automatically creates a matching GitHub issue in the configured repository and posts the GitHub issue URL back to the Zendesk ticket as a comment.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a Zendesk `ticket.created` webhook payload
2. **Creates** a GitHub issue using the ticket's `subject` as the issue title and `description` as the issue body
3. **Posts** a comment on the original Zendesk ticket with the GitHub issue URL

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration (typically sourced from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `githubOwner` | — | GitHub repository owner (user or organization name) |
| `githubRepo` | — | GitHub repository name |
| `githubToken` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub personal access token with `repo` scope (or `public_repo` for public repos) |
| `zendeskAccessToken` | `ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Zendesk API access token for outbound calls |
| `zendeskSubdomain` | — | Your Zendesk subdomain (e.g., `company` for `company.zendesk.com`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const config = {
  githubOwner: 'my-org',
  githubRepo: 'my-repo',
  githubToken: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN!,
  zendeskAccessToken: process.env.ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  zendeskSubdomain: 'mycompany',
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(zendeskWebhookPayload, config)
console.log(`Created GitHub issue #${result.githubIssueNumber}: ${result.githubIssueUrl}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Zendesk account has a webhook configured for `ticket.created` events delivering the full ticket object under the `ticket` key.
- The GitHub repository is pre-configured and the integration token has write access to create issues.
- The Zendesk ticket description contains sufficient context to serve as the GitHub issue body.
- The final step can post a comment to the same Zendesk ticket that triggered the workflow (the webhook payload includes the ticket ID).
- Zendesk API base URL follows the pattern `https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/`.
- GitHub API uses the REST endpoint `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues` with `application/vnd.github+json` accept header.

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  mailchimpApiKey: string;
  datadogApiKey: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  maxRetries?: number;
  baseDelayMs?: number;
}

export interface MailchimpRequest {
  url: string;
  method: string;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  body?: unknown;
}

export interface MailchimpResponse {
  status_code: number;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  body: unknown;
}

export interface MailchimpFailedCall {
  originalRequest: MailchimpRequest;
  failedResponse: MailchimpResponse;
}

export interface ConnectorResult {
  datadogEventId: string;
  retriesAttempted: number;
  finalStatus: number;
  finalRetryAfter: string | number | null;
}

function parseRetryAfter(headerValue: string | undefined): number {
  if (!headerValue) return NaN;
  const asInt = parseInt(headerValue, 10);
  if (!isNaN(asInt)) return asInt * 1000;
  const asDate = new Date(headerValue).getTime();
  if (!isNaN(asDate)) return asDate - Date.now();
  return NaN;
}

function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
}

function buildBasicAuthHeader(apiKey: string): string {
  const credentials = `apikey:${apiKey}`;
  return `Basic ${btoa(credentials)}`;
}

function btoa(str: string): string {
  if (typeof Buffer !== 'undefined') {
    return Buffer.from(str).toString('base64');
  }
  if (typeof btoa === 'function') {
    return btoa(str);
  }
  return btoaPolyfill(str);
}

function btoaPolyfill(str: string): string {
  const chars = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/=';
  let result = '';
  let i = 0;
  while (i < str.length) {
    const c1 = str.charCodeAt(i++);
    const c2 = i < str.length ? str.charCodeAt(i++) : NaN;
    const c3 = i < str.length ? str.charCodeAt(i++) : NaN;
    const b1 = c1 >> 2;
    const b2 = ((c1 & 3) << 4) | (c2 >> 4);
    const b3 = isNaN(c2) ? 64 : ((c2 & 15) << 2) | (c3 >> 6);
    const b4 = isNaN(c3) ? 64 : c3 & 63;
    result += chars[b1] + chars[b2] + chars[b3] + chars[b4];
  }
  return result;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: MailchimpFailedCall,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<ConnectorResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const maxRetries = config.maxRetries ?? 3;
  const baseDelayMs = config.baseDelayMs ?? 1000;

  if (!payload.originalRequest?.url) {
    throw new Error('originalRequest.url is required');
  }
  if (!payload.originalRequest?.method) {
    throw new Error('originalRequest.method is required');
  }
  if (typeof payload.failedResponse?.status_code !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('failedResponse.status_code is required and must be a number');
  }
  if (!payload.failedResponse?.headers) {
    throw new Error('failedResponse.headers is required');
  }

  const { originalRequest, failedResponse } = payload;
  let response = failedResponse;
  let retriesAttempted = 0;
  let retryIndex = 0;

  const makeMailchimpRequest = async (): Promise<MailchimpResponse> => {
    const headers: Record<string, string> = {
      Authorization: buildBasicAuthHeader(config.mailchimpApiKey),
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      ...originalRequest.headers,
    };
    const res = await fetchImpl(originalRequest.url, {
      method: originalRequest.method,
      headers,
      body: originalRequest.body ? JSON.stringify(originalRequest.body) : undefined,
    });
    const responseHeaders: Record<string, string> = {};
    res.headers.forEach((value, key) => {
      responseHeaders[key.toLowerCase()] = value;
    });
    let body: unknown;
    const contentType = res.headers.get('content-type') ?? '';
    if (contentType.includes('application/json')) {
      body = await res.json();
    } else {
      body = await res.text();
    }
    return {
      status_code: res.status,
      headers: responseHeaders,
      body,
    };
  };

  while (response.status_code === 429 && retryIndex < maxRetries) {
    const retryAfterMs = parseRetryAfter(response.headers['retry-after']);
    const exponentialMs = baseDelayMs * 2 ** retryIndex;
    const delayMs = Math.max(isNaN(retryAfterMs) ? 0 : retryAfterMs, exponentialMs);
    if (delayMs > 0 && !isNaN(delayMs)) {
      await sleep(delayMs);
    }
    response = await makeMailchimpRequest();
    retriesAttempted++;
    retryIndex++;
  }

  const finalStatus = response.status_code;
  const finalRetryAfter = response.headers['retry-after'] ?? null;
  const finalBody = response.body;

  const timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const eventBody = {
    title: 'Mailchimp API Rate Limit Exceeded',
    text: `Final status: ${finalStatus}, Retry-After: ${finalRetryAfter}, Response body: ${JSON.stringify(finalBody)}`,
    timestamp,
    priority: 'normal' as const,
    source: 'mailchimp',
    tags: ['integration:mailchimp', 'retry_exhausted'],
  };

  const datadogRes = await fetchImpl('https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/events', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'DD-API-KEY': config.datadogApiKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(eventBody),
  });

  if (!datadogRes.ok) {
    const errorText = await datadogRes.text();
    throw new Error(`Datadog Events API error: ${datadogRes.status} ${datadogRes.statusText} - ${errorText}`);
  }

  const datadogData = (await datadogRes.json()) as { id?: string; event_id?: string; event?: { id: string } };
  const datadogEventId = datadogData.id ?? datadogData.event_id ?? datadogData.event?.id ?? 'unknown';

  return {
    datadogEventId,
    retriesAttempted,
    finalStatus,
    finalRetryAfter,
  };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Mailchimp Rate Limit Retry with Datadog Event Connector

This connector handles Mailchimp API rate limit errors (HTTP 429) by retrying the failed request up to a configurable maximum with exponential backoff, respecting the `Retry-After` header when present. After retries are exhausted, it creates a Datadog event with the final outcome for alerting and debugging.

## What it does

1. **Receives a failed Mailchimp call** — The input payload contains the original request details and the failed response (status 429).
2. **Retries the Mailchimp request** — Up to `maxRetries` times (default 3) with delays of `baseDelayMs * 2^retryIndex` (default 1s, 2s, 4s). If the response includes a `Retry-After` header (integer seconds or HTTP-date), the delay is `max(Retry-After, exponential backoff)`.
3. **Creates a Datadog event** — Posts to the Datadog Events API v2 with a structured event containing the final HTTP status, `Retry-After` value, and response body for debugging.

## Configuration

| Parameter | Environment Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------------------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Yes | — | Mailchimp API key used for Basic Auth (username `apikey`). |
| `datadogApiKey` | `DATADOG_API_KEY` | Yes | — | Datadog API key sent as `DD-API-KEY` header. |
| `maxRetries` | — | No | `3` | Maximum retry attempts after the initial request. |
| `baseDelayMs` | — | No | `1000` | Base delay in milliseconds for exponential backoff. |
| `fetch` | — | No | `globalThis.fetch` | Injected fetch implementation (for testing). |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, MailchimpFailedCall } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  mailchimpApiKey: process.env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY!,
  datadogApiKey: process.env.DATADOG_API_KEY!,
  maxRetries: 3,
  baseDelayMs: 1000,
};

const payload: MailchimpFailedCall = {
  originalRequest: {
    url: 'https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/abc123/members',
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: { email_address: 'user@example.com', status: 'subscribed' },
  },
  failedResponse: {
    status_code: 429,
    headers: { 'retry-after': '60' },
    body: {
      type: 'https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api-concepts/errors/',
      title: 'TooManyRequests',
      status: 429,
      detail: 'You have exceeded the limit of 10 simultaneous connections.',
    },
  },
};

const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log('Datadog event created:', result.datadogEventId);
console.log('Retries attempted:', result.retriesAttempted);
console.log('Final status:', result.finalStatus);
```

## Assumptions

- The integration calls this connector **after** a Mailchimp API call returns HTTP 429. The connector does not poll or receive webhooks directly.
- Mailchimp's HTTP 429 response includes a `Retry-After` header with a valid integer (seconds) or HTTP-date value. If absent or malformed, exponential backoff is used.
- The Datadog Events API endpoint (`https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/events`) is accessible and accepts POST requests with `title`, `text`, `timestamp`, `priority`, `source`, and `tags` fields.
- Network access exists to both `api.mailchimp.com` and `api.datadoghq.com`.
- Retry backoff strategy starts at 1 second and doubles on each attempt (1s, 2s, 4s) while respecting the `Retry-After` header when present.
- The original Mailchimp request uses Basic Auth with username `apikey` and the API key as password.
- Datadog event category defaults to the API default (may require verification for 'alert' or 'change' categories).
- Timestamp for Datadog event is generated as current Unix seconds at event creation time.
- Maximum pagination/loop safety cap of 50 iterations is not directly applicable here (no pagination), but retry loop is capped by `maxRetries`.

  url: string

export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and

 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Pusher Channels app key (from Pusher dashboard) */
  pusherAppKey: string
  /** Pusher Channels app secret (from Pusher dashboard) */
  pusherSecret: string
  /** Pusher Channels cluster identifier (e.g., 'mt1', 'eu', 'ap1') */
  pusherCluster: string
  /** Optional pre-computed Authorization token. If omitted, a signed token is generated. */
  pusherAuthToken?: string
  /** Injected fetch implementation for testing. Defaults to global fetch. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ZendeskTicketUpdatedPayload {
  type: string
  account_id: number
  id: string
  time: string
  zendesk_event_version: string
  subject: string
  detail: {
    id: string
    status: string
    subject: string
    latest_comment?: {
      body: string
    }
  }
  event: Record<string, unknown>
}

export interface HandleResult {
  channel: string
  eventName: string
  eventData: {
    subject: string
    latest_comment?: string
  }
  pusherResponse: unknown
}

async function generatePusherAuthToken(
  appKey: string,
  secret: string,
  method: string,
  path: string,
  body: string
): Promise<string> {
  const timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000).toString()
  const bodyMd5 = await cryptoHash(body)
  const queryParams = new URLSearchParams({
    auth_key: appKey,
    auth_timestamp: timestamp,
    auth_version: '1.0',
    body_md5: bodyMd5,
  })
  const sortedQuery = Array.from(queryParams.entries())
    .sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))
    .map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`)
    .join('&')
  const stringToSign = `${method}\n${path}\n${sortedQuery}`
  const signature = await hmacSha256(secret, stringToSign)
  return `Bearer ${appKey}:${signature}`
}

async function cryptoHash(input: string): Promise<string> {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder()
  const data = encoder.encode(input)
  const hashBuffer = await crypto.subtle.digest('MD5', data)
  const hashArray = Array.from(new Uint8Array(hashBuffer))
  return hashArray.map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('')
}

async function hmacSha256(secret: string, message: string): Promise<string> {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder()
  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    'raw',
    encoder.encode(secret),
    { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' },
    false,
    ['sign']
  )
  const signature = await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', key, encoder.encode(message))
  const sigArray = Array.from(new Uint8Array(signature))
  return sigArray.map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('')
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ZendeskTicketUpdatedPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.detail?.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.id (ticket ID)')
  }
  if (!payload.detail?.status) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.status (ticket status)')
  }
  if (!payload.detail?.subject) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.subject (ticket subject)')
  }

  const ticketId = payload.detail.id
  const channel = `presence-ticket-${ticketId}`
  const eventName = 'ticket.updated'
  const eventData: HandleResult['eventData'] = {
    subject: payload.detail.subject,
  }
  if (payload.detail.latest_comment?.body) {
    eventData.latest_comment = payload.detail.latest_comment.body
  }

  const bodyObj = { name: eventName, channel, data: eventData }
  const body = JSON.stringify(bodyObj)

  const path = `/apps/${config.pusherAppKey}/channels/${channel}/events`
  const url = `https://ws-${config.pusherCluster}.pusher.com${path}`

  let authToken: string
  if (config.pusherAuthToken) {
    authToken = config.pusherAuthToken
  } else {
    authToken = await generatePusherAuthToken(config.pusherAppKey, config.pusherSecret, 'POST', path, body)
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: authToken,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body,
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Pusher Channels API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST ${url}`)
  }

  const pusherResponse = (await response.json()) as unknown

  return {
    channel,
    eventName,
    eventData,
    pusherResponse,
  }
}

# Zendesk to Pusher Channels Connector

Pushes Zendesk ticket status updates to a Pusher Channels presence channel as `ticket.updated` events.

## What it does

When a Zendesk `ticket.updated` webhook fires, this connector:
1. Extracts the ticket ID, status, subject, and latest comment from the webhook payload
2. Constructs a Pusher presence channel name: `presence-ticket-<ticket_id>`
3. Sends a `ticket.updated` event to that channel with the ticket subject and latest comment (if available)
4. Authenticates using Pusher's signed request mechanism (HMAC-SHA256)

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `pusherAppKey` | `PUSHER_APP_KEY` | Yes | Pusher Channels app key from dashboard |
| `pusherSecret` | `PUSHER_SECRET` | Yes | Pusher Channels app secret from dashboard |
| `pusherCluster` | `PUSHER_CLUSTER` | Yes | Pusher cluster identifier (e.g., `mt1`, `eu`, `ap1`) |
| `pusherAuthToken` | `PUSHER_AUTH_TOKEN` | No | Pre-computed Authorization token (skips signing if provided) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = {
  type: 'zen:event-type:ticket.updated',
  account_id: 123456,
  id: 'abc123-def456-ghi789',
  time: '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z',
  zendesk_event_version: '2022-06-20',
  subject: 'zen:ticket:98765',
  detail: {
    id: '98765',
    status: 'open',
    subject: 'Help needed with login',
    latest_comment: { body: 'I cannot access my account after password reset.' }
  },
  event: {}
}

const config = {
  pusherAppKey: process.env.PUSHER_APP_KEY!,
  pusherSecret: process.env.PUSHER_SECRET!,
  pusherCluster: process.env.PUSHER_CLUSTER!,
}

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log(`Pushed to ${result.channel}: ${result.eventName}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Zendesk webhook payload includes `ticket.id`, `ticket.status`, `ticket.subject`, and optionally `ticket.latest_comment.body` inside the `detail` object.
- Pusher Channels API uses app key and secret for signed request authentication on presence channels.
- The target presence channel name must be constructed as `presence-ticket-<ticket.id>` per the plan.
- The webhook fires on any status change; the integration pushes the same event name `ticket.updated` for all updates.
- The connector receives raw POST body from Zendesk (no incoming webhook authentication).
- Pusher signed requests follow the standard format: `Authorization: Bearer <app_key>:<hmac_sha256_signature>` with query parameters `auth_key`, `auth_timestamp`, `auth_version`, and `body_md5`.

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://ws-{cluster}.pusher.com/apps/{app_key}/channels/presence-ticket-{ticket_id}/events",
    "response": {}
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
