export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Pipedrive API token from environment variable PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN */
  pipedriveApiToken: string
  /** Optional field ID overrides for Typeform form fields */
  fieldIds?: {
    firstName?: string
    lastName?: string
    email?: string
    company?: string
  }
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
  /** Maximum retry attempts for 429 responses (default: 3) */
  maxRetries?: number
  /** Base delay in ms for exponential backoff (default: 1000) */
  baseRetryDelayMs?: number
}

export interface TypeformWebhookPayload {
  event_id: string
  event_type: string
  form_response: {
    form_id: string
    token: string
    submitted_at: string
    answers: Array<{
      type: string
      text?: string
      email?: string
      field: {
        id: string
        type: string
      }
    }>
    hidden: Record<string, unknown>
  }
}

export interface ConnectorResult {
  organizationId: number
  personId: number
  dealId: number
}

interface PipedriveOrganizationResponse {
  success: boolean
  data: {
    id: number
    name: string
    add_time: string
    update_time: string
  }
}

interface PipedrivePersonResponse {
  success: boolean
  data: {
    id: number
    first_name: string
    last_name: string
    email: Array<{ value: string; primary: boolean; label: string }>
    org_id: number
    add_time: string
    update_time: string
  }
}

interface PipedriveDealResponse {
  success: boolean
  data: {
    id: number
    title: string
    person_id: number
    value: number
    currency: string
    status: string
    add_time: string
    update_time: string
  }
}

function extractFieldValue(
  answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers'],
  fieldId: string
): string | undefined {
  const answer = answers.find((a) => a.field.id === fieldId)
  if (!answer) return undefined
  return answer.text ?? answer.email
}

function parseRetryAfter(header: string | null): number | null {
  if (!header) return null
  const seconds = Number(header)
  if (!Number.isNaN(seconds)) return seconds * 1000
  const date = new Date(header).getTime()
  if (!Number.isNaN(date)) return date - Date.now()
  return null
}

async function fetchWithRetry(
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
  url: string,
  init: RequestInit,
  maxRetries: number,
  baseDelayMs: number
): Promise<Response> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) {
    const response = await fetchFn(url, init)
    if (response.status === 429) {
      if (attempt === maxRetries) {
        throw new Error('Max retries exceeded')
      }
      const retryAfter = parseRetryAfter(response.headers.get('retry-after'))
      const delay = retryAfter ?? baseDelayMs * 2 ** attempt
      if (delay > 0 && !Number.isNaN(delay)) {
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay))
      }
      continue
    }
    return response
  }
  throw new Error('Max retries exceeded')
}

function throwOnError(response: Response, endpoint: string): void {
  if (response.status >= 200 && response.status < 300) return
  throw new Error(`Pipedrive API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} on ${endpoint}`)
}

export async function handle(
  payload: TypeformWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<ConnectorResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const maxRetries = config.maxRetries ?? 3
  const baseDelayMs = config.baseRetryDelayMs ?? 1000

  const fieldIds = {
    firstName: config.fieldIds?.firstName ?? 'JwWggjAKtOkA',
    lastName: config.fieldIds?.lastName ?? 'LAST_NAME_FIELD_ID',
    email: config.fieldIds?.email ?? 'SMEUb7VJz92Q',
    company: config.fieldIds?.company ?? 'COMPANY_FIELD_ID',
  }

  const { form_response } = payload
  const { answers, hidden } = form_response

  const firstName = extractFieldValue(answers, fieldIds.firstName)
  const lastName = extractFieldValue(answers, fieldIds.lastName)
  const email = extractFieldValue(answers, fieldIds.email)
  const company = extractFieldValue(answers, fieldIds.company)

  if (!firstName) throw new Error('Missing required field: first_name')
  if (!lastName) throw new Error('Missing required field: last_name')
  if (!email) throw new Error('Missing required field: email')
  if (!company) throw new Error('Missing required field: company')

  const authHeader = `Bearer ${config.pipedriveApiToken}`
  const commonHeaders = {
    Authorization: authHeader,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    Accept: 'application/json',
  }

  // 1. Create Organization
  const orgResponse = await fetchWithRetry(
    fetchFn,
    'https://api.pipedrive.com/v2/organizations',
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: commonHeaders,
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: company }),
    },
    maxRetries,
    baseDelayMs
  )
  throwOnError(orgResponse, 'POST https://api.pipedrive.com/v2/organizations')
  const orgData = (await orgResponse.json()) as PipedriveOrganizationResponse
  const organizationId = orgData.data.id

  // 2. Create Person
  const personResponse = await fetchWithRetry(
    fetchFn,
    'https://api.pipedrive.com/v2/persons',
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: commonHeaders,
      body: JSON.stringify({
        first_name: firstName,
        last_name: lastName,
        email: [{ value: email, primary: true, label: 'Work' }],
        org_id: organizationId,
      }),
    },
    maxRetries,
    baseDelayMs
  )
  throwOnError(personResponse, 'POST https://api.pipedrive.com/v2/persons')
  const personData = (await personResponse.json()) as PipedrivePersonResponse
  const personId = personData.data.id

  // 3. Create Deal
  const dealValue = typeof hidden.value === 'number' ? hidden.value : 0
  const dealResponse = await fetchWithRetry(
    fetchFn,
    'https://api.pipedrive.com/v2/deals',
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: commonHeaders,
      body: JSON.stringify({
        title: company,
        person_id: personId,
        value: dealValue,
        currency: 'USD',
      }),
    },
    maxRetries,
    baseDelayMs
  )
  throwOnError(dealResponse, 'POST https://api.pipedrive.com/v2/deals')
  const dealData = (await dealResponse.json()) as PipedriveDealResponse
  const dealId = dealData.data.id

  return { organizationId, personId, dealId }
}

# Typeform to Pipedrive Connector

Creates a Pipedrive organization, person, and deal when a Typeform contact form is submitted.

## What it does

1. Receives a Typeform webhook payload (form response submitted)
2. Extracts first name, last name, email, and company from the form answers
3. Creates a Pipedrive **Organization** with the company name
4. Creates a Pipedrive **Person** linked to that organization
5. Creates a Pipedrive **Deal** linked to the person, using the company name as title and optional monetary value from hidden fields

## Configuration

| Parameter | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `pipedriveApiToken` | `PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN` | Yes | Pipedrive API bearer token |
| `fieldIds.firstName` | — | No | Typeform field ID for first name (default: `JwWggjAKtOkA`) |
| `fieldIds.lastName` | — | No | Typeform field ID for last name (default: `LAST_NAME_FIELD_ID`) |
| `fieldIds.email` | — | No | Typeform field ID for email (default: `SMEUb7VJz92Q`) |
| `fieldIds.company` | — | No | Typeform field ID for company (default: `COMPANY_FIELD_ID`) |
| `maxRetries` | — | No | Max retry attempts on 429 (default: 3) |
| `baseRetryDelayMs` | — | No | Base delay for exponential backoff in ms (default: 1000) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, TypeformWebhookPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  pipedriveApiToken: process.env.PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN!,
  // Optional: override field IDs if your form uses different ones
  // fieldIds: { firstName: 'YOUR_FIELD_ID', ... },
}

const payload: TypeformWebhookPayload = await req.json() // Typeform webhook POST body

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log('Created:', result)
// { organizationId: 12345, personId: 67890, dealId: 54321 }
```

## Assumptions

- The Typeform contact form collects first name, last name, email, and company name fields with the documented field IDs (or custom IDs provided in config).
- The user has an active Pipedrive account with API permissions to create organizations, persons, and deals.
- A new organization record is created for each submission (no deduplication against existing organizations).
- Deal monetary value comes from `hidden.value` in the Typeform payload; defaults to 0 if absent or not a number.
- The created person is used as `person_id` when creating the deal to establish the link.
- Currency defaults to USD for deals.
- Retry logic handles 429 (Too Many Requests) with exponential backoff and `Retry-After` header support (seconds or HTTP date).
- All Pipedrive API calls use bearer token authentication via `Authorization` header.

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

  baseDelayMs: number,
): Promise<Response> {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (true) {
    const response = await fetchFn(url, init);
    if (response.status !== 429 || attempt >= maxRetries) {
      return response;
    }
    const retryAfter = response.headers.get('retry-after');
    let delayMs: number;
    if (retryAfter) {
      const parsed = parseRetryAfter(retryAfter);
      delayMs = Number.isNaN(parsed) ? baseDelayMs * 2 ** attempt : parsed;
    } else {
      delayMs = baseDelayMs * 2 ** attempt;
    }
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));
    attempt++;
  }
}

function parseRetryAfter(value: string): number {
  const seconds = parseInt(value, 10);
  if (!Number.isNaN(seconds)) {
    return seconds * 1000;
  }
  const dateMs = new Date(value).getTime();
  if (!Number.isNaN(dateMs)) {
    return Math.max(0, dateMs - Date.now());
  }
  return Number.NaN;
}

async function findCardInList(
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
  listId: string,
  apiKey: string,
  token: string,
  cardName: string,
  maxRetries: number,
  baseDelayMs: number,
): Promise<TrelloCard> {
  const url = buildUrlWithAuth(
    `https://api.trello.com/1/lists/${encodeURIComponent(listId)}/cards`,
    apiKey,
    token,
  );
  const response = await requestWithRetry(fetchFn, url, { method: 'GET' }, maxRetries, baseDelayMs);
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Trello GET /lists/${listId}/cards failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
  }
  const data = (await response.json()) as { cards: TrelloCard[] };
  const card = data.cards.find((c) => c.name === cardName);
  if (card) {
    return card;
  }
  if (data.cards.length > 0) {
    return data.cards[0];
  }
  throw new Error(`Card with name "${cardName}" not found in list ${listId} and no fallback card available`);
}

async function createChecklist(
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
  cardId: string,
  checklistName: string,
  apiKey: string,
  token: string,
  maxRetries: number,
  baseDelayMs: number,
): Promise<TrelloChecklist> {
  const url = buildUrlWithAuth('https://api.trello.com/1/checklists', apiKey, token);
  const body = JSON.stringify({ name: checklistName, idCard: cardId });
  const response = await requestWithRetry(
    fetchFn,
    url,
    { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body },
    maxRetries,
    baseDelayMs,
  );
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Trello POST /checklists failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
  }
  return (await response.json()) as TrelloChecklist;
}

async function addChecklistItem(
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
  checklistId: string,
  itemName: string,
  apiKey: string,
  token: string,
  maxRetries: number,
  baseDelayMs: number,
): Promise<TrelloCheckItem> {
  const url = buildUrlWithAuth(
    `https://api.trello.com/1/checklists/${encodeURIComponent(checklistId)}/checkItems`,
    apiKey,
    token,
  );
  const body = JSON.stringify({ name: itemName, checked: false });
  const response = await requestWithRetry(
    fetchFn,
    url,
    { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body },
    maxRetries,
    baseDelayMs,
  );
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Trello POST /checklists/${checklistId}/checkItems failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
  }
  return (await response.json()) as TrelloCheckItem;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: CalendarEventPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.event || payload.event !== 'calendar_event_created') {
    throw new Error('Payload event must be "calendar_event_created"');
  }
  if (!payload.attendees || payload.attendees.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('Payload must contain at least one attendee');
  }
  const firstAttendee = payload.attendees[0];
  const attendeeValue = firstAttendee.email ?? firstAttendee.display_name;
  if (!attendeeValue) {
    throw new Error('First attendee must have either email or display_name');
  }
  if (!config.trelloApiKey) {
    throw new Error('Config trelloApiKey is required');
  }
  if (!config.trelloToken) {
    throw new Error('Config trelloToken is required');
  }
  if (!config.trelloListId) {
    throw new Error('Config trelloListId is required');
  }

  const fetchFn = getFetch(config);
  const maxRetries = config.maxRetries ?? 3;
  const baseDelayMs = config.baseRetryDelayMs ?? 1000;
  const checklistName = config.checklistName ?? 'Attendee Info';

  const card = await findCardInList(
    fetchFn,
    config.trelloListId,
    config.trelloApiKey,
    config.trelloToken,
    payload.title,
    maxRetries,
    baseDelayMs,
  );

  const checklist = await createChecklist(
    fetchFn,
    card.id,
    checklistName,
    config.trelloApiKey,
    config.trelloToken,
    maxRetries,
    baseDelayMs,
  );

  const checkItem = await addChecklistItem(
    fetchFn,
    checklist.id,
    attendeeValue,
    config.trelloApiKey,
    config.trelloToken,
    maxRetries,
    baseDelayMs,
  );

  return {
    cardId: card.id,
    checklistId: checklist.id,
    checkItemId: checkItem.id,
    attendeeValue,
  };
}

# Google Calendar to Trello Checklist Connector

This connector processes a Google Calendar "event created" webhook (delivered via Unipile) and adds the first attendee as a checklist item on a Trello card in a configured list.

## What it does

1. Receives a `calendar_event_created` webhook payload from Unipile (Google Calendar integration).
2. Extracts the first attendee's email (preferred) or display name.
3. Finds a Trello card in the configured list whose name matches the Calendar event title. Falls back to the first card in the list if no exact name match is found.
4. Creates a checklist on that card (default name: "Attendee Info").
5. Adds a checklist item with the attendee's email/name.

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration (typically provided via environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `trelloApiKey` | `TRELLO_API_KEY` | Trello API key |
| `trelloToken` | `TRELLO_TOKEN` | Trello API token (required alongside key for all endpoints) |
| `trelloListId` | — | ID of the Trello list containing the target card |
| `checklistName` | — | Optional: name for the created checklist (default: "Attendee Info") |
| `maxRetries` | — | Optional: max retry attempts for 429 responses (default: 3) |
| `baseRetryDelayMs` | — | Optional: base delay in ms for exponential backoff (default: 1000) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, CalendarEventPayload } from './connector';

const payload: CalendarEventPayload = {
  event: 'calendar_event_created',
  webhook_name: 'CALENDAR_EVENTS_WEBHOOK',
  account_id: 'a4qFy0liRAGo-oZ2YFpirQ',
  id: '5m8lnvb64dt2uuaq99k4685eeq',
  calendar_id: 'user@example.com',
  created_at: '2026-01-16T16:14:01.000Z',
  updated_at: '2026-01-16T16:14:02.021Z',
  title: 'Meeting with customer',
  attendees: [{ email: 'customer@example.com', display_name: 'Customer Name' }],
  start: { date_time: '2026-01-20T14:30:00+01:00', time_zone: 'Europe/Paris' },
  end: { date_time: '2026-01-20T15:30:00+01:00', time_zone: 'Europe/Paris' },
};

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  trelloApiKey: process.env.TRELLO_API_KEY!,
  trelloToken: process.env.TRELLO_TOKEN!,
  trelloListId: 'target-list-id',
};

const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log(result); // { cardId, checklistId, checkItemId, attendeeValue }
```

## Assumptions

- The Trello list ID is known and configured in the integration settings.
- The Google Calendar event has at least one attendee with either an email or display name.
- A Trello card with a name matching the Calendar event title already exists in the target list. If not found, the first card in the list is used as a fallback.
- The Trello API requires creating a checklist first, then adding items to it (two API calls).
- All Trello endpoints require both `key` and `token` as query parameters.
- Retry logic handles 429 (Too Many Requests) with exponential backoff and `Retry-After` header support (seconds or HTTP date).

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN: string;
  NOTION_TOKEN: string;
  NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface IntercomConversationPart {
  id: string;
  part_type: string;
  author: {
    type: 'user' | 'admin';
    id: string;
  };
  body: string;
  created_at: number;
}

export interface ConnectorInput {
  conversation?: {
    id: string;
    participants?: Array<{
      id: string;
      type: string;
      email?: string;
      phone?: string;
    }>;
  };
  conversation_parts?: IntercomConversationPart[];
  pages?: {
    next?: string | null;
  };
}

export interface ConnectorResult {
  notionPageId: string;
  conversationId: string;
  partsCount: number;
}

const EMAIL_REGEX = /\b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b/gi;
const PHONE_REGEX = /\+?[0-9\s\-\(\)]{10,}/g;

function redactText(text: string): string {
  return text
    .replace(EMAIL_REGEX, '[REDACTED EMAIL]')
    .replace(PHONE_REGEX, '[REDACTED PHONE]');
}

function buildNotionRichTextBlock(content: string): object {
  const redacted = redactText(content);
  return {
    object: 'block',
    type: 'paragraph',
    paragraph: {
      rich_text: [
        {
          type: 'text',
          text: {
            content: redacted,
            link: null,
          },
          annotations: {
            bold: false,
            italic: false,
            strikethrough: false,
            underline: false,
            code: false,
            color: 'default',
          },
          plain_text: redacted,
          href: null,
        },
      ],
    },
  };
}

async function fetchAllConversationParts(
  conversationId: string,
  accessToken: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
): Promise<IntercomConversationPart[]> {
  const allParts: IntercomConversationPart[] = [];
  let nextUrl = `https://api.intercom.io/conversations/${conversationId}/parts`;

  while (nextUrl) {
    const response = await fetchFn(nextUrl, {
      method: 'GET',
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
        Accept: 'application/json',
      },
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Intercom API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${nextUrl}`);
    }

    const data = (await response.json()) as {
      conversation_parts: IntercomConversationPart[];
      pages: { next: string | null };
    };

    allParts.push(...data.conversation_parts);
    nextUrl = data.pages.next ?? '';
  }

  return allParts;
}

export async function handle(payload: ConnectorInput, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<ConnectorResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  let conversationId: string;
  let parts: IntercomConversationPart[];

  if (payload.conversation_parts && payload.conversation_parts.length > 0) {
    parts = payload.conversation_parts;
    const nextUrl = payload.pages?.next;
    if (nextUrl) {
      const match = nextUrl.match(/\/conversations\/([^/]+)\/parts/);
      conversationId = match?.[1] ?? 'unknown';
    } else {
      conversationId = 'unknown';
    }
  } else if (payload.conversation?.id) {
    conversationId = payload.conversation.id;
    parts = await fetchAllConversationParts(conversationId, config.INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN, fetchFn);
  } else {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: either conversation.id or conversation_parts must be provided');
  }

  if (parts.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('No conversation parts found to create transcript');
  }

  const children = parts.map((part) => {
    const authorLabel = part.author.type === 'user' ? 'User' : 'Support';
    const content = `${authorLabel} (${part.author.id}): ${part.body}`;
    return buildNotionRichTextBlock(content);
  });

  const notionPayload = {
    parent: {
      type: 'page_id',
      page_id: config.NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID,
    },
    properties: {
      title: {
        title: [
          {
            text: {
              content: `Intercom Conversation Transcript - ${conversationId}`,
            },
          },
        ],
      },
    },
    children,
  };

  const notionResponse = await fetchFn('https://api.notion.com/v1/pages', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.NOTION_TOKEN}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Notion-Version': '2022-06-28',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(notionPayload),
  });

  if (!notionResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Notion API error: ${notionResponse.status} ${notionResponse.statusText} for https://api.notion.com/v1/pages`);
  }

  const notionData = (await notionResponse.json()) as { id: string };

  return {
    notionPageId: notionData.id,
    conversationId,
    partsCount: parts.length,
  };
}

# Intercom to Notion Transcript Connector

This connector processes Intercom conversation closed webhooks, retrieves the full conversation transcript via paginated API calls, redacts personally identifiable information (emails and phone numbers), and creates a formatted Notion page with the cleaned transcript.

## What It Does

1. **Receives** an Intercom `conversation.admin.closed` webhook payload (or direct conversation parts for testing)
2. **Fetches** the complete conversation history using Intercom's paginated `/conversations/{id}/parts` endpoint
3. **Redacts** email addresses and phone numbers from all message bodies using regex patterns
4. **Creates** a Notion page with rich-text formatted transcript blocks, preserving author attribution

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables (passed via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Config Key | Environment Variable | Description |
|------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN` | `INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Bearer token for Intercom API authentication |
| `NOTION_TOKEN` | `NOTION_TOKEN` | Bearer token for Notion API authentication |
| `NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID` | `NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID` | Notion page ID to parent the created transcript page under |
| `fetch` | (injected) | Optional fetch implementation for testing |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN: process.env.INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  NOTION_TOKEN: process.env.NOTION_TOKEN!,
  NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID: process.env.NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID!,
};

// Webhook payload from Intercom
const webhookPayload = {
  conversation: {
    id: 'conv_987',
    participants: [
      { id: 'user_abc', type: 'user', email: 'user@example.com' },
      { id: 'admin_def', type: 'admin' }
    ]
  }
};

const result = await handle(webhookPayload, config);
console.log(`Created Notion page: ${result.notionPageId}`);
console.log(`Conversation: ${result.conversationId}, Parts: ${result.partsCount}`);
```

## Assumptions

- The Intercom webhook payload includes a `conversation.id` field to seed the paginated parts retrieval
- Intercom's `/conversations/{id}/parts` endpoint uses cursor-based pagination via `starting_after` parameter; pagination stops when `pages.next` is null
- Each conversation part includes a `body` field (plain text since v2.15) and `author` info needed to reconstruct the transcript
- The Notion API accepts a `children` array where each block is a rich-text paragraph element containing `annotations` for formatting and `plain_text` for content
- Redaction regex patterns:
  - Email: `\b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b` (case-insensitive)
  - Phone: `\+?[0-9\s\-\(\)]{10,}` (matches 10+ digits with common separators)
- Identified email and phone patterns are replaced with `[REDACTED EMAIL]` and `[REDACTED PHONE]` respectively
- The Notion parent page ID is a valid page ID (not database or workspace)
- Transcript lines are formatted as paragraphs with author attribution: `"User (user_id): message"` or `"Support (admin_id): message"`

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors when required fields (`conversation.id` or `conversation_parts`) are missing
- Throws with status code and endpoint on non-2xx responses from Intercom or Notion APIs
- Throws when no conversation parts are found for a given conversation ID

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
npm test
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload
- Happy path with direct conversation parts (no Intercom fetch)
- Full pagination fetch from Intercom API
- Missing required field validation
- Non-2xx error responses from both APIs
- Auth header verification
- Field mapping to Notion rich-text blocks
- PII redaction verification

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Brevo API key from environment variable BREVO_API_KEY */
  brevoApiKey: string;
  /** Typeform field ID that contains the respondent's email address */
  emailFieldId: string;
  /** Typeform field ID that contains the respondent's name */
  nameFieldId: string;
  /** Default Brevo list ID to subscribe contacts to */
  brevoListId: number;
  /** Optional mappings from Typeform custom field IDs to Brevo list IDs */
  customFieldMappings?: Array<{ fieldId: string; listId: number }>;
  /** Injected fetch for testing; defaults to global fetch */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface TypeformWebhookPayload {
  event_id: string;
  event_type: string;
  form_response: {
    form_id: string;
    token: string;
    submitted_at: string;
    answers: Array<{
      type: string;
      email?: string;
      text?: string;
      field: {
        id: string;
        type: string;
      };
    }>;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  contactId: number;
  subscribedListIds: number[];
}

function extractAnswerValue(
  answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers'],
  fieldId: string,
): string | undefined {
  const answer = answers.find((a) => a.field.id === fieldId);
  if (!answer) return undefined;
  return answer.email ?? answer.text;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: TypeformWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  // Validate required fields
  if (!config.brevoApiKey) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: brevoApiKey (BREVO_API_KEY)');
  }
  if (!config.emailFieldId) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: emailFieldId');
  }
  if (!config.nameFieldId) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: nameFieldId');
  }
  if (typeof config.brevoListId !== 'number' || Number.isNaN(config.brevoListId)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: brevoListId (must be a number)');
  }

  const { form_response } = payload;
  const { answers } = form_response;

  // Extract email
  const email = extractAnswerValue(answers, config.emailFieldId);
  if (!email) {
    throw new Error(`Email not found in answers for field ID: ${config.emailFieldId}`);
  }

  // Extract name
  const name = extractAnswerValue(answers, config.nameFieldId);
  if (!name) {
    throw new Error(`Name not found in answers for field ID: ${config.nameFieldId}`);
  }

  // Build listIds array starting with default list
  const listIds: number[] = [config.brevoListId];

  // Add custom field mappings
  if (config.customFieldMappings?.length) {
    for (const mapping of config.customFieldMappings) {
      const value = extractAnswerValue(answers, mapping.fieldId);
      if (value) {
        listIds.push(mapping.listId);
      }
    }
  }

  // Deduplicate listIds
  const uniqueListIds = [...new Set(listIds)];

  // Prepare Brevo request body
  const body = {
    email,
    attributes: {
      FULLNAME: name,
    },
    listIds: uniqueListIds,
    updateEnabled: true,
  };

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'api-key': config.brevoApiKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(
      `Brevo API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts - ${errorText}`,
    );
  }

  const result = (await response.json()) as { id: number };
  return {
    contactId: result.id,
    subscribedListIds: uniqueListIds,
  };
}

# Typeform to Brevo Connector

Creates a contact in Brevo and subscribes them to a mailing list when a Typeform form response is submitted.

## What it does

1. Receives a Typeform `form_response` webhook payload
2. Extracts the respondent's email and name from the `answers` array using configured field IDs
3. Optionally maps additional custom fields to Brevo list IDs
4. Calls Brevo's `POST /v3/contacts` endpoint to create/update the contact with:
   - Email address
   - Full name (as `attributes.FULLNAME`)
   - List subscriptions (`listIds` array)
   - `updateEnabled: true` to avoid conflicts on existing contacts

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `brevoApiKey` | `BREVO_API_KEY` | Yes | Brevo API key for authentication |
| `emailFieldId` | — | Yes | Typeform field ID containing the email answer |
| `nameFieldId` | — | Yes | Typeform field ID containing the name answer |
| `brevoListId` | — | Yes | Default Brevo list ID to subscribe contacts to |
| `customFieldMappings` | — | No | Array of `{ fieldId, listId }` to map Typeform custom fields to additional Brevo lists |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, TypeformWebhookPayload } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  brevoApiKey: process.env.BREVO_API_KEY!,
  emailFieldId: 'SMEUb7VJz92Q',    // From your Typeform form configuration
  nameFieldId: 'JwWggjAKtOkA',     // From your Typeform form configuration
  brevoListId: 123,                // From Brevo UI or GET /v3/lists
  customFieldMappings: [
    { fieldId: 'plan-field', listId: 456 },  // e.g., "Premium Plan" -> List 456
    { fieldId: 'tier-field', listId: 789 },  // e.g., "Enterprise" -> List 789
  ],
};

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(typeformPayload as TypeformWebhookPayload, config);
console.log(`Created contact ${result.contactId}, subscribed to lists: ${result.subscribedListIds}`);
```

## Assumptions

- The Typeform webhook payload follows the documented structure with `form_response.answers` array
- Email and name are extracted by matching `field.id` to configured `emailFieldId` and `nameFieldId`
- Custom fields are also present in the `answers` array and mapped via `customFieldMappings`
- The Brevo API accepts `attributes.FULLNAME` (uppercase) for the contact's full name
- `listIds` expects an array of numeric list IDs from Brevo
- Setting `updateEnabled: true` prevents 400 errors when the contact already exists
- No authentication is performed by Typeform on webhook delivery; securing the endpoint is the responsibility of the hosting infrastructure
- Field IDs vary per Typeform form and must be configured by the user

 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  intercomAccessToken: string
  notionApiKey: string
  notionBlockId: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface IntercomWebhookPayload {
  topic: string
  data: {
    item: {
      id: string
      state: string
    }
  }
}

export interface IntercomAuthor {
  type: string
  name: string
  email: string
  phone: string
}

export interface IntercomMessage {
  id: string
  author: IntercomAuthor
  created_at: number
  type: string
  content: string
}

export interface IntercomMessagesResponse {
  conversation_messages: IntercomMessage[]
  pages: {
    type: string
    next?: {
      starting_after: string
    }
  }
}

export interface NotionBlock {
  object: 'block'
  type: 'paragraph'
  paragraph: {
    rich_text: Array<{
      type: 'text'
      text: {
        content: string
        link: null
      }
      annotations: Record<string, unknown>
      plain_text: string
      href: null
    }>
    color: 'default'
  }
}

export interface NotionAppendResponse {
  object: 'list'
  results: Array<{
    object: 'block'
    id: string
    type: string
    paragraph: {
      rich_text: unknown[]
    }
  }>
}

export interface ConnectorResult {
  messageCount: number
  notionBlockIds: string[]
}

type FetchFn = typeof fetch

export async function handle(payload: IntercomWebhookPayload, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<ConnectorResult> {
  const { intercomAccessToken, notionApiKey, notionBlockId, fetch = globalThis.fetch } = config

  // Validate webhook payload
  if (!payload || payload.topic !== 'conversation.updated') {
    throw new Error('topic must be "conversation.updated"')
  }
  if (!payload.data?.item?.id) {
    throw new Error('missing conversation ID')
  }
  if (payload.data.item.state !== 'closed') {
    throw new Error('state must be "closed"')
  }

  const conversationId = payload.data.item.id

  // Fetch all messages with pagination
  const messages = await fetchAllMessages(intercomAccessToken, conversationId, fetch)

  // Redact and convert to Notion blocks
  const blocks = messages.map(messageToBlock)

  // Append to Notion
  const response = await appendBlocksToNotion(notionApiKey, notionBlockId, blocks, fetch)

  return {
    messageCount: messages.length,
    notionBlockIds: response.results.map((r: { id: string }) => r.id)
  }
}

async function fetchAllMessages(
  intercomAccessToken: string,
  conversationId: string,
  fetch: FetchFn
): Promise<IntercomMessage[]> {
  const allMessages: IntercomMessage[] = []
  let cursor: string | undefined
  let pageCount = 0
  const MAX_PAGES = 10

  do {
    if (pageCount >= MAX_PAGES) break
    pageCount++

    const url = cursor
      ? `https://api.intercom.io/conversations/${conversationId}/messages?starting_after=${encodeURIComponent(cursor)}`
      : `https://api.intercom.io/conversations/${conversationId}/messages`

    const response = await fetch(url, {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${intercomAccessToken}`,
        Accept: 'application/json'
      }
    })

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Intercom API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for GET ${url}`)
    }

    const data = (await response.json()) as IntercomMessagesResponse
    allMessages.push(...data.conversation_messages)
    cursor = data.pages?.next?.starting_after
  } while (cursor)

  return allMessages
}

const EMAIL_REGEX = /\b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b/gi
const PHONE_REGEX = /\+?[0-9]{1,3}[\s.-]?\(?[0-9]{3}\)?[\s.-]?[0-9]{3}[\s.-]?[0-9]{4}/g

function redactContent(content: string): string {
  return content
    .replace(EMAIL_REGEX, '[REDACTED EMAIL]')
    .replace(PHONE_REGEX, '[REDACTED PHONE]')
}

function messageToBlock(message: IntercomMessage): NotionBlock {
  const redactedContent = redactContent(message.content)

  return {
    object: 'block',
    type: 'paragraph',
    paragraph: {
      rich_text: [
        {
          type: 'text',
          text: {
            content: redactedContent,
            link: null
          },
          annotations: {},
          plain_text: redactedContent,
          href: null
        }
      ],
      color: 'default'
    }
  }
}

async function appendBlocksToNotion(
  notionApiKey: string,
  notionBlockId: string,
  blocks: NotionBlock[],
  fetch: FetchFn
): Promise<NotionAppendResponse> {
  const url = `https://api.notion.com/v1/blocks/${notionBlockId}/children`
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${notionApiKey}`,
      'Notion-Version': '2022-06-28',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ children: blocks })
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    const text = await response.text()
    throw new Error(`Notion API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for PATCH ${url}: ${text}`)
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<NotionAppendResponse>
}

# Intercom to Notion Transcript Connector

This connector processes Intercom `conversation.updated` webhooks (when a conversation is closed), fetches the full message transcript via the Intercom API with pagination, redacts email addresses and phone numbers from message content, and appends the cleaned transcript as rich-text blocks to a Notion page.

## What It Does

1. **Receives** an Intercom webhook payload with `topic: "conversation.updated"` and `data.item.state: "closed"`
2. **Fetches** all messages for the conversation using cursor-based pagination (`GET /conversations/{id}/messages`)
3. **Redacts** sensitive data from each message's `content` field:
   - Email addresses → `[REDACTED EMAIL]`
   - Phone numbers → `[REDACTED PHONE]`
4. **Builds** Notion rich-text paragraph blocks with the cleaned content
5. **Appends** blocks to the configured Notion page (`PATCH /blocks/{block_id}/children`)

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `intercomAccessToken` | `INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Bearer token for Intercom API authentication |
| `notionApiKey` | `NOTION_API_KEY` | Bearer token for Notion API authentication |
| `notionBlockId` | `NOTION_BLOCK_ID` | The Notion page/block ID to append transcript blocks to |
| `fetch` | (injected) | Optional fetch implementation for testing |

All secrets must be provided via the config object at runtime. Never hard-code credentials.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  intercomAccessToken: process.env.INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  notionApiKey: process.env.NOTION_API_KEY!,
  notionBlockId: process.env.NOTION_BLOCK_ID!,
  // fetch is optional; defaults to global fetch
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(webhookPayload, config)
console.log(`Appended ${result.messageCount} messages as blocks:`, result.notionBlockIds)
```

## Assumptions

- The Intercom webhook fires with `state=closed` and includes the conversation ID in `data.item.id`
- The Notion page already exists and its `block_id` (page ID) is known and stored in configuration
- Each message's `content` field contains the raw transcript text requiring redaction
- Author `email` and `phone` fields are present on author objects within the messages array
- Redaction regex patterns:
  - Email: `\b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b` (case-insensitive)
  - Phone: `\+?[0-9]\s*\(?[0-9]{3}\)?[\s.-]?[0-9]{3}[\s.-]?[0-9]{4}`
- Notion rich-text blocks accept an array of objects with `type: "text"`, `annotations`, and `plain_text`
- Intercom messages pagination uses cursor-based approach with `starting_after` parameter; the connector loops until no `next` cursor is returned
- The connector uses `Notion-Version: 2022-06-28` header for Notion API calls

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing/invalid webhook payload fields
- Throws on non-2xx responses from Intercom or Notion APIs, including status code and endpoint in the message
- All network calls use the injected `fetch` for testability

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  slackBotToken: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface TwilioWebhookPayload {
  Body: string
  From: string
  To: string
}

export interface SlackMessageResult {
  ok: boolean
  channel: string
  ts: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  channel: string
  slackResponse: SlackMessageResult
}

const SALES_KEYWORDS = /pricing|quote|demo/i

function parseFormBody(body: string): Record<string, string> {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(body)
  const result: Record<string, string> = {}
  for (const [key, value] of params.entries()) {
    result[key] = value
  }
  return result
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): TwilioWebhookPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: expected an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (typeof p.Body !== 'string' || p.Body.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: Body')
  }
  if (typeof p.From !== 'string' || p.From.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: From')
  }
  return {
    Body: p.Body,
    From: p.From,
    To: typeof p.To === 'string' ? p.To : '',
  }
}

function determineChannel(body: string): string {
  return SALES_KEYWORDS.test(body) ? '#sales' : '#support'
}

async function sendSlackMessage(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  channel: string,
  text: string,
): Promise<SlackMessageResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const url = 'https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage'
  const body = JSON.stringify({ channel, text })
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.slackBotToken}`,
    },
    body,
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  return (await response.json()) as SlackMessageResult
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!config.slackBotToken) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: slackBotToken')
  }
  const validated = validatePayload(payload)
  const channel = determineChannel(validated.Body)
  const slackResponse = await sendSlackMessage(config, channel, validated.Body)
  return { channel, slackResponse }
}

# Twilio SMS to Slack Connector

Routes incoming Twilio SMS webhooks to Slack channels based on message content.

## What it does

When a Twilio incoming SMS webhook arrives, this connector:
1. Parses the form-encoded payload (Body, From, To)
2. Checks if the message body matches `/pricing|quote|demo/i` (case-insensitive)
3. Routes to `#sales` if matched, otherwise to `#support`
4. Sends the message to the determined Slack channel via `chat.postMessage`

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `slackBotToken` | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | Yes | Slack bot token (xoxb-...) for posting messages |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Workers)
app.post('/twilio-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    // Twilio sends application/x-www-form-urlencoded
    const formBody = req.body // already parsed by body-parser or similar
    const result = await handle(formBody, {
      slackBotToken: process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN,
    })
    res.json({ success: true, channel: result.channel })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err)
    res.status(500).json({ error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The Twilio webhook payload includes `Body`, `From`, and `To` fields as documented.
- Slack bot token is configured with permissions to post to both `#sales` and `#support` channels.
- The regex pattern `/pricing|quote|demo/i` is evaluated case-insensitively on the message body.
- Only one Slack message send action is performed per webhook invocation based on the routing decision.
- Signature validation for Twilio webhooks is recommended but not implemented in this connector.
- The connector expects the incoming request body to already be parsed from `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` format.

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** OpenAI API key for authentication */
  OPENAI_API_KEY: string;
  /** GitHub token for posting comments (requires pull_requests: write permission) */
  GITHUB_TOKEN: string;
  /** Injected fetch implementation for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface GitHubPullRequestOpenedPayload {
  action: 'opened';
  pull_request: {
    title: string;
    body: string | null;
    number: number;
  };
  repository: {
    owner: {
      login: string;
    };
    name: string;
  };
}

export interface OpenAIAnalysisResponse {
  summary: string;
  risks: string[];
  suggestedReviewers: string[];
}

export interface GitHubCommentResponse {
  id: number;
  body: string;
  html_url: string;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  openaiAnalysis: OpenAIAnalysisResponse;
  githubCommentId: number;
  githubCommentUrl: string;
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch;
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is GitHubPullRequestOpenedPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object');
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (p.action !== 'opened') {
    throw new Error(`Expected action "opened", got "${p.action}"`);
  }
  if (!p.pull_request || typeof p.pull_request !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing pull_request object');
  }
  const pr = p.pull_request as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof pr.title !== 'string' || pr.title.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('pull_request.title is required and must be a non-empty string');
  }
  if (pr.body !== null && pr.body !== undefined && typeof pr.body !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('pull_request.body must be a string or null');
  }
  if (typeof pr.number !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(pr.number)) {
    throw new Error('pull_request.number is required and must be an integer');
  }
  if (!p.repository || typeof p.repository !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing repository object');
  }
  const repo = p.repository as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (!repo.owner || typeof repo.owner !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing repository.owner object');
  }
  const owner = repo.owner as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof owner.login !== 'string' || owner.login.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('repository.owner.login is required and must be a non-empty string');
  }
  if (typeof repo.name !== 'string' || repo.name.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('repository.name is required and must be a non-empty string');
  }
}

async function callOpenAI(
  prompt: string,
  apiKey: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<OpenAIAnalysisResponse> {
  const url = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions';
  const body = {
    model: 'gpt-4o-2024-11-20',
    messages: [
      {
        role: 'user' as const,
        content: prompt,
      },
    ],
    response_format: {
      type: 'json_schema' as const,
      json_schema: {
        name: 'pr_analysis',
        schema: {
          type: 'object',
          properties: {
            summary: { type: 'string' },
            risks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
            suggestedReviewers: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
          },
          required: ['summary', 'risks', 'suggestedReviewers'],
          additionalProperties: false,
        },
        strict: true,
      },
    },
  };

  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`OpenAI API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
  }

  const data = await response.json() as OpenAIAnalysisResponse;
  return data;
}

async function postGitHubComment(
  owner: string,
  repo: string,
  issueNumber: number,
  commentBody: string,
  token: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<GitHubCommentResponse> {
  const url = `https://api.github.com/repos/${encodeURIComponent(owner)}/${encodeURIComponent(repo)}/issues/${issueNumber}/comments`;
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/vnd.github+json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ body: commentBody }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GitHub API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
  }

  return await response.json() as GitHubCommentResponse;
}

function buildPrompt(title: string, body: string | null): string {
  const bodyText = body ?? '(no description provided)';
  return `PR Title: ${title}\n\nPR Body: ${bodyText}\n\nPlease provide a structured analysis with summary, risks, and suggested reviewers.`;
}

function formatComment(analysis: OpenAIAnalysisResponse): string {
  const risksList = analysis.risks.map(r => `- ${r}`).join('\n');
  const reviewersList = analysis.suggestedReviewers.map(r => `- ${r}`).join('\n');
  return `Summary: ${analysis.summary}\n\nRisks:\n${risksList}\n\nSuggested Reviewers:\n${reviewersList}`;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload);
  const typedPayload = payload as GitHubPullRequestOpenedPayload;

  const fetchFn = getFetch(config);

  const prompt = buildPrompt(typedPayload.pull_request.title, typedPayload.pull_request.body);
  const analysis = await callOpenAI(prompt, config.OPENAI_API_KEY, fetchFn);

  const commentBody = formatComment(analysis);
  const comment = await postGitHubComment(
    typedPayload.repository.owner.login,
    typedPayload.repository.name,
    typedPayload.pull_request.number,
    commentBody,
    config.GITHUB_TOKEN,
    fetchFn
  );

  return {
    openaiAnalysis: analysis,
    githubCommentId: comment.id,
    githubCommentUrl: comment.html_url,
  };
}

# GitHub PR Analysis Connector

This connector processes GitHub `pull_request.opened` webhook events, sends the PR title and body to OpenAI for structured analysis, and posts the generated summary back as a comment on the pull request.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a GitHub webhook payload when a pull request is opened
2. **Validates** the payload contains required fields (title, body, PR number, repository info)
3. **Calls OpenAI** with a structured prompt requesting analysis (summary, risks, suggested reviewers)
4. **Formats** the OpenAI response into a markdown comment
5. **Posts** the comment to the GitHub PR using the Issues Comments API
6. **Returns** the OpenAI analysis and GitHub comment ID/URL

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables (passed via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key for chat completions |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub token with `pull_requests:write` permission (fine-grained PAT or GitHub App installation token) |
| `fetch` | (injected) | Optional fetch implementation for testing |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  OPENAI_API_KEY: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY!,
  GITHUB_TOKEN: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN!,
};

// In a webhook handler:
app.post('/github-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config);
    console.log('Posted comment:', result.githubCommentUrl);
    res.json({ success: true, commentId: result.githubCommentId });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connector error:', err);
    res.status(500).json({ error: err.message });
  }
});
```

## Assumptions

- The GitHub webhook payload includes `action: "opened"`, `pull_request.title`, `pull_request.body` (may be null), `pull_request.number`, `repository.owner.login`, and `repository.name`.
- The OpenAI model (`gpt-4o-2024-11-20`) supports structured output with the specified JSON schema.
- The GitHub token has permission to create comments on pull requests (via the Issues Comments API).
- The OpenAI response adheres to the schema: `{ summary: string, risks: string[], suggestedReviewers: string[] }`.
- Pull requests are treated as issues in the GitHub REST API, so the `/issues/{number}/comments` endpoint is used.
- No webhook secret validation is performed by this connector; that should be handled at the HTTP layer.

## API Calls

1. **POST** `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` (Bearer auth: `OPENAI_API_KEY`)
   - Request includes structured output schema with `strict: true`
2. **POST** `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments` (Bearer auth: `GITHUB_TOKEN`)
   - Posts formatted analysis as comment body

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing/invalid payload fields
- Throws with status code and endpoint for non-2xx responses from OpenAI or GitHub
- Handles `null` PR body gracefully (uses placeholder text)

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions",
    "response": {
      "summary": "This PR addresses a login timeout by updating the auth middleware, improving reliability.",
      "risks": [
        "Potential regression in session handling",

      ],

      ]
    }
  },

    "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/comments",
    "response": {
      "id": 123,
      "body": "Summary: ...",
      "html_url": "https://github.com/octocat/hello-world/pull/42#issuecomment-123"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
