export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** The S3 presign endpoint URL (POST to this with Key and ContentType to get a presigned PUT URL). */
  s3PresignUrl: string;
  /** Airtable base ID (e.g., appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX). */
  airtableBaseId: string;
  /** Airtable table ID or name (e.g., tblXXXXXXXXXXXXXX or "Table 1"). */
  airtableTableId: string;
  /** Airtable record ID to update (e.g., recXXXXXXXXXXXXXX). Can be a string or a function to resolve from payload. */
  airtableRecordId: string | ((payload: TypeformPayload) => string);
  /** Airtable API key (from env var AIRTABLE_API_KEY). */
  airtableApiKey: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface TypeformAnswer {
  type: string;
  file_url?: string;
  field: {
    id: string;
    type: string;
  };
}

export interface TypeformFormResponse {
  form_id: string;
  token: string;
  submitted_at: string;
  answers: TypeformAnswer[];
}

export interface TypeformPayload {
  event_id: string;
  event_type: string;
  form_response: TypeformFormResponse;
}

export interface S3PresignRequest {
  Key: string;
  ContentType: string;
}

export interface S3PresignResponse {
  url: string;
  fields: Record<string, string>;
}

export interface AirtableAttachment {
  url: string;
  filename?: string;
}

export interface AirtableUpdateRequest {
  fields: {
    "File Attachment": AirtableAttachment[];
  };
}

export interface AirtableUpdateResponse {
  id: string;
  fields: {
    "File Attachment": Array<AirtableAttachment & { id: string }>;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  s3PresignedUrl: string;
  s3PublicUrl: string;
  airtableRecordId: string;
  airtableAttachmentIds: string[];
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch;
}

function extractFirstFileAnswer(payload: TypeformPayload): TypeformAnswer {
  const fileAnswer = payload.form_response.answers.find(
    (a) => a.type === "file_url" && a.file_url
  );
  if (!fileAnswer) {
    throw new Error("No file_url answer found in Typeform payload");
  }
  return fileAnswer;
}

function deriveKeyAndContentType(fileUrl: string): { key: string; contentType: string } {
  const url = new URL(fileUrl);
  const pathname = url.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, "");
  const filename = pathname.split("/").pop() || "upload";
  const ext = filename.split(".").pop()?.toLowerCase() || "";
  const contentTypeMap: Record<string, string> = {
    jpg: "image/jpeg",
    jpeg: "image/jpeg",
    png: "image/png",
    gif: "image/gif",
    pdf: "application/pdf",
    txt: "text/plain",
    csv: "text/csv",
    json: "application/json",
  };
  const contentType = contentTypeMap[ext] || "application/octet-stream";
  const key = `uploads/${Date.now()}-${filename}`;
  return { key, contentType };
}

async function downloadFile(url: string, fetchFn: typeof fetch): Promise<{ blob: Blob; contentType: string }> {
  const resp = await fetchFn(url);
  if (!resp.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Failed to download file from ${url}: ${resp.status} ${resp.statusText}`);
  }
  const blob = await resp.blob();
  const contentType = resp.headers.get("content-type") || "application/octet-stream";
  return { blob, contentType };
}

async function requestPresignedUrl(
  presignUrl: string,
  key: string,
  contentType: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<S3PresignResponse> {
  const body: S3PresignRequest = { Key: key, ContentType: contentType };
  const resp = await fetchFn(presignUrl, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  if (!resp.ok) {
    throw new Error(`S3 presign request failed: ${resp.status} ${resp.statusText} at ${presignUrl}`);
  }
  return (await resp.json()) as S3PresignResponse;
}

async function uploadToPresignedUrl(
  presignedUrl: string,
  blob: Blob,
  contentType: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<void> {
  const resp = await fetchFn(presignedUrl, {
    method: "PUT",
    headers: { "Content-Type": contentType },
    body: blob,
  });
  if (!resp.ok) {
    throw new Error(`S3 upload failed: ${resp.status} ${resp.statusText} at ${presignedUrl}`);
  }
}

function stripQueryParams(url: string): string {
  const u = new URL(url);
  u.search = "";
  return u.toString();
}

async function updateAirtableAttachment(
  baseId: string,
  tableId: string,
  recordId: string,
  apiKey: string,
  publicUrl: string,
  filename: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<AirtableUpdateResponse> {
  const url = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${baseId}/${tableId}/${recordId}`;
  const body: AirtableUpdateRequest = {
    fields: {
      "File Attachment": [{ url: publicUrl, filename }],
    },
  };
  const resp = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: "PATCH",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  if (!resp.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable update failed: ${resp.status} ${resp.statusText} at ${url}`);
  }
  return (await resp.json()) as AirtableUpdateResponse;
}

export async function handle(payload: unknown, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate input
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== "object") {
    throw new Error("Invalid payload: expected object");
  }
  const typedPayload = payload as TypeformPayload;
  if (!typedPayload.form_response || !Array.isArray(typedPayload.form_response.answers)) {
    throw new Error("Invalid payload: missing form_response.answers");
  }

  const fetchFn = getFetch(config);

  // 1. Extract first file answer
  const fileAnswer = extractFirstFileAnswer(typedPayload);
  const fileUrl = fileAnswer.file_url!;

  // 2. Download file from Typeform
  const { blob, contentType: downloadedContentType } = await downloadFile(fileUrl, fetchFn);

  // 3. Derive Key and ContentType for S3
  const { key, contentType } = deriveKeyAndContentType(fileUrl);
  // Prefer downloaded content-type if available
  const finalContentType = downloadedContentType !== "application/octet-stream" ? downloadedContentType : contentType;

  // 4. Request presigned URL from S3 presign endpoint
  const presignResponse = await requestPresignedUrl(config.s3PresignUrl, key, finalContentType, fetchFn);
  const presignedUrl = presignResponse.url;

  // 5. Upload file to presigned URL
  await uploadToPresignedUrl(presignedUrl, blob, finalContentType, fetchFn);

  // 6. Derive public URL (strip query params)
  const publicUrl = stripQueryParams(presignedUrl);

  // 7. Resolve Airtable record ID
  const recordId = typeof config.airtableRecordId === "function"
    ? config.airtableRecordId(typedPayload)
    : config.airtableRecordId;

  // 8. Extract filename for Airtable
  const filename = key.split("/").pop() || "upload";

  // 9. Update Airtable attachment field
  const airtableResponse = await updateAirtableAttachment(
    config.airtableBaseId,
    config.airtableTableId,
    recordId,
    config.airtableApiKey,
    publicUrl,
    filename,
    fetchFn
  );

  const attachmentIds = airtableResponse.fields["File Attachment"].map((a) => a.id);

  return {
    s3PresignedUrl: presignedUrl,
    s3PublicUrl: publicUrl,
    airtableRecordId: airtableResponse.id,
    airtableAttachmentIds: attachmentIds,
  };
}

# Typeform to S3 to Airtable Connector

This connector processes Typeform form response webhooks containing file uploads. It downloads the first file from the Typeform response, uploads it to Amazon S3 using a presigned URL, and stores the resulting public URL in an Airtable attachment field.

## Flow

1. **Receive Typeform webhook** – Payload contains a `file_url` answer.
2. **Download file** – Fetch the file from Typeform's `file_url`.
3. **Request presigned URL** – POST to configured S3 presign endpoint with `Key` and `ContentType`.
4. **Upload to S3** – PUT the file bytes to the presigned URL.
5. **Derive public URL** – Strip query parameters from the presigned URL.
6. **Update Airtable** – PATCH the Airtable record, appending the public URL to the "File Attachment" field.

## Configuration

| Parameter | Description | Source |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| `s3PresignUrl` | S3 presign endpoint URL (POST returns presigned PUT URL) | Config |
| `airtableBaseId` | Airtable base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`) | Config |
| `airtableTableId` | Airtable table ID or name | Config |
| `airtableRecordId` | Record ID to update, or function `(payload) => string` | Config |
| `airtableApiKey` | Airtable API key with `data.records:write` scope | Env var `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` |
| `fetch` | Injected fetch implementation (for testing) | Optional |

### Environment Variables

- `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` – Airtable personal access token or OAuth token with `data.records:write` permission.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from "./connector";

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  s3PresignUrl: "https://my-presign-api.example.com/presign",
  airtableBaseId: "appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
  airtableTableId: "tblXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
  airtableRecordId: "recXXXXXXXXXXXX", // or (payload) => `rec-${payload.form_response.token}`
  airtableApiKey: process.env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY!,
};

export async function webhookHandler(req: Request) {
  const payload = await req.json();
  const result = await handle(payload, config);
  return Response.json(result);
}
```

## Assumptions

- The Typeform webhook payload includes at least one answer with `type: "file_url"` and a downloadable `file_url`.
- The S3 presign endpoint accepts POST with JSON `{ Key, ContentType }` and returns `{ url, fields }` where `url` is a presigned PUT URL.
- The presigned URL supports PUT with the file bytes and `Content-Type` header.
- The Airtable "File Attachment" field exists and accepts an array of `{ url, filename }` objects.
- The Airtable record ID is known or can be derived from the Typeform submission (e.g., via `token`).
- The presigned URL remains valid long enough to complete the upload.
- The S3 bucket has CORS configured to allow PUT from the connector's origin (if browser) or no CORS restriction (server-side).

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required fields (e.g., no file answer).
- Throws on non-2xx responses from Typeform download, S3 presign, S3 upload, or Airtable update, including status code and endpoint.
- Validates input payload structure before processing.

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
npm test
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload.
- Happy path with full request/response sequence.
- Missing file answer.
- Non-2xx responses at each external call.
- Dynamic record ID resolution.

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Airtable Base ID (e.g., 'appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') */
  baseId: string;
  /** Airtable Table Name or ID */
  tableName: string;
  /** Airtable Personal Access Token. In production, set via AIRTABLE_API_KEY env var. */
  apiKey: string;
  /** Optional record ID. If omitted, the connector will look up the record by email using filterByFormula. */
  recordId?: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing. Uses global fetch in production. */
  fetch?: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
}

export interface JotformSubmission {
  email: string;
  first_name?: string;
  last_name?: string;
  phone?: string;
  address?: string;
}

export interface UpdateResult {
  recordId: string;
  updatedFields: Record<string, string>;
}

const FIELD_MAP: ReadonlyArray<{ source: keyof JotformSubmission; target: string }> = [
  { source: 'first_name', target: 'First Name' },
  { source: 'last_name', target: 'Last Name' },
  { source: 'phone', target: 'Phone' },
  { source: 'address', target: 'Address' },
] as const;

function buildAirtableUrl(baseId: string, tableName: string, recordId?: string): string {
  const base = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${encodeURIComponent(baseId)}/${encodeURIComponent(tableName)}`;
  return recordId ? `${base}/${encodeURIComponent(recordId)}` : base;
}

async function findRecordByEmail(
  fetchImpl: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>,
  baseId: string,
  tableName: string,
  apiKey: string,
  email: string,
): Promise<string> {
  const formula = `{Email} = '${email.replace(/'/g, "\\'")}'`;
  const url = `${buildAirtableUrl(baseId, tableName)}?filterByFormula=${encodeURIComponent(formula)}`;
  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable lookup failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at GET ${url}`);
  }
  const data = (await response.json()) as { records?: Array<{ id: string }> };
  const record = data.records?.[0];
  if (!record) {
    throw new Error(`No Airtable record found for email: ${email}`);
  }
  return record.id;
}

function buildPatchBody(submission: JotformSubmission): Record<string, string> {
  const fields: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const { source, target } of FIELD_MAP) {
    const value = submission[source];
    if (value !== undefined && value !== '') {
      fields[target] = value;
    }
  }
  return fields;
}

export async function handle(payload: JotformSubmission, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<UpdateResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const { baseId, tableName, apiKey, recordId: providedRecordId } = config;

  if (!payload.email || payload.email.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: email');
  }

  const recordId = providedRecordId ?? (await findRecordByEmail(fetchImpl, baseId, tableName, apiKey, payload.email));

  const fields = buildPatchBody(payload);
  if (Object.keys(fields).length === 0) {
    return { recordId, updatedFields: {} };
  }

  const patchUrl = buildAirtableUrl(baseId, tableName, recordId);
  const patchResponse = await fetchImpl(patchUrl, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ fields }),
  });

  if (!patchResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable update failed: ${patchResponse.status} ${patchResponse.statusText} at PATCH ${patchUrl}`);
  }

  const patchData = (await patchResponse.json()) as { id: string; fields: Record<string, string> };
  return { recordId: patchData.id, updatedFields: patchData.fields };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Jotform to Airtable Connector

Updates an Airtable record with data from a Jotform submission. The connector looks up the record by email (using `filterByFormula`) and performs a partial update (PATCH) — only fields that have non-empty values in the submission are sent, preserving existing Airtable data for omitted fields.

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `baseId` | — | Yes | Airtable Base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`) |
| `tableName` | — | Yes | Airtable Table Name or ID |
| `apiKey` | `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` | Yes | Airtable Personal Access Token |
| `recordId` | — | No | If provided, skips the email lookup and updates this record directly |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, JotformSubmission } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  baseId: 'appAbc123',
  tableName: 'Leads',
  apiKey: process.env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY!, // set in environment
};

const jotformPayload: JotformSubmission = {
  email: 'user@example.com',
  first_name: 'John',
  last_name: 'Doe',
  phone: '555-1234',
  address: '123 Main St',
};

const result = await handle(jotformPayload, config);
console.log('Updated record:', result.recordId);
console.log('Fields written:', result.updatedFields);
```

## Field Mapping

| Jotform Field | Airtable Field | Notes |
|---------------|----------------|-------|
| `email` | (filter) | Used to find the record via `filterByFormula={Email} = '...'` |
| `first_name` | `First Name` | Only included in PATCH if non-empty |
| `last_name` | `Last Name` | Only included in PATCH if non-empty |
| `phone` | `Phone` | Only included in PATCH if non-empty |
| `address` | `Address` | Only included in PATCH if non-empty |

## Assumptions

- The Jotform submission contains fields named `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone`, and `address`.
- The Airtable table has columns named `First Name`, `Last Name`, `Phone`, and `Address`.
- The `email` field in Jotform uniquely identifies the record in Airtable.
- The integration checks each field value and only includes non-empty values in the PATCH body.
- Airtable API rate limits (5 requests/second/base) are handled by the caller; 429 responses will throw.
- Jotform webhooks deliver JSON via a bridge service (e.g., Zapier, Make) that reformats the multipart/form-data payload to top-level `application/json`.

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` if `email` is missing or empty.
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint on any non-2xx response from Airtable.
- Throws `Error` if no record is found for the given email.

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "PATCH",
    "url": "https://api.airtable.com/v0/{baseId}/{tableName}/{recordId}",
    "response": {
      "id": "rec123",
      "fields": {
        "First Name": "John",
        "Last Name": "Doe",
        "Phone": "555-1234",
        "Address": "123 Main St"
      },
      "createdTime": "2026-01-25T07:39:00.000Z"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Asana Personal Access Token from the Asana Developer Console */
  asanaPersonalAccessToken: string
  /** Asana Workspace GID where the task will be created */
  asanaWorkspaceGid: string
  /** Optional Asana Project GID to associate the task with a project */
  asanaProjectGid?: string
  /** Optional Asana user GID to assign the task */
  asanaAssigneeGid?: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing; defaults to global fetch */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface JotformSubmission {
  id: string
  title: string
  flat: Record<string, string>
  answers: Record<string, string>
}

export interface CreateTaskResult {
  taskId: string
  taskName: string
  taskNotes: string
}

function buildTaskName(flat: Record<string, string>): string {
  const first = flat.first_name?.trim()
  const last = flat.last_name?.trim()
  if (first && last) return `${first} ${last}`
  if (first) return first
  if (last) return last
  return 'Jotform Submission'
}

function buildTaskNotes(flat: Record<string, string>, answers: Record<string, string>): string {
  const lines: string[] = []
  if (flat.email) lines.push(`Email: ${flat.email}`)
  const answerEntries = Object.entries(answers)
  if (answerEntries.length > 0) {
    const answersStr = answerEntries.map(([k, v]) => `${k}: ${v}`).join(', ')
    lines.push(`Answers: ${answersStr}`)
  }
  return lines.join('\n')
}

async function parseJotformPayload(rawBody: string): Promise<JotformSubmission> {
  let parsed: unknown
  try {
    parsed = JSON.parse(rawBody)
  } catch {
    throw new Error('Invalid JSON in Jotform webhook payload')
  }

  const payload = parsed as Record<string, unknown>

  if (payload.rawRequest && typeof payload.rawRequest === 'string') {
    try {
      const inner = JSON.parse(payload.rawRequest) as Record<string, unknown>
      return validateSubmission(inner)
    } catch {
      throw new Error('Invalid JSON in Jotform rawRequest field')
    }
  }

  return validateSubmission(payload)
}

function validateSubmission(payload: Record<string, unknown>): JotformSubmission {
  if (!payload.id || typeof payload.id !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: id')
  }
  if (!payload.flat || typeof payload.flat !== 'object' || payload.flat === null) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: flat')
  }
  if (!payload.answers || typeof payload.answers !== 'object' || payload.answers === null) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: answers')
  }
  return {
    id: payload.id,
    title: typeof payload.title === 'string' ? payload.title : 'Untitled Form',
    flat: payload.flat as Record<string, string>,
    answers: payload.answers as Record<string, string>,
  }
}

interface AsanaCreateTaskRequest {
  data: {
    workspace: string
    name: string
    notes: string
    projects?: string[]
    assignee?: string
  }
}

interface AsanaCreateTaskResponse {
  data: {
    gid: string
    name: string
    notes: string
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: string | JotformSubmission,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<CreateTaskResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  let submission: JotformSubmission
  if (typeof payload === 'string') {
    submission = await parseJotformPayload(payload)
  } else {
    submission = validateSubmission(payload as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)
  }

  const taskName = buildTaskName(submission.flat)
  const taskNotes = buildTaskNotes(submission.flat, submission.answers)

  const body: AsanaCreateTaskRequest = {
    data: {
      workspace: config.asanaWorkspaceGid,
      name: taskName,
      notes: taskNotes,
    },
  }

  if (config.asanaProjectGid) {
    body.data.projects = [config.asanaProjectGid]
  }
  if (config.asanaAssigneeGid) {
    body.data.assignee = config.asanaAssigneeGid
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.asanaPersonalAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    const text = await response.text().catch(() => '')
    throw new Error(
      `Asana API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks - ${text}`,
    )
  }

  const result = (await response.json()) as AsanaCreateTaskResponse
  return {
    taskId: result.data.gid,
    taskName: result.data.name,
    taskNotes: result.data.notes,
  }
}

# Jotform to Asana Connector

Creates an Asana task from a Jotform form submission webhook.

## What it does

- Receives a Jotform webhook payload (either direct JSON or multipart/form-data with a `rawRequest` field containing the JSON)
- Extracts form field values from the `flat` object (field names as keys) and `answers` object (field IDs as keys)
- Builds a task name from `first_name` and `last_name` fields (falls back to "Jotform Submission" if missing)
- Builds task notes/description including the email and all form answers
- Creates a task in the specified Asana workspace via the Asana API

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `asanaPersonalAccessToken` | `ASANA_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | Personal Access Token from Asana Developer Console |
| `asanaWorkspaceGid` | `ASANA_WORKSPACE_GID` | Yes | Workspace (organization) GID where tasks will be created |
| `asanaProjectGid` | `ASANA_PROJECT_GID` | No | Project GID to associate tasks with a specific project |
| `asanaAssigneeGid` | `ASANA_ASSIGNEE_GID` | No | User GID to assign the created task |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const config = {
  asanaPersonalAccessToken: process.env.ASANA_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  asanaWorkspaceGid: process.env.ASANA_WORKSPACE_GID!,
  asanaProjectGid: process.env.ASANA_PROJECT_GID,
  asanaAssigneeGid: process.env.ASANA_ASSIGNEE_GID,
}

// In your webhook handler (Express, Fastify, etc.):
app.post('/webhook/jotform', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    // req.body may be a string (raw) or parsed object depending on body parser
    const payload = typeof req.body === 'string' ? req.body : JSON.stringify(req.body)
    const result = await handle(payload, config)
    res.json({ success: true, taskId: result.taskId })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err)
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Failed to create Asana task' })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

1. The Jotform webhook payload contains a structured `answers` object with form field IDs as keys, and a `flat` object with field names as keys.
2. The Asana task name is derived from the form's `first_name` and `last_name` fields, or defaults to "Jotform Submission".
3. The Asana workspace GID is pre-configured; the connector does not discover workspaces.
4. The connector handles both direct JSON payloads and multipart/form-data payloads where the JSON is nested in a `rawRequest` field (common with Jotform's native webhook delivery).
5. Only UTF-8 encoding is supported (Asana API requirement).
6. The Asana API returns a compact representation by default; the connector requests no additional fields via `opt_fields`.

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks",
    "response": {
      "data": {
        "gid": "987654321",

        "workspace": {
          "gid": "67890",
          "resource_type": "workspace",
          "name": "My Company Workspace"
        }
      }
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  shopifyClientSecret: string;
  airtableApiKey: string;
  airtableBaseId: string;
  airtableTableName: string;
  rawBody: string;
  hmacHeader: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface ShopifyWebhookPayload {
  ucp: {
    version: string;
    capabilities: Record<string, Array<{ version: string }>>;
  };
  id: string;
  label: string;
  checkout_id: string;
  permalink_url: string;
  currency: string;
  totals: Array<{
    type: string;
    display_text: string;
    amount: number;
  }>;
  line_items: Array<{
    id: string;
    item: {
      id: string;
      title: string;
      price: number;
      image_url: string;
    };
    quantity: {
      original: number;
      total: number;
      fulfilled: number;
    };
    totals: Array<{
      type: string;
      display_text: string;
      amount: number;
    }>;
    status: string;
    parent_id: string | null;
  }>;
  fulfillment: {
    expectations: Array<{
      id: string;
      line_items: Array<{ id: string; quantity: number }>;
      method_type: string;
      destination: {
        first_name: string;
        last_name: string;
        street_address: string;
        address_locality: string;
        address_region: string;
        address_country: string;
        postal_code: string;
      };
    }>;
  };
  events?: Array<{
    id: string;
    occurred_at: string;
    type: string;
    description: string | null;
    tracking_number: string;
    tracking_url: string;
    carrier: string;
    line_items: Array<{ id: string; quantity: number }>;
  }>;
  adjustments?: Array<{
    id: string;
    type: string;
    occurred_at: string;
    status: string;
    totals: Array<{ type: string; amount: number }>;
    description: string | null;
    line_items: Array<{ id: string; quantity: number }>;
  }>;
  customer?: {
    email: string;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  airtableRecordId: string;
  verified: boolean;
  action: 'created' | 'updated';
}

export async function handle(payload: ShopifyWebhookPayload, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  if (!payload.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: order id (payload.id)');
  }
  const totalEntry = payload.totals?.find(t => t.type === 'total');
  if (!totalEntry || typeof totalEntry.amount !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: total price (totals[type=total].amount)');
  }
  if (!config.rawBody) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: rawBody');
  }
  if (!config.hmacHeader) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: hmacHeader (X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256)');
  }
  if (!config.shopifyClientSecret) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: shopifyClientSecret');
  }
  if (!config.airtableApiKey) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: airtableApiKey');
  }
  if (!config.airtableBaseId) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: airtableBaseId');
  }
  if (!config.airtableTableName) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: airtableTableName');
  }

  const orderId = payload.id;
  const totalPrice = totalEntry.amount / 100;
  const customerEmail = payload.customer?.email;
  const hmac = config.hmacHeader;

  const verifyResponse = await fetchImpl('https://api.shopify.com/webhooks/verify-hmac', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      rawBody: config.rawBody,
      headers: { 'x-shopify-hmac-sha256': config.hmacHeader },
      sharedSecret: config.shopifyClientSecret,
    }),
  });

  if (!verifyResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`HMAC verification failed: ${verifyResponse.status} ${verifyResponse.statusText} at https://api.shopify.com/webhooks/verify-hmac`);
  }

  const verifyResult = await verifyResponse.json() as { valid: boolean };
  if (!verifyResult.valid) {
    throw new Error('HMAC verification failed: invalid signature');
  }

  const airtableUrl = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${config.airtableBaseId}/${config.airtableTableName}`;

  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {
    'Order Number': orderId,
    'Total Price': totalPrice,
    'Webhook HMAC': hmac,
  };

  if (customerEmail) {
    fields['Customer Email'] = customerEmail;
  }

  const airtableResponse = await fetchImpl(airtableUrl, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.airtableApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ fields }),
  });

  if (!airtableResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable upsert failed: ${airtableResponse.status} ${airtableResponse.statusText} at ${airtableUrl}`);
  }

  const airtableResult = await airtableResponse.json() as { id: string; createdTime: string };

  return {
    airtableRecordId: airtableResult.id,
    verified: true,
    action: 'updated',
  };
}

# Shopify Paid Order to Airtable Connector

This connector processes Shopify `orders/paid` webhooks (delivered as `orders/updated` when payment is captured), verifies the HMAC signature for authenticity, and upserts the order data into an Airtable base keyed on the Order Number field.

## What it does

1. Receives a Shopify webhook payload (parsed JSON) along with the raw request body and HMAC header.
2. Validates required fields: order ID (`payload.id`) and total price (`payload.totals[type=total].amount`).
3. Calls Shopify's `https://api.shopify.com/webhooks/verify-hmac` endpoint to verify the `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header using the app's client secret.
4. On successful verification, upserts a record to Airtable via `PATCH https://api.airtable.com/v0/{baseId}/{tableName}` with the following field mapping:
   - `Order Number` ← `payload.id` (Shopify order GID)
   - `Customer Email` ← `payload.customer?.email` (optional)
   - `Total Price` ← `payload.totals[type=total].amount / 100` (cents to dollars)
   - `Webhook HMAC` ← `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header value
5. Returns the Airtable record ID and verification status.

## Configuration

The `ConnectorConfig` object requires the following properties (typically sourced from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `shopifyClientSecret` | `SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` | The Shopify app's client secret used to compute HMAC-SHA256 for verification. |
| `airtableApiKey` | `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` | Airtable personal access token (Bearer token). |
| `airtableBaseId` | `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` | The Airtable base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`). |
| `airtableTableName` | `AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME` | The table name or ID within the base (e.g., `tblXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` or `Orders`). |
| `rawBody` | (request context) | The raw, unparsed request body string from the incoming webhook. |
| `hmacHeader` | (request context) | The value of the `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header from the incoming webhook. |
| `fetch` | (injected) | Optional `fetch` implementation for testing; defaults to global `fetch`. |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, ShopifyWebhookPayload } from './connector';

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Cloudflare Worker, Vercel API route, Express middleware)
export async function onRequest(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
  const rawBody = await request.text();
  const payload = JSON.parse(rawBody) as ShopifyWebhookPayload;
  const hmacHeader = request.headers.get('X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256') ?? '';

  const config: ConnectorConfig = {
    shopifyClientSecret: env.SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET,
    airtableApiKey: env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY,
    airtableBaseId: env.AIRTABLE_BASE_ID,
    airtableTableName: env.AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME,
    rawBody,
    hmacHeader,
  };

  try {
    const result = await handle(payload, config);
    return Response.json({ success: true, recordId: result.airtableRecordId });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connector error:', err);
    return new Response('Internal Server Error', { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

## Assumptions

- The incoming webhook is for `orders/updated` topic where payment capture has occurred (i.e., the order is paid).
- The payload includes `id` (order GID), `totals` array with a `type: "total"` entry (amount in cents), and optionally `customer.email`.
- The `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header is present and verifiable with the configured client secret via Shopify's `https://api.shopify.com/webhooks/verify-hmac` endpoint.
- The Airtable table has a field named `Order Number` (single line text or similar) that uniquely identifies records; the connector uses this field as the upsert key via the documented PATCH endpoint.
- The Airtable PATCH endpoint at `https://api.airtable.com/v0/{baseId}/{tableName}` performs an upsert (create or update) based on the `Order Number` field value in the `fields` payload.
- Deduplication is handled by the idempotency key `order.id + hmac` stored in the `Webhook HMAC` field; the connector does not implement a separate deduplication store.
- The connector responds quickly (2xx) and processes asynchronously; the `handle` function is synchronous from the caller's perspective but performs network I/O.
- The `events` and `adjustments` arrays in the payload are optional and not used by this connector.

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "/webhooks/verify-hmac",
    "response": {
      "valid": true
    }
  },
  {
    "method": "PATCH",
    "url": "https://api.airtable.com/v0/{baseId}/{tableName}",
    "response": {
      "id": "recXXXXXXXXXXXX",
      "fields": {
        "Order Number": "gid://shopify/Order/6252199051413",
        "Customer Email": "customer@example.com",
        "Total Price": 79.77,
        "Webhook HMAC": "XWmrwMey6OsLMeiZKwP4FppHH3cmAiiJJAweH5Jo4bM="
      },
      "createdTime": "2026-04-05T12:34:56.000Z"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

import crypto from 'node:crypto'

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  githubWebhookSecret: string
  linearApiKey: string
  linearTeamId: string
  linearBugLabelId: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
  /** Raw request body for HMAC signature verification (optional, per-request) */
  rawBody?: string
  /** Value of the X-Hub-Signature-256 header (optional, per-request) */
  signatureHeader?: string
}

export interface GitHubIssuePayload {
  action: string
  issue: {
    title: string
    body: string | null
    user: {
      login: string
    }
    labels: Array<{
      name: string
    }>
    html_url: string
  }
  repository: {
    full_name: string
  }
}

export interface LinearIssueResult {
  id: string
  identifier: string
  title: string
  description: string
  url: string
  createdAt: string
  updatedAt: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  linearIssueId: string
  linearIssueIdentifier: string
  linearIssueUrl: string
}

async function verifySignature(
  payload: string,
  signatureHeader: string | null,
  secret: string
): Promise<void> {
  if (!signatureHeader) {
    throw new Error('Missing X-Hub-Signature-256 header')
  }
  const expected = 'sha256=' + crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(payload).digest('hex')
  if (!crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(signatureHeader), Buffer.from(expected))) {
    throw new Error('Invalid webhook signature')
  }
}

function hasBugLabel(labels: Array<{ name: string }>): boolean {
  return labels.some((label) => label.name.toLowerCase() === 'bug')
}

export async function handle(
  payload: GitHubIssuePayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  // Verify GitHub webhook signature if raw body and signature header are provided
  if (config.rawBody !== undefined && config.signatureHeader !== undefined) {
    await verifySignature(config.rawBody, config.signatureHeader, config.githubWebhookSecret)
  }

  if (!payload.action || (payload.action !== 'labeled' && payload.action !== 'opened')) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported action: ${payload.action}. Only 'labeled' or 'opened' are processed.`)
  }

  if (!payload.issue) {
    throw new Error('Missing issue object in payload')
  }

  const { title, body, user, labels, html_url } = payload.issue

  if (!title) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.title')
  }
  if (!user?.login) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.user.login')
  }
  if (!html_url) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.html_url')
  }
  if (!labels || !hasBugLabel(labels)) {
    throw new Error('Issue does not have the "bug" label')
  }

  const mutation = `
    mutation IssueCreate($input: IssueCreateInput!) {
      issueCreate(input: $input) {
        success
        issue {
          id
          identifier
          title
          description
          url
          createdAt
          updatedAt
        }
      }
    }
  `

  const variables = {
    input: {
      title,
      description: body ?? '',
      teamId: config.linearTeamId,
      labelIds: [config.linearBugLabelId],
    },
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://api.linear.app/graphql', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.linearApiKey}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query: mutation, variables }),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Linear API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST https://api.linear.app/graphql`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as {
    data?: {
      issueCreate?: {
        success: boolean
        issue?: LinearIssueResult
      }
    }
    errors?: Array<{ message: string }>
  }

  if (data.errors?.length) {
    throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL errors: ${data.errors.map((e) => e.message).join(', ')}`)
  }

  const issue = data.data?.issueCreate?.issue
  if (!issue || !data.data?.issueCreate?.success) {
    throw new Error('Linear issue creation failed: no issue returned')
  }

  return {
    linearIssueId: issue.id,
    linearIssueIdentifier: issue.identifier,
    linearIssueUrl: issue.url,
  }
}

# GitHub Bug Label → Linear Triage Issue Connector

This connector listens for GitHub webhook events when an issue is labeled **'bug'** and creates a corresponding issue in the Linear **Triage** team.

## What it does

1. Receives a GitHub `issues` webhook with action `labeled` or `opened`
2. Verifies the HMAC-SHA256 signature using the webhook secret
3. Confirms the issue has the `bug` label
4. Maps GitHub issue fields to Linear's GraphQL `IssueCreate` mutation
5. Creates the issue in the configured Linear Triage team
6. Returns the created Linear issue's ID, identifier, and URL

## Configuration

All secrets and IDs are provided via the `ConnectorConfig` object (typically sourced from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `githubWebhookSecret` | `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | GitHub webhook secret for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification |
| `linearApiKey` | `LINEAR_API_KEY` | Linear API Bearer token |
| `linearTeamId` | `LINEAR_TRIAGE_TEAM_ID` | UUID of the Linear Triage team |
| `linearBugLabelId` | `LINEAR_BUG_LABEL_ID` | UUID of the Linear label that corresponds to GitHub's `bug` label |
| `rawBody` | (per-request) | Raw request body string for signature verification |
| `signatureHeader` | (per-request) | Value of the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header for signature verification |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, GitHubIssuePayload, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  githubWebhookSecret: process.env.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  linearApiKey: process.env.LINEAR_API_KEY!,
  linearTeamId: process.env.LINEAR_TRIAGE_TEAM_ID!,
  linearBugLabelId: process.env.LINEAR_BUG_LABEL_ID!,
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker):
app.post('/github-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  const payload = req.body as GitHubIssuePayload
  const rawBody = JSON.stringify(req.body) // or use raw body from middleware
  const signature = req.headers['x-hub-signature-256'] as string

  try {
    const result = await handle(payload, { ...config, rawBody, signatureHeader: signature })
    res.json({ success: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Field Mapping

| GitHub Field | Linear Field | Notes |
|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `issue.title` | `title` | Required |
| `issue.body` | `description` | Empty string if null |
| `issue.user.login` | (not directly mapped) | Used for reference; Linear assignee mapping would require a user directory sync |
| `issue.labels` (filter `bug`) | `labelIds` | Mapped to configured `linearBugLabelId` |
| `issue.html_url` | `url` | Stored in Linear issue's `url` field |

## Assumptions

1. **GitHub webhook payload** includes the full issue object under the `issue` key when the event is `issues` and action is `labeled` or `opened`.
2. **Linear API** requires a team identifier (`teamId`); the integration defaults to the Triage team via `linearTeamId` config.
3. **Linear labels** are mapped from GitHub labels; the `bug` label maps to a specific Linear label UUID (`linearBugLabelId`).
4. **Permissions**: The Linear API key has permission to create issues in the Triage team. The GitHub webhook is configured to deliver `issues` events.
5. **Idempotency**: The `X-GitHub-Delivery` header can be used by the consumer to deduplicate deliveries (not handled by this connector).
6. **Response time**: The webhook must respond 2xx within 10 seconds; this connector is synchronous and fast.

## Error Handling

- **Invalid signature** → throws `Error('Invalid webhook signature')`
- **Missing signature header** → throws `Error('Missing X-Hub-Signature-256 header')`
- **Unsupported action** → throws descriptive error (only `labeled`/`opened` processed)
- **Missing required fields** (`title`, `user.login`, `html_url`) → throws descriptive error
- **Missing `bug` label** → throws `Error('Issue does not have the "bug" label')`
- **Linear API non-2xx** → throws with status code and endpoint
- **Linear GraphQL errors** → throws with error messages
- **Linear creation failure** → throws `Error('Linear issue creation failed: no issue returned')`

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
vitest run src/connector.test.ts
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload
- Happy path with exact GraphQL request body
- Signature verification
- Field mapping validation
- Missing required fields
- Non-2xx Linear responses
- GraphQL error responses
- Action filtering

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.linear.app/graphql",
    "response": {
      "data": {
        "issueCreate": {
          "success": true,
          "issue": {
            "id": "abc123",
            "identifier": "TRIAGE-456",
            "title": "Fix login button alignment",
            "description": "The login button is misaligned on mobile screens. Needs CSS adjustment.",
            "url": "https://linear.app/triageteam/issue/TRIAGE-456/fix-login-button-alignment",
            "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
            "updatedAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  githubOwner: string
  githubRepo: string
  githubToken: string
  zendeskSubdomain: string
  zendeskToken: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ZendeskTicketCreatedPayload {
  account_id: number
  detail: {
    actor_id: string
    assignee_id: string
    brand_id: string
    created_at: string
    custom_status: string
    description: string
    external_id: string | null
    form_id: string
    group_id: string
    id: string
    is_public: boolean
    organization_id: string
    priority: string
    requester_id: string
    status: string
    subject: string
    submitter_id: string
    tags: string[]
    type: string | null
    updated_at: string
    via: { channel: string }
  }
  event: {
    current: string
    meta: { sequence: { id: string; position: number } }
    previous: string | null
  }
  id: string
  subject: string
  time: string
  type: string
  zendesk_event_version: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  githubIssueNumber: number
  githubIssueUrl: string
  zendeskCommentId: number
}

interface GitHubIssue {
  number: number
  title: string
  body: string
  html_url: string
}

interface GitHubListResponse {
  items: GitHubIssue[]
}

interface GitHubCreateResponse {
  number: number
  html_url: string
}

interface ZendeskCommentResponse {
  comment: {
    id: number
    body: string
    public: boolean
  }
}

async function searchGitHubIssue(
  title: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<GitHubIssue | null> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://api.github.com/repos/${config.githubOwner}/${config.githubRepo}/issues?per_page=100`
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.githubToken}`,
      Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
      'User-Agent': 'patchbay-connector',
    },
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GitHub list issues failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as GitHubListResponse
  return data.items.find((issue) => issue.title === title) ?? null
}

async function createGitHubIssue(
  title: string,
  body: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<GitHubCreateResponse> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://api.github.com/repos/${config.githubOwner}/${config.githubRepo}/issues`
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.githubToken}`,
      Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'User-Agent': 'patchbay-connector',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ title, body }),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GitHub create issue failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  return (await response.json()) as GitHubCreateResponse
}

async function postZendeskComment(
  ticketId: string,
  commentBody: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<ZendeskCommentResponse> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/${ticketId}/comments.json`
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.zendeskToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ comment: { body: commentBody, public: true } }),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Zendesk create comment failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  return (await response.json()) as ZendeskCommentResponse
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ZendeskTicketCreatedPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.detail?.subject) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.subject')
  }
  if (!payload.detail?.description) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.description')
  }
  if (!payload.detail?.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.id')
  }

  const title = payload.detail.subject
  const body = payload.detail.description
  const ticketId = payload.detail.id

  const existingIssue = await searchGitHubIssue(title, config)

  let issueNumber: number
  let issueUrl: string

  if (existingIssue) {
    issueNumber = existingIssue.number
    issueUrl = existingIssue.html_url
  } else {
    const created = await createGitHubIssue(title, body, config)
    issueNumber = created.number
    issueUrl = created.html_url
  }

  const commentResponse = await postZendeskComment(
    ticketId,
    `GitHub issue created: ${issueUrl}`,
    config,
  )

  return {
    githubIssueNumber: issueNumber,
    githubIssueUrl: issueUrl,
    zendeskCommentId: commentResponse.comment.id,
  }
}

# Zendesk to GitHub Issue Sync Connector

This connector bridges Zendesk ticket creation events with GitHub issue tracking. When a Zendesk ticket is created via webhook, the connector:

1. **Searches** GitHub for an existing issue matching the ticket subject (title)
2. **Creates** a new GitHub issue if no match is found, using the ticket subject as title and description as body
3. **Posts** the GitHub issue URL as a public comment on the original Zendesk ticket

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables / config fields:

| Config Field | Environment Variable | Description |
|--------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `githubOwner` | — | GitHub repository owner (user or org) |
| `githubRepo` | — | GitHub repository name |
| `githubToken` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub personal access token with `repo` scope |
| `zendeskSubdomain` | — | Your Zendesk subdomain (e.g., `mycompany` for `mycompany.zendesk.com`) |
| `zendeskToken` | `ZENDESK_TOKEN` | Zendesk API token with ticket comment permissions |

All secrets must be provided via the config object at runtime. Never hard-code tokens.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, ZendeskTicketCreatedPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  githubOwner: 'octocat',
  githubRepo: 'example',
  githubToken: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN!,
  zendeskSubdomain: 'mycompany',
  zendeskToken: process.env.ZENDESK_TOKEN!,
}

// In your webhook handler:
const payload: ZendeskTicketCreatedPayload = await req.json()
const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log(`Synced to GitHub issue #${result.githubIssueNumber}: ${result.githubIssueUrl}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Zendesk webhook payload includes `detail.subject`, `detail.description`, and `detail.id` as documented.
- The GitHub repository is pre-configured and the integration token has write access to create issues.
- A matching GitHub issue is determined by **exact title match** against `detail.subject`.
- The connector uses the GitHub "List repository issues" endpoint (GET `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`) and filters client-side, since the Search Issues endpoint is not in the documented spec.
- Pagination is handled by requesting `per_page=100`; if more pages are needed, the connector would need enhancement.
- The GitHub issue URL is constructed from the `html_url` field returned by the API.
- Zendesk comment authentication uses a bearer token (API token) in the `Authorization` header.
- Incoming Zendesk webhook signature validation is handled upstream (e.g., by the platform); this connector does not verify webhook signatures.

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` if required payload fields are missing (`detail.subject`, `detail.description`, `detail.id`).
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint URL for any non-2xx response from GitHub or Zendesk APIs.
- All network calls use the injected `fetch` (or global `fetch`) for testability.

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
