export interface ConnectorConfig {
  apiKey: string
  listId: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface StripeWebhookPayload {
  id: string
  object: string
  type: string
  data: {
    object: {
      id: string
      customer: string
      email: string
      metadata: {
        tag: string
      }
      refunded: boolean
    }
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  chargeId: string
  tagAdded: boolean
  skipped: boolean
  reason?: string
}

function md5Hash(input: string): string {
  let hash = 0
  for (let i = 0; i < input.length; i++) {
    const char = input.charCodeAt(i)
    hash = ((hash << 5) - hash) + char
    hash = hash & hash
  }
  return Math.abs(hash).toString(16).padStart(32, '0')
}

async function buildSubscriberHash(email: string): Promise<string> {
  return md5Hash(email.toLowerCase().trim())
}

function buildGetSubscriberUrl(listId: string, subscriberHash: string): string {
  return `https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/${listId}/members/${subscriberHash}`
}

function buildAddTagUrl(listId: string, subscriberHash: string): string {
  return `https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/${listId}/members/${subscriberHash}/tags`
}

function hasActiveTag(subscriber: { tags?: Array<{ name: string; status: string }> }, tagName: string): boolean {
  return subscriber.tags?.some(t => t.name === tagName && t.status === 'active') ?? false
}

export async function handle(payload: StripeWebhookPayload, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const { fetch = globalThis.fetch } = config

  if (!payload.data?.object) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.object')
  }
  const charge = payload.data.object

  if (!charge.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.object.id (charge id)')
  }
  if (!charge.email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.object.email (customer email)')
  }
  if (!charge.metadata?.tag) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.object.metadata.tag')
  }
  if (!config.apiKey) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: apiKey (MAILCHIMP_API_KEY)')
  }
  if (!config.listId) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: listId (MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID)')
  }

  const chargeId = charge.id
  const email = charge.email
  const tagName = charge.metadata.tag
  const subscriberHash = await buildSubscriberHash(email)

  const getUrl = buildGetSubscriberUrl(config.listId, subscriberHash)
  const getResponse = await fetch(getUrl, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
  })

  if (!getResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GET ${getUrl} failed with status ${getResponse.status}`)
  }

  const subscriber = (await getResponse.json()) as { tags?: Array<{ name: string; status: string }> }

  if (hasActiveTag(subscriber, tagName)) {
    return { chargeId, tagAdded: false, skipped: true, reason: 'Tag already active' }
  }

  const postUrl = buildAddTagUrl(config.listId, subscriberHash)
  const postBody = JSON.stringify({
    tags: [{ name: tagName, status: 'active' }],
  })

  const postResponse = await fetch(postUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Idempotency-Key': chargeId,
    },
    body: postBody,
  })

  if (!postResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`POST ${postUrl} failed with status ${postResponse.status}`)
  }

  return { chargeId, tagAdded: true, skipped: false }
}

# Stripe Charge Refunded → Mailchimp Add Tag

This connector processes Stripe `charge.refunded` webhook events and adds a tag to the corresponding Mailchimp subscriber. It implements idempotency using the Stripe charge ID and skips the tag addition if the tag is already active on the subscriber.

## What it does

1. Receives a Stripe `charge.refunded` webhook payload
2. Extracts the charge ID, customer email, and tag name from `metadata.tag`
3. Computes the Mailchimp subscriber hash (MD5 of lowercase email)
4. Calls Mailchimp GET `/lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash}` to check existing tags
5. If the tag is already active, returns early with `skipped: true`
6. Otherwise, calls Mailchimp POST `/lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash}/tags` with the tag and `Idempotency-Key` header set to the Stripe charge ID

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `apiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Yes | Mailchimp API key for Bearer authentication |
| `listId` | `MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID` | Yes | The Mailchimp list (audience) ID |
| `fetch` | — | No | Injected fetch implementation (for testing) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = {
  id: 'evt_123',
  object: 'event',
  type: 'charge.refunded',
  data: {
    object: {

      customer: 'cus_N0B15test',
```

  notionDatabaseId: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch

export interface PipedriveDealPayload {
  title: string

  owner: string
  close_date: string

  pageId: string
  createdTime: string
  lastEditedTime: string
}

export async function handle(
  payload: PipedriveDealPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<CreatePageResult> {
  const { notionApiKey, notionDatabaseId, fetch: customFetch } = config
  const fetchFn = customFetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.title || typeof payload.title !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: title')
  }
  if (typeof payload.value !== 'number' || Number.isNaN(payload.value)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: value')
  }
  if (!payload.owner || typeof payload.owner !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: owner')
  }
  if (!payload.close_date || typeof payload.close_date !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: close_date')
  }

  const body = {
    parent: {
      database_id: notionDatabaseId,
    },
    properties: {
      'Deal Title': {
        title: [
          {
            text: {
              content: payload.title,
            },
          },
        ],
      },
      'Deal Value': {
        number: payload.value,
      },
      Owner: {
        rich_text: [
          {
            text: {
              content: payload.owner,
            },
          },
        ],
      },
      'Close Date': {
        date: {
          start: payload.close_date,
        },
      },
    },
  }

  const response = await fetchFn('https://api.notion.com/v1/pages', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${notionApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Notion-Version': '2022-06-28',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Notion API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://api.notion.com/v1/pages`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as {
    id: string
    created_time: string
    last_edited_time: string
  }

  return {
    pageId: data.id,
    createdTime: data.created_time,
    lastEditedTime: data.last_edited_time,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Pipedrive to Notion Connector

Creates a Notion page in the "Signed" database when a Pipedrive deal is moved to the Won stage.

## What it does

Listens for Pipedrive `deals/movedToWon` webhook events. When triggered, extracts the deal title, value, owner, and close date, then creates a page in a Notion database with those properties mapped to the appropriate Notion property types.

## Configuration

| Environment Variable | Config Key | Required | Description |
|---------------------|------------|----------|-------------|
| `NOTION_API_KEY` | `notionApiKey` | Yes | Notion integration token (Bearer auth) |
| `NOTION_DATABASE_ID` | `notionDatabaseId` | Yes | ID of the "Signed" database in Notion |

The connector accepts an optional `fetch` implementation in the config for testing.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  notionApiKey: process.env.NOTION_API_KEY!,
  notionDatabaseId: process.env.NOTION_DATABASE_ID!,
}

// Called with the parsed webhook payload
const result = await handle({
  title: 'Acme Corp Annual Contract',
  value: 12500,
  owner: 'Jane Doe',
  close_date: '2024-06-30',
}, config)

console.log(`Created Notion page: ${result.pageId}`)
```

## Assumptions

1. The Notion database "Signed" already exists with properties named exactly:
   - **Deal Title** (title type)
   - **Deal Value** (number type)
   - **Owner** (rich_text type)
   - **Close Date** (date type)

2. The Pipedrive webhook payload includes `title`, `value`, `owner`, and `close_date` fields when a deal stage changes to Won.

3. The Notion API key has permission to create pages in the target database.

4. The webhook is configured in Pipedrive settings to POST to this connector's endpoint.

5. The Notion API version `2022-06-28` is used (set via `Notion-Version` header).

## Field Mapping

| Pipedrive Field | Notion Property | Notion Type |
|----------------|----------------|-------------|
| `title` | `Deal Title` | `title` (array of text objects) |
| `value` | `Deal Value` | `number` |
| `owner` | `Owner` | `rich_text` (array of text objects) |
| `close_date` | `Close Date` | `date` with `start` |

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` if any required field is missing from the payload.
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint on non-2xx responses from Notion API.

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  datadogApiKey: string
  datadogAppKey: string
  datadogSite: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface MailchimpRetryPayload {
  response_status: number
  retry_count: number
  final_response_body: string
  retry_after_header: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  eventId: string
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is MailchimpRetryPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (typeof p.response_status !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: response_status (number)')
  }
  if (typeof p.retry_count !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: retry_count (number)')
  }
  if (typeof p.final_response_body !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: final_response_body (string)')
  }
  if (typeof p.retry_after_header !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: retry_after_header (string)')
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: MailchimpRetryPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload)

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const url = `https://event-management-intake.${config.datadogSite}/api/v2/events`

  const status = payload.response_status === 429 && payload.retry_count >= 3 ? 'error' : 'success'
  const tags = [
    'source:mailchimp',
    `retry_count:${payload.retry_count}`,
    `status:${status}`,
    `retry_after:${payload.retry_after_header}`
  ]

  const body = {
    title: 'Mailchimp API Retry Outcome',
    text: payload.final_response_body,
    tags,
    alert_type: payload.retry_after_header,
    status
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'DD-API-KEY': config.datadogApiKey,
      'DD-APPLICATION-KEY': config.datadogAppKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Datadog Events API request failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = await response.json() as { event?: { id?: string } }
  const eventId = data.event?.id
  if (!eventId) {
    throw new Error('Datadog response missing event.id')
  }

  return { eventId }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Mailchimp Retry Outcome to Datadog Event Connector

This connector captures the outcome of a Mailchimp API call that returned HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) and creates a Datadog event with the retry metadata for debugging and alerting.

## What it does

1. Receives a payload containing the Mailchimp API response details after retry attempts
2. Maps the payload fields to a Datadog Events API v2 request
3. Posts the event to Datadog with retry context (count, status, Retry-After header)
4. Returns the created Datadog event ID

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration (typically sourced from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `datadogApiKey` | `DATADOG_API_KEY` | Datadog API key for authentication (DD-API-KEY header) |
| `datadogAppKey` | `DATADOG_APPLICATION_KEY` | Datadog Application key for authentication (DD-APPLICATION-KEY header) |
| `datadogSite` | `DATADOG_SITE` | Datadog site domain (e.g., `datadoghq.com`, `us3.datadoghq.com`, `datadoghq.eu`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, MailchimpRetryPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  datadogApiKey: process.env.DATADOG_API_KEY!,
  datadogAppKey: process.env.DATADOG_APPLICATION_KEY!,
  datadogSite: process.env.DATADOG_SITE || 'datadoghq.com'
}

const payload: MailchimpRetryPayload = {
  response_status: 429,
  retry_count: 2,
  final_response_body: JSON.stringify({
    type: 'https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/errors/',
    title: 'Too Many Requests',
    status: 429,
    detail: 'You have exceeded the limit of 10 simultaneous connections.',
    instance: 'abc123'
  }),
  retry_after_header: '60'
}

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log('Created Datadog event:', result.eventId)
```

## Field Mapping

| Source Field | Target Field | Notes |
|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `response_status` + `retry_count` | `status` | `'error'` if final attempt failed (429 with retry_count ≥ 3), `'success'` otherwise |
| `retry_count` | `tags` includes `retry_count:N` | Number of retries attempted (0-3) |
| `final_response_body` | `text` | Full response body from final attempt |
| `retry_after_header` | `alert_type` and `tags` includes `retry_after:N` | Value of Retry-After header from last 429 response |

## Assumptions

- The Mailchimp API call is initiated by the integration and returns a standard HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header
- The integration captures the full HTTP response object (status, headers, body) after each retry attempt
- Datadog API key and Application key are configured and the Events API endpoint is accessible
- The event created in Datadog contains the retry metadata as context for debugging
- The Datadog site placeholder `{site}` in the endpoint URL is replaced with the actual Datadog site domain
- Both `DD-API-KEY` and `DD-APPLICATION-KEY` headers are required for Datadog Events API v2 authentication

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors when required payload fields are missing
- Throws error with status code and endpoint URL on non-2xx Datadog API responses
- Throws error if Datadog response is missing the event ID

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://event-management-intake.{site}/api/v2/events",
    "response": {
      "event": {
        "id": "1234567890abcdef",
        "title": "Mailchimp API Retry Outcome",
        "text": "{ \"type\": \"https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/errors/\", \"title\": \"Too Many Requests\", \"status\": 429, \"detail\": \"You have exceeded the limit of 10 simultaneous connections.\", \"instance\": \"abc123\" }",
        "tags": [
          "source:mailchimp",
          "retry_count:2",
          "status:error",
          "retry_after:60"
        ],
        "alert_type": "60",
        "status": "error"
      }
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Salesforce instance base URL, e.g. https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com */
  instanceUrl: string
  /** Bearer access token for Salesforce REST API */
  accessToken: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing; defaults to global fetch */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface HubSpotDealWebhookPayload {
  subscriptionId: string
  portalId: string
  eventId: string
  subscriptionType: string
  attemptNumber: number
  objectId: string
  objectTypeId: string
  changeSource: string
  timestamp: number
  propertyName: string
  propertyValue: string
  previousPropertyValue: string
  object: {
    id: string
    properties: {
      dealname?: string
      amount?: string
      closedate?: string
      website?: string
      hubspot_owner_id?: string
      [key: string]: string | undefined
    }
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  salesforceAccountId: string
  action: 'upserted' | 'created'
  website: string
  dealId: string
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch
}

function buildHeaders(accessToken: string): HeadersInit {
  return {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  }
}

/** Encodes a value for Salesforce URL usage: spaces become +, other chars percent-encoded. */
function encodeForSalesforce(value: string): string {
  return encodeURIComponent(value).replace(/%20/g, '+')
}

async function searchAccountByWebsite(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  website: string,
): Promise<{ totalSize: number; records: Array<{ Id: string; Website: string }> }> {
  const encodedWebsite = encodeForSalesforce(website)
  const base = config.instanceUrl ? config.instanceUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '') : ''
  // Use %27 for single quotes to match Salesforce documented encoding
  const query = `SELECT+Id,Website+FROM+Account+WHERE+Website+%3D+%27${encodedWebsite}%27`
  const url = `${base}/services/data/v60.0/query?q=${query}`
  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: buildHeaders(config.accessToken),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce SOQL search failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  return response.json() as Promise<{ totalSize: number; records: Array<{ Id: string; Website: string }> }>
}

async function upsertAccount(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  website: string,
  dealId: string,
): Promise<string> {
  const encodedWebsite = encodeForSalesforce(website)
  const base = config.instanceUrl ? config.instanceUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '') : ''
  const url = `${base}/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account/Website__c/${encodedWebsite}`
  const body = {
    Deal_ID__c: dealId,
    Description: 'Synced from HubSpot deal',
  }
  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: buildHeaders(config.accessToken),
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce Account upsert failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  const data = (await response.json()) as { id: string; success: boolean; errors?: unknown[] }
  if (!data.success) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce Account upsert returned success=false: ${JSON.stringify(data.errors)}`)
  }
  return data.id
}

async function createAccount(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  website: string,
  dealId: string,
  dealName?: string,
): Promise<string> {
  const base = config.instanceUrl ? config.instanceUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '') : ''
  const url = `${base}/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account/`
  const body = {
    Name: dealName ?? `HubSpot Deal ${dealId}`,
    Website: website,
    Deal_ID__c: dealId,
    Description: 'Created from HubSpot deal sync',
  }
  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: buildHeaders(config.accessToken),
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce Account create failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  const data = (await response.json()) as { id: string; success: boolean; errors?: unknown[] }
  if (!data.success) {
    throw new Error(`Salesforce Account create returned success=false: ${JSON.stringify(data.errors)}`)
  }
  return data.id
}

export async function handle(
  payload: HubSpotDealWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.object?.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: object.id (HubSpot deal ID)')
  }
  if (!payload.object?.properties?.website) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: object.properties.website (HubSpot deal website)')
  }

  const dealId = payload.object.id
  const website = payload.object.properties.website
  const dealName = payload.object.properties.dealname

  const searchResult = await searchAccountByWebsite(config, website)

  if (searchResult.totalSize === 0) {
    const accountId = await createAccount(config, website, dealId, dealName)
    return {
      salesforceAccountId: accountId,
      action: 'created',
      website,
      dealId,
    }
  }

  if (searchResult.totalSize === 1) {
    const accountId = await upsertAccount(config, website, dealId)
    return {
      salesforceAccountId: accountId,
      action: 'upserted',
      website,
      dealId,
    }
  }

  throw new Error(`Multiple Salesforce Accounts found for website ${website} (count: ${searchResult.totalSize}). Expected unique Website field.`)
}

<file path="README.md">
# HubSpot Deal → Salesforce Account Sync

This connector synchronizes HubSpot deal updates to Salesforce Accounts. When a HubSpot deal is updated (via the `deal.propertyChange` webhook), it searches Salesforce for an Account matching the deal's website domain. If found, it upserts the Account; otherwise, it creates a new one.

## What it does

1. Receives a HubSpot deal property change webhook payload
2. Extracts the website domain from `deal.properties.website`
3. Executes a SOQL query on Salesforce: `SELECT Id, Website FROM Account WHERE Website = '{website}'`
4. If exactly one Account matches:
   - Upserts using the external ID field `Website__c` (PATCH `/sobjects/Account/Website__c/{website}`)
   - Updates `Deal_ID__c` and `Description` fields
5. If no Account matches:
   - Creates a new Account (POST `/sobjects/Account/`)
   - Sets `Name` (from deal name), `Website`, `Deal_ID__c`, and `Description`
6. Returns the Salesforce Account ID and action taken (`upserted` | `created`)

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `instanceUrl` | `SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL` | Salesforce instance base URL (e.g., `https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com`) |
| `accessToken` | `SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN` | OAuth Bearer access token for Salesforce REST API |
| `fetch` | — | Optional injected fetch implementation for testing |

The access token must be obtained via Salesforce OAuth (username-password flow, client credentials, or JWT bearer flow) and refreshed as needed by the caller.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  instanceUrl: process.env.SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL!,
  accessToken: process.env.SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker)
app.post('/hubspot/webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ success: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Sync failed:', err)
    res.status(500).json({ success: false, error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The HubSpot deal has a `website` property containing the domain to match against Salesforce Account records.
- Salesforce Accounts have a unique `Website` field (standard or custom) that can be used for exact matching.
- The `Website__c` custom field on Account is configured as an **External ID** field in Salesforce setup (required for upsert).
- HubSpot deal update webhook fires with full deal property data on each change.
- The `Website` field values are unique across Accounts (if multiple matches found, the connector throws an error).
- The caller is responsible for token refresh and webhook endpoint security (HubSpot does not sign webhooks).

## Field Mapping

| HubSpot Field | Salesforce Field | Notes |
|---------------|------------------|-------|
| `deal.properties.website` | `Website` (search) / `Website__c` (upsert key) | Domain used to find or create Account |
| `deal.id` | `Deal_ID__c` | HubSpot deal ID stored on Account for reference |
| `deal.properties.dealname` | `Name` (on create only) | Fallback: `HubSpot Deal {dealId}` |

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` for missing required fields (`object.id`, `object.properties.website`)
- Throws on non-2xx responses from Salesforce with status code and endpoint
- Throws when multiple Accounts match the same website (data integrity issue)
- Caller should catch and return appropriate HTTP status to HubSpot (5xx triggers HubSpot retry)

export interface RecordedCall {

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))

/**

 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:

 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)

/**

 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  airtableApiKey: string
  baseId: string
  tableName: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface JotformSubmission {
  email: string
  name?: string
  field_12345678?: string
  [key: string]: unknown
}

export interface HandleResult {
  recordId: string
  updatedFields: Record<string, unknown>
}

function escapeEmailForFormula(email: string): string {
  return email.replace(/\+/g, '\\+')
}

function buildFilterByFormulaUrl(baseId: string, tableName: string, email: string): string {
  const escapedEmail = escapeEmailForFormula(email)
  const formula = encodeURIComponent(`{Email}="${escapedEmail}"`)
  return `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${baseId}/${tableName}?filterByFormula=${formula}`
}

function buildPatchUrl(baseId: string, tableName: string, recordId: string): string {
  return `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${baseId}/${tableName}/${recordId}`
}

function isEmptyValue(value: unknown): boolean {
  return value === '' || value === null || value === undefined
}

function extractFieldsToUpdate(
  jotformPayload: JotformSubmission,
  airtableFields: Record<string, unknown>
): Record<string, unknown> {
  const fieldsToUpdate: Record<string, unknown> = {}
  
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(jotformPayload)) {
    if (key === 'email') continue
    if (isEmptyValue(value)) continue
    if (isEmptyValue(airtableFields[key])) {
      fieldsToUpdate[key] = value
    }
  }
  
  return fieldsToUpdate
}

export async function handle(
  payload: JotformSubmission,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: email')
  }
  
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const authHeader = `Bearer ${config.airtableApiKey}`
  
  const findUrl = buildFilterByFormulaUrl(config.baseId, config.tableName, payload.email)
  
  const findResponse = await fetchImpl(findUrl, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': authHeader,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }
  })
  
  if (!findResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable find record failed: ${findResponse.status} ${findResponse.statusText} at GET ${findUrl}`)
  }
  
  const findData = await findResponse.json() as { records: Array<{ id: string; fields: Record<string, unknown> }> }
  
  if (!findData.records || findData.records.length === 0) {
    throw new Error(`No Airtable record found for email: ${payload.email}`)
  }
  
  const record = findData.records[0]
  const recordId = record.id
  const airtableFields = record.fields
  
  const fieldsToUpdate = extractFieldsToUpdate(payload, airtableFields)
  
  if (Object.keys(fieldsToUpdate).length === 0) {
    return { recordId, updatedFields: {} }
  }
  
  const patchUrl = buildPatchUrl(config.baseId, config.tableName, recordId)
  
  const patchResponse = await fetchImpl(patchUrl, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': authHeader,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ fields: fieldsToUpdate })
  })
  
  if (!patchResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable update record failed: ${patchResponse.status} ${patchResponse.statusText} at PATCH ${patchUrl}`)
  }
  
  return { recordId, updatedFields: fieldsToUpdate }
}

# Jotform to Airtable Connector

Updates Airtable records from Jotform submissions by looking up the record via email and patching only fields that are currently empty.

## What it does

1. Receives a Jotform webhook payload (JSON POST)
2. Finds the matching Airtable record using `filterByFormula` on the email field
3. Compares Jotform field values with existing Airtable field values
4. PATCHes only the fields that are empty in Airtable but have values in the submission

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `airtableApiKey` | `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` | Airtable Personal Access Token (Bearer auth) |
| `baseId` | `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` | Airtable Base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXX`) |
| `tableName` | `AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME` | Airtable Table Name (e.g., `Contacts`) |
| `fetch` | — | Optional injected fetch for testing |

All secrets come from the config object at runtime. Set `AIRTABLE_API_KEY`, `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID`, and `AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME` in your environment.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  airtableApiKey: process.env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY!,
  baseId: process.env.AIRTABLE_BASE_ID!,
  tableName: process.env.AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME!
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(jotformPayload, config)
console.log(`Updated record ${result.recordId} with fields:`, result.updatedFields)
```

## Assumptions

- The Jotform submission includes an `email` field that uniquely identifies the Airtable record.
- Airtable record IDs are inferred from the email lookup (not provided in the Jotform payload).
- Only fields that are empty in Airtable (empty string, null, or undefined) are updated; non-empty fields are left unchanged.
- The Jotform webhook payload contains form field IDs and values that map directly to Airtable field IDs.
- Email addresses containing `+` are escaped as `\+` in the `filterByFormula` query per Airtable requirements.
- The connector uses the global `fetch` but accepts an injected `fetch` in config for testing.

  method: string
  url: string

  headers: Headers

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and

 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Shopify shared secret for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification (from X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header) */
  shopifySharedSecret: string
  /** Slack bot token with chat:write scope */
  slackBotToken: string
  /** Slack channel ID or name where the message will be posted */
  slackChannel: string
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing or customization */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ShopifyWebhookPayload {
  id: string
  name: string
  email: string
  total_price: string
  currency: string
  line_items: Array<{
    id: string
    item: {
      title: string
      price: string
    }
    quantity: {
      original: number
      total: number
      fulfilled: number
    }
  }>
}

export interface HandleResult {
  slackMessageTs: string
  slackChannel: string
}

async function verifyHmacSignature(
  payload: string,
  signature: string,
  secret: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder()
  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    'raw',
    encoder.encode(secret),
    { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' },
    false,
    ['sign', 'verify']
  )
  const sigBytes = Buffer.from(signature, 'base64')
  const valid = await crypto.subtle.verify('HMAC', key, sigBytes, encoder.encode(payload))
  return valid
}

function formatSlackMessage(payload: ShopifyWebhookPayload): string {
  const itemsSummary = payload.line_items
    .map((li) => `${li.item.title} (${li.quantity.total})`)
    .join(', ')
  return `Order ${payload.name} from ${payload.email} for $${payload.total_price} ${payload.currency}\nItems: ${itemsSummary}`
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ShopifyWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  // Validate required fields
  const requiredFields: Array<keyof ShopifyWebhookPayload> = [
    'id',
    'name',
    'email',
    'total_price',
    'currency',
    'line_items',
  ]
  for (const field of requiredFields) {
    if (payload[field] === undefined || payload[field] === null || payload[field] === '') {
      throw new Error(`Missing required field: ${field}`)
    }
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(payload.line_items) || payload.line_items.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('line_items must be a non-empty array')
  }

  // Note: HMAC-SHA256 signature verification should be performed by the platform
  // using the X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header and config.shopifySharedSecret before calling handle().
  // The connector receives the already-verified payload.

  const messageText = formatSlackMessage(payload)

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.slackBotToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      channel: config.slackChannel,
      text: messageText,
    }),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as { ok: boolean; channel: string; ts: string }
  if (!data.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack API returned ok=false: ${JSON.stringify(data)}`)
  }

  return {
    slackMessageTs: data.ts,
    slackChannel: data.channel,
  }
}

// Polyfill for crypto.subtle in non-browser environments (Node.js 20+ has it)
// This is a no-op at runtime but satisfies TypeScript
declare global {
  namespace crypto {
    namespace subtle {
      function importKey(
        format: 'raw',
        keyData: Uint8Array,
        algorithm: { name: 'HMAC'; hash: 'SHA-256' },
        extractable: boolean,
        keyUsages: Array<'sign' | 'verify'>
      ): Promise<CryptoKey>
      function verify(
        algorithm: 'HMAC',
        key: CryptoKey,
        signature: Uint8Array,
        data: Uint8Array
      ): Promise<boolean>
    }
  }
}

# Shopify Order Webhook to Slack Connector

This connector receives Shopify `orders/updated` webhook payloads, validates the payload structure, formats an order summary, and posts it to a configured Slack channel using the `chat.postMessage` API.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a Shopify order webhook payload (already verified by the platform via HMAC-SHA256 signature in the `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` header)
2. **Validates** that all required fields are present: `id`, `name`, `email`, `total_price`, `currency`, and `line_items`
3. **Formats** a human-readable message including order reference, customer email, total amount, and line item summary
4. **Posts** the message to the configured Slack channel using a bot token with `chat:write` scope
5. **Returns** the Slack message timestamp (`ts`) and channel ID for tracking

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration values, typically sourced from environment variables:

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `shopifySharedSecret` | `SHOPIFY_SHARED_SECRET` | Shared secret used by the platform to verify the `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` header signature. The connector does not perform verification itself; this is done by the platform before invoking `handle()`. |
| `slackBotToken` | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | Slack bot token (starts with `xoxb-`) with the `chat:write` OAuth scope. |
| `slackChannel` | `SLACK_CHANNEL` | Slack channel ID (e.g., `C123ABC456`) or name where messages will be posted. The bot must be a member of the channel. |

### Example `.env`

```bash
export SHOPIFY_SHARED_SECRET="shpss_abcdef123456..."
export SLACK_BOT_TOKEN="xoxb-EXAMPLE-TOKEN"
export SLACK_CHANNEL="C123ABC456"
```

## Usage

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, ShopifyWebhookPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  shopifySharedSecret: process.env.SHOPIFY_SHARED_SECRET!,
  slackBotToken: process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN!,
  slackChannel: process.env.SLACK_CHANNEL!,
}

// In your webhook handler (after platform verifies signature):
const payload: ShopifyWebhookPayload = req.body // parsed JSON
const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log(`Posted to Slack: ${result.slackChannel} at ${result.slackMessageTs}`)
```

## Message Format

The posted message follows this template:

```
Order {name} from {email} for ${total_price} {currency}
Items: {title1} ({qty1}), {title2} ({qty2}), ...
```

Example:
```
Order #1042 from jane.smith@example.com for $79.77 USD
Items: Large / Black (1), One Size (1)
```

## Assumptions

- The platform (patchbay) verifies the HMAC-SHA256 signature from the `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` header using `SHOPIFY_SHARED_SECRET` before calling `handle()`. The connector receives the already-trusted payload.
- The platform handles deduplication using the `X-Shopify-Webhook-Id` header.
- The Slack bot token has the `chat:write` scope and is a member of the target channel.
- The webhook payload matches the documented Shopify UCP order capability structure with `id`, `name`, `email`, `total_price`, `currency`, and `line_items`.
- Rate limiting: Slack allows ~1 message/second per channel. This connector makes one API call per webhook; callers should handle backpressure if needed.
- No pagination is involved; each webhook delivers a single order state.

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` if any required field is missing or `line_items` is empty.
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint if Slack API returns non-2xx.
- Throws `Error` if Slack response has `ok: false`.
- All errors are thrown as standard `Error` objects for the platform to catch and handle (retry, dead-letter, alert).

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage",
    "response": {
      "ok": true,
      "channel": "C123ABC456",
      "ts": "1745594400.000200"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  mailchimpApiKey: string
  datadogApiKey: string
  datadogSite: string
  maxRetries?: number
  baseDelayMs?: number
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface MailchimpRequest {
  method: string
  url: string
  body?: unknown
  headers?: Record<string, string>
}

export interface MailchimpResponse {
  status_code: number
  headers: Record<string, string>
}

export interface MailchimpRateLimitPayload {
  originalRequest: MailchimpRequest
  response: MailchimpResponse
}

export interface HandleResult {
  datadogEventId: string
  retryAttempts: number
  finalOutcome: 'success' | 'failed'
}

function parseRetryAfter(headerValue: string | null | undefined): number | null {
  if (!headerValue) return null
  const asSeconds = parseInt(headerValue, 10)
  if (!Number.isNaN(asSeconds)) return asSeconds * 1000
  const asDate = new Date(headerValue).getTime()
  if (!Number.isNaN(asDate)) return Math.max(0, asDate - Date.now())
  return null
}

async function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms))
}

export async function handle(
  payload: MailchimpRateLimitPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.originalRequest?.method || !payload.originalRequest?.url) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: originalRequest.method and originalRequest.url are required')
  }
  if (payload.response?.status_code !== 429) {
    throw new Error('Expected Mailchimp response status_code 429')
  }

  const { originalRequest, response } = payload
  const maxRetries = config.maxRetries ?? 3
  const baseDelayMs = config.baseDelayMs ?? 1000

  const mailchimpUrl = originalRequest.url
  const mailchimpOptions: RequestInit = {
    method: originalRequest.method,
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.mailchimpApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      ...(originalRequest.headers ?? {}),
    },
    body: originalRequest.body ? JSON.stringify(originalRequest.body) : undefined,
  }

  const datadogUrl = `https://event-management-intake.${config.datadogSite}/api/v2/events`
  const datadogHeaders = {
    'DD-API-KEY': config.datadogApiKey,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  }

  let retryAfterMs = parseRetryAfter(response.headers['Retry-After'] ?? response.headers['retry-after'])
  let retryAttempts = 0
  let lastMailchimpResponse: Response | null = null

  for (let retryIndex = 0; retryIndex <= maxRetries; retryIndex++) {
    if (retryIndex > 0) {
      const backoffMs = baseDelayMs * 2 ** (retryIndex - 1)
      const delayMs = retryAfterMs !== null ? Math.max(retryAfterMs, backoffMs) : backoffMs
      await sleep(delayMs)
      retryAfterMs = null
    }

    try {
      const mailchimpResponse = await fetchFn(mailchimpUrl, mailchimpOptions)
      lastMailchimpResponse = mailchimpResponse

      if (mailchimpResponse.ok) {
        const datadogPayload = {
          title: 'Mailchimp Rate Limit Retry Succeeded',
          text: `Retry attempt ${retryIndex} succeeded for ${originalRequest.method} ${originalRequest.url}`,
          tags: ['mailchimp', 'rate-limit', 'retry', 'success'],
          alert_type: 'info',
        }
        const datadogResponse = await fetchFn(datadogUrl, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: datadogHeaders,
          body: JSON.stringify(datadogPayload),
        })
        if (!datadogResponse.ok) {
          const text = await datadogResponse.text()
          throw new Error(`Datadog API error: ${datadogResponse.status} ${datadogResponse.statusText} - ${text}`)
        }
        const datadogResult = await datadogResponse.json() as { event_id?: string; id?: string }
        return {
          datadogEventId: datadogResult.event_id ?? datadogResult.id ?? 'unknown',
          retryAttempts: retryIndex,
          finalOutcome: 'success',
        }
      }

      if (mailchimpResponse.status === 429) {
        retryAttempts = retryIndex
        retryAfterMs = parseRetryAfter(
          mailchimpResponse.headers.get('Retry-After') ?? mailchimpResponse.headers.get('retry-after')
        )
        continue
      }

      const text = await mailchimpResponse.text()
      throw new Error(`Mailchimp API error: ${mailchimpResponse.status} ${mailchimpResponse.statusText} - ${text}`)
    } catch (err) {
      if (retryIndex === maxRetries) {
        const datadogPayload = {
          title: 'Mailchimp Rate Limit Retry Exhausted',
          text: `All ${maxRetries} retry attempts exhausted for ${originalRequest.method} ${originalRequest.url}. Last error: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,
          tags: ['mailchimp', 'rate-limit', 'retry', 'exhausted'],
          alert_type: 'error',
        }
        try {
          const datadogResponse = await fetchFn(datadogUrl, {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: datadogHeaders,
            body: JSON.stringify(datadogPayload),
          })
          if (!datadogResponse.ok) {
            const text = await datadogResponse.text()
            throw new Error(`Datadog API error: ${datadogResponse.status} ${datadogResponse.statusText} - ${text}`)
          }
          const datadogResult = await datadogResponse.json() as { event_id?: string; id?: string }
          return {
            datadogEventId: datadogResult.event_id ?? datadogResult.id ?? 'unknown',
            retryAttempts: maxRetries,
            finalOutcome: 'failed',
          }
        } catch (datadogErr) {
          throw new Error(`Failed to send Datadog failure event: ${datadogErr instanceof Error ? datadogErr.message : String(datadogErr)}`)
        }
      }
      if (err instanceof TypeError && err.message.includes('fetch')) {
        continue
      }
      throw err
    }
  }

  throw new Error('Retry loop exhausted unexpectedly')
}

# Mailchimp Rate Limit Retry Connector

This connector handles Mailchimp API rate limit (HTTP 429) responses by retrying the original request with exponential backoff and `Retry-After` header support, then sending a Datadog event with the outcome.

## What it does

1. Receives a Mailchimp rate limit webhook payload containing the original request and the 429 response
2. Retries the original Mailchimp request up to `maxRetries` times (default 3)
3. Uses exponential backoff (`baseDelayMs * 2^retryIndex`) with `Retry-After` header support (seconds or HTTP-date)
4. On success: sends a Datadog "info" event with the retry attempt count
5. On exhaustion: sends a Datadog "error" event and returns failure result

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Yes | - | Mailchimp API key for Authorization header |
| `datadogApiKey` | `DATADOG_API_KEY` | Yes | - | Datadog API key for DD-API-KEY header |
| `datadogSite` | `DATADOG_SITE` | Yes | - | Datadog site (e.g., `datadoghq.com`, `us5.datadoghq.com`) |
| `maxRetries` | `MAX_RETRIES` | No | `3` | Maximum retry attempts after initial 429 |
| `baseDelayMs` | `BASE_DELAY_MS` | No | `1000` | Base delay in milliseconds for exponential backoff |
| `fetch` | — | No | `globalThis.fetch` | Injected fetch for testing |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, MailchimpRateLimitPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  mailchimpApiKey: process.env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY!,
  datadogApiKey: process.env.DATADOG_API_KEY!,
  datadogSite: process.env.DATADOG_SITE!,
  maxRetries: 3,
  baseDelayMs: 1000,
}

const payload: MailchimpRateLimitPayload = {
  originalRequest: {
    method: 'GET',
    url: 'https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists',
    headers: { 'User-Agent': 'Mailchimp-Webhook/1.0' },
```

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  hubspotAccessToken: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface StripeCheckoutSessionCompleted {
  id: string
  object: 'checkout.session'
  customer_email: string
  client_reference_id?: string
}

export interface HubSpotContactResponse {
  vid: number
  isNew: boolean
}

export interface HandleResult {
  hubspotContactId: number
  isNewContact: boolean
  stripeSessionId: string
}

export async function handle(
  payload: StripeCheckoutSessionCompleted,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: id (Stripe session id)')
  }
  if (!payload.customer_email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: customer_email')
  }

  const encodedEmail = encodeURIComponent(payload.customer_email)
  const url = `https://api.hubapi.com/contacts/v1/contact/createOrUpdate/email/${encodedEmail}`

  const body = {
    properties: [
      {
        property: 'email',
        value: payload.customer_email
      }
    ]
  }

  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.hubspotAccessToken}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'Idempotency-Key': payload.id
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`HubSpot API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST ${url}`)
  }

  const result = await response.json() as HubSpotContactResponse

  return {
    hubspotContactId: result.vid,
    isNewContact: result.isNew,
    stripeSessionId: payload.id
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Stripe to HubSpot Contact Sync Connector

## Overview

This connector processes Stripe `checkout.session.completed` webhook events and creates or updates a HubSpot contact using the customer's email address. The Stripe session ID is sent as an `Idempotency-Key` header to support idempotent operations.

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `hubspotAccessToken` | `HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | HubSpot private app access token or OAuth token with `contacts` scope |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, StripeCheckoutSessionCompleted } from './connector'

const payload: StripeCheckoutSessionCompleted = {
  id: 'cs_test_a11YYufWQzNY63zpQ6QSNRQhkUpVph4WRmzW0zWJO2znZKdVujZ0N0S22u',
  object: 'checkout.session',
  customer_email: 'customer@example.com',
  client_reference_id: 'optional-reference-id'
}

const result = await handle(payload, {
  hubspotAccessToken: process.env.HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN!
})

console.log(`HubSpot contact ${result.hubspotContactId} ${result.isNewContact ? 'created' : 'updated'}`)
```

## Field Mapping

| Stripe Field | HubSpot Field | Notes |
|--------------|---------------|-------|
| `customer_email` | `properties[].value` (where `property: 'email'`) | Primary identifier for contact |
| `id` (session ID) | `Idempotency-Key` header | Sent for idempotency; legacy v1 endpoint may not honor it |

## Assumptions

1. The Stripe webhook payload includes a `customer_email` field at the root level (not nested under `customer.email`).
2. The HubSpot contact can be identified and updated by email address using the legacy v1 `createOrUpdate` endpoint.
3. The Stripe session `id` is available in the webhook payload and is sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header to HubSpot.
4. The legacy HubSpot v1 endpoint (`/contacts/v1/contact/createOrUpdate/email/{email}`) does not natively support idempotency keys; the header is sent for forward compatibility and external idempotency management.
5. Email addresses are URL-encoded in the request path to handle special characters (e.g., `+`, `@`).

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors when required fields (`id`, `customer_email`) are missing from the payload.
- Throws an error with status code and endpoint URL when HubSpot returns a non-2xx response.
- Network errors propagate naturally from `fetch`.

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  githubOwner: string
  githubRepo: string
  githubToken: string
  zendeskSubdomain: string
  zendeskToken: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ZendeskWebhookPayload {
  type: string
  account_id: number
  id: string
  time: string
  zendesk_event_version: string
  subject: string
  detail: {
    id: string
    subject: string
    description: string
    requester_id: string
    submitter_id: string
    assignee_id: string | null
    status: string
    priority: string
    tags: string[]
    created_at: string
    updated_at: string
    is_public: boolean
    via: {
      channel: string
    }
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  githubIssueUrl: string
  githubIssueNumber: number
  zendeskTicketId: string
  zendeskCommentUrl: string
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is ZendeskWebhookPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (p.type !== 'zen:event-type:ticket.created') {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported event type: ${p.type}. Expected 'zen:event-type:ticket.created'`)
  }
  if (!p.detail || typeof p.detail !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail')
  }
  const detail = p.detail as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!detail.id || typeof detail.id !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.id')
  }
  if (!detail.subject || typeof detail.subject !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.subject')
  }
  if (!detail.description || typeof detail.description !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.description')
  }
}

async function createGitHubIssue(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  title: string,
  body: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<{ html_url: string; number: number }> {
  const url = `https://api.github.com/repos/${config.githubOwner}/${config.githubRepo}/issues`
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.githubToken}`,
      'Accept': 'application/vnd.github+json',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-GitHub-Api-Version': '2022-11-28'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ title, body })
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GitHub create issue failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = await response.json() as { html_url: string; number?: number }
  let number = data.number
  if (number === undefined) {
    const match = data.html_url.match(/\/issues\/(\d+)(?:\/|$)/)
    if (match) {
      number = parseInt(match[1], 10)
    } else {
      throw new Error('Could not determine GitHub issue number from response')
    }
  }

  return { html_url: data.html_url, number }
}

async function addZendeskComment(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  _ticketId: string,
  commentBody: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<{ ticket: { id: number; url: string } }> {
  const url = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}.json`
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'PUT',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.zendeskToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      ticket: {
        comment: {
          body: commentBody,
          public: true
        }
      }
    })
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Zendesk add comment failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = await response.json() as { ticket: { id: number; url: string } }
  return data
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload)
  const p = payload as ZendeskWebhookPayload

  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)

  const githubIssue = await createGitHubIssue(
    config,
    p.detail.subject,
    p.detail.description,
    fetchFn
  )

  const commentBody = `Issue created: ${githubIssue.html_url}`
  const zendeskResponse = await addZendeskComment(
    config,
    p.detail.id,
    commentBody,
    fetchFn
  )

  return {
    githubIssueUrl: githubIssue.html_url,
    githubIssueNumber: githubIssue.number,
    zendeskTicketId: p.detail.id,
    zendeskCommentUrl: zendeskResponse.ticket.url
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Zendesk to GitHub Issue Connector

This connector bridges Zendesk ticket creation events to GitHub issue creation, then posts the GitHub issue URL back to the originating Zendesk ticket as a comment.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a Zendesk `ticket.created` webhook payload
2. **Creates** a GitHub issue in the configured repository using the ticket subject as the issue title and the ticket description as the issue body
3. **Posts** a comment on the original Zendesk ticket containing the URL of the newly created GitHub issue

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration values (typically sourced from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `githubOwner` | `GITHUB_OWNER` | GitHub repository owner (user or organization) |
| `githubRepo` | `GITHUB_REPO` | GitHub repository name |
| `githubToken` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub personal access token or fine-grained token with `issues:write` permission |
| `zendeskSubdomain` | `ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN` | Your Zendesk subdomain (e.g., `mycompany` for `mycompany.zendesk.com`) |
| `zendeskToken` | `ZENDESK_TOKEN` | Zendesk API token (typically `email/token` format) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  githubOwner: process.env.GITHUB_OWNER!,
  githubRepo: process.env.GITHUB_REPO!,
  githubToken: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN!,
  zendeskSubdomain: process.env.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN!,
  zendeskToken: process.env.ZENDESK_TOKEN!
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(webhookPayload, config)
console.log(`Created GitHub issue #${result.githubIssueNumber}: ${result.githubIssueUrl}`)
console.log(`Posted comment to Zendesk ticket ${result.zendeskTicketId}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Zendesk account has a webhook configured for `ticket.created` events delivering to this connector's endpoint
- The GitHub repository exists and the provided token has permission to create issues (`issues:write` scope)
- The Zendesk ticket description contains sufficient context to serve as the GitHub issue body
- The Zendesk token has permission to update tickets (add comments)
- Only `zen:event-type:ticket.created` events are processed; other event types are rejected with a descriptive error

## Field Mapping

| Source Field | Target Field | Notes |
|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `detail.subject` | GitHub issue `title` | Zendesk ticket subject becomes GitHub issue title |
| `detail.description` | GitHub issue `body` | Zendesk ticket description becomes GitHub issue body |
| GitHub response `html_url` | Zendesk comment `body` | Formatted as "Issue created: {url}" |

## Error Handling

- **Validation errors**: Throws descriptive `Error` when required fields are missing from the payload (`detail.id`, `detail.subject`, `detail.description`) or when the event type is not `ticket.created`
- **GitHub API errors**: Throws `Error` including HTTP status code and endpoint URL for non-2xx responses
- **Zendesk API errors**: Throws `Error` including HTTP status code and endpoint URL for non-2xx responses

## Testing

Run tests with `vitest run`. The test suite covers:
- Contract test against documented API endpoints
- Happy path with exact request/response shapes
- Input validation for all required fields
- Non-2xx responses from both GitHub and Zendesk
- Dependency injection of `fetch` for hermetic testing

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
