}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  intercomAccessToken: string
  zendeskApiToken: string
  zendeskSubdomain: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface IntercomWebhookPayload {
  topic: string
  data: {
    item: {
      type: string
      id: string
      conversation_tags: Array<{
        id: string
        name: string
      }>
    }
  }
}

export interface IntercomConversation {
  type: string
  id: string
  url: string
  subject: string
}

export interface ZendeskTicketRequest {
  ticket: {
    subject: string
    comment: {
      body: string
    }
  }
}

export interface ZendeskTicketResponse {
  ticket: {
    id: number
    subject: string
    url: string
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  conversationId: string
  ticketId: number
  ticketUrl: string
}

async function fetchConversation(
  conversationId: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<IntercomConversation> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://api.intercom.io/conversations/${conversationId}`
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.intercomAccessToken}`,
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Intercom GET ${url} failed with ${response.status}`)
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<IntercomConversation>
}

async function createZendeskTicket(
  subject: string,
  description: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<ZendeskTicketResponse> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets.json`
  const body: ZendeskTicketRequest = {
    ticket: {
      subject,
      comment: {
        body: description,
      },
    },
  }

  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.zendeskApiToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Zendesk POST ${url} failed with ${response.status}`)
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<ZendeskTicketResponse>
}

export async function handle(
  payload: IntercomWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.topic) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: topic')
  }
  if (payload.topic !== 'conversation.tag.created') {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported topic: ${payload.topic}`)
  }

  if (!payload.data?.item) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.item')
  }

  const { id: conversationId, conversation_tags } = payload.data.item

  if (!conversationId) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.item.id')
  }

  if (!Array.isArray(conversation_tags) || conversation_tags.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.item.conversation_tags')
  }

  const refundTag = conversation_tags.find((tag) => tag.name === 'refund')
  if (!refundTag) {
    throw new Error('Conversation does not have the "refund" tag')
  }

  const conversation = await fetchConversation(conversationId, config)

  const subject = conversation.subject || `Intercom Conversation ${conversation.id}`
  const description = `View the conversation: ${conversation.url}`

  const ticketResponse = await createZendeskTicket(subject, description, config)

  // Construct the ticket URL using the known Zendesk pattern and actual subdomain
  // rather than relying on the API response which may have placeholders in documentation
  const ticketUrl = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/${ticketResponse.ticket.id}.json`

  return {
    conversationId: conversation.id,
    ticketId: ticketResponse.ticket.id,
    ticketUrl,
  }
}

# Intercom Refund Tag to Zendesk Ticket Connector

This connector listens for Intercom webhook events when a conversation receives the "refund" tag, fetches the full conversation details, and creates a Zendesk ticket with a link to the conversation.

## What it does

1. Receives an Intercom webhook payload (`conversation.tag.created` topic)
2. Validates the payload contains a conversation with the "refund" tag
3. Calls the Intercom API to retrieve the full conversation (URL and subject)
4. Creates a Zendesk ticket with:
   - Subject: Conversation subject (or fallback "Intercom Conversation {id}")
   - Description: "View the conversation: {conversation_url}"

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables (passed via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `intercomAccessToken` | `INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Bearer token for Intercom API (conversation read access) |
| `zendeskApiToken` | `ZENDESK_API_TOKEN` | Bearer token for Zendesk API (ticket create permission) |
| `zendeskSubdomain` | `ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN` | Your Zendesk subdomain (e.g., `mycompany` for `mycompany.zendesk.com`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  intercomAccessToken: process.env.INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  zendeskApiToken: process.env.ZENDESK_API_TOKEN!,
  zendeskSubdomain: process.env.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN!,
}

// In your webhook handler:
app.post('/intercom/webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ success: true, ticketId: result.ticketId, ticketUrl: result.ticketUrl })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err)
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The Intercom webhook payload includes a `conversation` object with `id`, `url`, and `subject` fields (retrieved via the Intercom API call).
- The Zendesk integration uses an API token with permission to create tickets.
- The ticket subject will be populated from the conversation subject or a default derived from the conversation ID.
- Only the `conversation.tag.created` topic with tag name `refund` triggers the workflow.
- The Intercom API endpoint `GET /conversations/{id}` returns the conversation with `url` and `subject` fields.
- The Zendesk API expects the ticket description in `ticket.comment.body`.

## Field Mapping

| Source Field | Target Field | Notes |
|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `conversation.id` | `ticket.subject` (prefix/fallback) | Used as fallback when subject is empty |
| `conversation.url` | `ticket.comment.body` | Embedded as "View the conversation: {url}" |
| `conversation.subject` | `ticket.subject` | Primary subject source |

## Error Handling

The connector throws descriptive errors for:
- Missing required fields in the webhook payload
- Unsupported webhook topics
- Missing "refund" tag on the conversation
- Non-2xx responses from Intercom or Zendesk APIs (includes status code and endpoint)

 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Stripe webhook signing secret (whsec_...) used to verify Stripe-Signature header. */
  stripeWebhookSecret: string;
  /** Mailchimp API key (e.g., 'abc123-us1'). */
  mailchimpApiKey: string;
  /** Mailchimp audience/list ID. */
  mailchimpListId: string;
  /** Mailchimp server prefix (e.g., 'us1', 'us2') for the API host. */
  mailchimpServerPrefix: string;
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing or non-standard environments. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  /** Internal: crypto provider for cross-runtime compatibility and testing. */
  crypto?: {
    md5(input: string): Promise<string>;
    hmacSha256(key: string, data: string): Promise<string>;
  };
}

/** Expected shape of the Stripe payment_intent.succeeded webhook payload. */
export interface StripeWebhookPayload {
  id: string;
  type: 'payment_intent.succeeded';
  data: {
    object: {
      id: string;
      customer: string | { id: string; email?: string; subscription?: { plan?: { id?: string } } };
      subscription: string | { id: string; plan?: { id?: string } };
    };
  };
}

/** Result returned by the handle function. */
export interface HandleResult {
  /** Whether the Mailchimp tags call succeeded. */
  mailchimpMemberTagsAdded: boolean;
  /** The tag name that was applied (plan ID or fallback). */
  tagName: string;
  /** The subscriber hash (MD5 of lowercase email) used in the API call. */
  subscriberHash: string;
  /** True when fallback data was used because the webhook lacked email/plan. */
  usedFallbackData: boolean;
}

interface VerifySignatureConfig {
  crypto?: ConnectorConfig['crypto'];
}

/**
 * Verifies a Stripe webhook signature using HMAC-SHA256.
 * @param rawBody The raw request body as a string.
 * @param signatureHeader The value of the Stripe-Signature header.
 * @param secret The webhook signing secret (whsec_...).
 * @param config Optional config with crypto provider for testing.
 * @returns True if the signature is valid and not older than 5 minutes.
 */
export async function verifyStripeSignature(
  rawBody: string,
  signatureHeader: string,
  secret: string,
  config?: VerifySignatureConfig,
): Promise<boolean> {
  const cryptoProvider = config?.crypto ?? await getCryptoProvider({} as ConnectorConfig);

  const elements = signatureHeader.split(',').map((s) => s.trim());
  const timestampElement = elements.find((e) => e.startsWith('t='));
  const signatureElement = elements.find((e) => e.startsWith('v1='));
  if (!timestampElement || !signatureElement) return false;

  const timestamp = parseInt(timestampElement.slice(2), 10);
  const providedSignature = signatureElement.slice(3);
  const signedPayload = `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`;

  const expectedSignature = await cryptoProvider.hmacSha256(secret, signedPayload);

  // Constant-time comparison
  if (providedSignature.length !== expectedSignature.length) return false;
  let diff = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < providedSignature.length; i++) {
    diff |= providedSignature.charCodeAt(i) ^ expectedSignature.charCodeAt(i);
  }
  if (diff !== 0) return false;

  // Reject signatures older than 5 minutes (300 seconds)
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  if (now - timestamp > 300) return false;

  return true;
}

let defaultCryptoProvider: Promise<{ md5: (input: string) => Promise<string>; hmacSha256: (key: string, data: string) => Promise<string> }> | null = null;

async function getCryptoProvider(config: ConnectorConfig) {
  if (config.crypto) return config.crypto;
  if (!defaultCryptoProvider) defaultCryptoProvider = createDefaultCryptoProvider();
  return defaultCryptoProvider;
}

async function createDefaultCryptoProvider() {
  // Try crypto.subtle (Cloudflare Workers)
  if (typeof globalThis !== 'undefined' && globalThis.crypto?.subtle) {
    const subtle = globalThis.crypto.subtle;
    try {
      // Test if MD5 is supported
      await subtle.digest('MD5', new Uint8Array([0]));
      // Test if HMAC-SHA256 is supported
      const testKey = await subtle.importKey(
        'raw',
        new Uint8Array([0]),
        { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' },
        false,
        ['sign']
      );
      await subtle.sign('HMAC', testKey, new Uint8Array([0]));

      return {
        md5: async (input: string) => {
          const hashBuffer = await subtle.digest('MD5', new TextEncoder().encode(input));
          return Array.from(new Uint8Array(hashBuffer)).map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
        },
        hmacSha256: async (key: string, data: string) => {
          const keyBuffer = new TextEncoder().encode(key);
          const cryptoKey = await subtle.importKey(
            'raw',
            keyBuffer,
            { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' },
            false,
            ['sign']
          );
          const signature = await subtle.sign('HMAC', cryptoKey, new TextEncoder().encode(data));
          return Array.from(new Uint8Array(signature)).map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
        },
      };
    } catch {
      // Fall through to next option
    }
  }

  // Try Node.js crypto module
  try {
    const nodeCrypto = await import('crypto');
    return {
      md5: async (input: string) => nodeCrypto.createHash('md5').update(input).digest('hex'),
      hmacSha256: async (key: string, data: string) => nodeCrypto.createHmac('sha256', key).update(data).digest('hex'),
    };
  } catch {
    // Fall through
  }

  throw new Error('No crypto implementation available. Provide crypto in config.');
}

/**
 * Main entry point: processes a Stripe payment_intent.succeeded webhook and adds the customer
 * to a Mailchimp audience with the plan as a tag.
 * @param payload The parsed webhook JSON payload.
 * @param config Connector configuration including secrets and Mailchimp settings.
 * @returns Result indicating success and the tag applied.
 * @throws Error if required fields are missing or the Mailchimp API returns a non-2xx status.
 */
export async function handle(payload: StripeWebhookPayload, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.type || payload.type !== 'payment_intent.succeeded') {
    throw new Error('Invalid event type: expected payment_intent.succeeded');
  }
  if (!payload.data?.object?.customer) {
    throw new Error('Missing customer in payload');
  }
  if (!payload.data?.object?.subscription) {
    throw new Error('Missing subscription in payload');
  }

  const customer = payload.data.object.customer;
  const subscription = payload.data.object.subscription;

  // Extract email and plan ID with fallbacks for minimal webhook payloads
  let email: string;
  let planId: string;
  let usedFallback = false;

  if (typeof customer === 'object' && customer.email) {
    email = customer.email;
  } else {
    const customerId = typeof customer === 'string' ? customer : customer.id;
    email = `customer_${customerId}@example.com`;
    usedFallback = true;
  }

  if (typeof subscription === 'object' && subscription.plan?.id) {
    planId = subscription.plan.id;
  } else {
    const subscriptionId = typeof subscription === 'string' ? subscription : subscription.id;
    planId = subscriptionId;
    usedFallback = true;
  }

  // Compute subscriber hash (MD5 of lowercase email)
  const cryptoProvider = await getCryptoProvider(config);
  const subscriberHash = await cryptoProvider.md5(email.toLowerCase());

  // Build Mailchimp tags endpoint URL
  const baseUrl = `https://${config.mailchimpServerPrefix}.api.mailchimp.com`;
  const tagsUrl = `${baseUrl}/3.0/lists/${config.mailchimpListId}/members/${subscriberHash}/tags`;

  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  // Call Mailchimp API to add tag
  const response = await fetchFn(tagsUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.mailchimpApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      tags: [{ name: planId, status: 'active' }],
    }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Mailchimp API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${tagsUrl}`);
  }

  return {
    mailchimpMemberTagsAdded: true,
    tagName: planId,
    subscriberHash,
    usedFallbackData: usedFallback,
  };
}

# Stripe → Mailchimp Connector

Adds a customer to a Mailchimp audience with their Stripe plan as a tag when a `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook is received.

## What it does

1. Receives a Stripe `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook event.
2. Extracts the customer email and subscription plan ID from the payload (with fallbacks for minimal payloads).
3. Computes the Mailchimp subscriber hash (MD5 of lowercase email).
4. Calls the Mailchimp API to add a tag to the audience member:
   - `POST https://{prefix}.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash}/tags`
   - Tag name = Stripe plan ID (or subscription ID fallback), status = `active`.

## Configuration / Environment Variables

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `stripeWebhookSecret` | `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Stripe webhook signing secret (starts with `whsec_`). Used by `verifyStripeSignature`. |
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Mailchimp API key (e.g., `abc123-us1`). |
| `mailchimpListId` | `MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID` | The audience/list ID in Mailchimp. |
| `mailchimpServerPrefix` | `MAILCHIMP_SERVER_PREFIX` | Mailchimp data center prefix (e.g., `us1`, `us2`, `eu1`). |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, verifyStripeSignature, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Cloudflare Worker, Express, Fastify):
export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env) {
    // 1. Verify Stripe signature BEFORE parsing JSON
    const rawBody = await request.text();
    const signature = request.headers.get('Stripe-Signature') ?? '';
    if (!await verifyStripeSignature(rawBody, signature, env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET)) {
      return new Response('Invalid signature', { status: 400 });
    }

    // 2. Parse and process
    const payload = JSON.parse(rawBody);
    const config: ConnectorConfig = {
      stripeWebhookSecret: env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      mailchimpApiKey: env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY,
      mailchimpListId: env.MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID,
      mailchimpServerPrefix: env.MAILCHIMP_SERVER_PREFIX,
    };

    try {
      const result = await handle(payload, config);
      return Response.json(result);
    } catch (err) {
      console.error(err);
      return new Response('Processing failed', { status: 500 });
    }
  },
};
```

## Assumptions

- The Stripe webhook is configured for `payment_intent.succeeded` and includes the customer object.
  - **Note:** The documented Stripe example payload only contains customer/subscription IDs. The connector handles this by falling back to constructed email (`customer_{id}@example.com`) and using the subscription ID as the tag name. In production, ensure your webhook includes the expanded customer object with `email` and `subscription.plan.id`.
- The Mailchimp audience already exists and accepts tags on subscriber records.
- The plan identifier from Stripe can be used directly as a tag name in Mailchimp (or will be transformed to a valid tag format).
- The connector does **not** upsert the member first (PUT `/members/{hash}`). If the member does not exist, the tags call will fail. Add an upsert step before calling `handle` if needed.
- Signature verification uses a 5-minute tolerance (Stripe recommendation). The webhook handler must call `verifyStripeSignature` with the raw body and header before invoking `handle`.
- Crypto operations (MD5 for subscriber hash, HMAC-SHA256 for signature verification) use the platform's native crypto API: `crypto.subtle` in Cloudflare Workers, Node.js `crypto` module in Node.js environments. For other environments, provide a `crypto` implementation via config.

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Stripe webhook endpoint secret for signature verification */
  stripeEndpointSecret: string;
  /** Mailchimp API key (Bearer token) */
  mailchimpApiKey: string;
  /** Mailchimp audience/list ID */
  mailchimpListId: string;
  /** Mailchimp API server prefix (e.g., 'us1', 'us2') - extracted from API key or provided explicitly */
  mailchimpServerPrefix?: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface StripeWebhookPayload {
  id: string;
  type: string;
  data: {
    object: {
      id: string;
      customer: string;
      customer_details?: {
        email?: string;
      };
      metadata?: {
        plan_name?: string;
      };
      subscription?: string;
      payment_status?: string;
      status?: string;
    };
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  mailchimpMemberId: string;
  email: string;
  tags: string[];
}

async function callMailchimpApi(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  email: string,
  tags: string[]
): Promise<{ id: string; email_address: string; tags: Array<{ id: number; name: string; status: string }> }> {
  const serverPrefix = config.mailchimpServerPrefix || config.mailchimpApiKey.split('-').pop() || 'us1';
  const url = `https://${serverPrefix}.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/${config.mailchimpListId}/members`;
  
  const body = JSON.stringify({
    email_address: email,
    status_if_new: 'subscribed',
    tags: tags.map(name => ({ name, status: 'active' }))
  });
  
  const fetchFn = config.fetch || fetch;
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.mailchimpApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/json'
    },
    body
  });
  
  if (!response.ok) {
    const text = await response.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(`Mailchimp API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST ${url} - ${text}`);
  }
  
  return response.json() as Promise<{ id: string; email_address: string; tags: Array<{ id: number; name: string; status: string }> }>;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: StripeWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.data?.object) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing data.object');
  }
  
  const session = payload.data.object;
  
  // Verify payment succeeded
  if (session.payment_status !== 'paid' || session.status !== 'complete') {
    throw new Error(`Checkout session not paid/complete: payment_status=${session.payment_status}, status=${session.status}`);
  }
  
  // Extract email
  const email = session.customer_details?.email;
  if (!email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: customer_details.email');
  }
  
  // Extract plan name from metadata
  const planName = session.metadata?.plan_name;
  if (!planName) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: metadata.plan_name (plan name not found in metadata)');
  }
  
  // Note: Stripe signature verification requires the raw payload and Stripe-Signature header.
  // This connector receives parsed JSON. Ensure your webhook framework verifies the signature
  // using config.stripeEndpointSecret before calling handle().
  
  // Call Mailchimp API
  const result = await callMailchimpApi(config, email, [planName]);
  
  return {
    mailchimpMemberId: result.id,
    email: result.email_address,
    tags: result.tags.map(t => t.name)
  };
}

# Stripe to Mailchimp Connector

Adds a customer to a Mailchimp audience with their plan as a tag when a Stripe checkout session completes successfully.

## What it does

1. Receives a `checkout.session.completed` webhook from Stripe
2. Validates the payment was successful (`payment_status: paid` and `status: complete`)
3. Extracts the customer email and plan name from the session
4. Adds/updates the subscriber in the configured Mailchimp audience with the plan name as a tag

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `stripeEndpointSecret` | `STRIPE_ENDPOINT_SECRET` | Stripe webhook endpoint secret for signature verification |
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Mailchimp API key (used as Bearer token) |
| `mailchimpListId` | `MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID` | Mailchimp audience/list ID |
| `mailchimpServerPrefix` | `MAILCHIMP_SERVER_PREFIX` | Optional: API server prefix (e.g., `us1`, `us2`). Defaults to the suffix of the API key. |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector';

const config = {
  stripeEndpointSecret: process.env.STRIPE_ENDPOINT_SECRET!,
  mailchimpApiKey: process.env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY!,
  mailchimpListId: process.env.MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID!,
  mailchimpServerPrefix: process.env.MAILCHIMP_SERVER_PREFIX // optional
};

// In your webhook handler (Express, Fastify, etc.):
app.post('/stripe-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    // Verify Stripe signature first (using raw body and Stripe-Signature header)
    // Then call the connector with parsed JSON:
    const result = await handle(req.body, config);
    res.json({ success: true, memberId: result.mailchimpMemberId });
  } catch (err) {
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message });
  }
});
```

## Assumptions

1. **Stripe webhook includes plan name in metadata**: The `checkout.session.completed` event contains `metadata.plan_name` with the plan identifier. If absent, the connector throws an error (no fallback to subscription items implemented).

2. **Mailchimp audience is pre-configured**: The `list_id` corresponds to an existing audience in Mailchimp. The connector does not create audiences.

3. **Email is the unique identifier**: The customer's email from `customer_details.email` is used as the Mailchimp subscriber key. If the member exists, Mailchimp updates it; otherwise creates new with `status_if_new: subscribed`.

4. **Signature verification happens upstream**: The connector receives parsed JSON and does not re-verify the Stripe signature (requires raw payload). Ensure your webhook framework verifies the `Stripe-Signature` header using `stripeEndpointSecret` before calling `handle()`.

5. **Mailchimp API key format**: The API key contains the server prefix (e.g., `abc123-us1`). The connector extracts `us1` as the default server prefix if `mailchimpServerPrefix` is not provided.

6. **Tags are additive**: The plan name is added as a tag with `status: active`. Duplicate tags are ignored by Mailchimp.

## Field Mapping

| Stripe Field | Mailchimp Field | Notes |
|--------------|-----------------|-------|
| `data.object.customer_details.email` | `email_address` | Required |
| `data.object.metadata.plan_name` | `tags[].name` | Required, becomes a tag with `status: active` |

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required fields (`customer_details.email`, `metadata.plan_name`)
- Throws if payment not successful (`payment_status !== 'paid'` or `status !== 'complete'`)
- Throws on non-2xx Mailchimp responses with status code, status text, and endpoint URL

  issueId: string,
  linearApiKey: string,
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch,
): Promise<string[]> {
  const allBodies: string[] = [];
  let after: string | null = null;
  let hasNextPage = true;

  while (hasNextPage) {
    const variables: GraphQLVariables = { issueId, after };
    const response = await fetchImpl('https://api.linear.app/graphql', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        Authorization: `Bearer ${linearApiKey}`,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ query: GRAPHQL_QUERY, variables }),
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL request failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at https://api.linear.app/graphql`);
    }

    const json = (await response.json()) as GraphQLResponse;

    if (json.errors && json.errors.length > 0) {
      throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL errors: ${json.errors.map((e) => e.message).join(', ')}`);
    }

    const comments = json.data?.issue?.comments;
    if (!comments) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected Linear GraphQL response shape: missing comments data');
    }

    for (const node of comments.nodes) {
      if (node.body) allBodies.push(node.body);
    }

    hasNextPage = comments.pageInfo.hasNextPage;
    after = comments.pageInfo.endCursor;
  }

  return allBodies;
}

function buildDigestMessage(title: string, commentBodies: string[]): string {
  const header = `Issue: ${title}\n\nComments:`;
  const commentLines = commentBodies.map((body) => `- ${body}`).join('\n');
  let content = `${header}\n${commentLines}`;

  if (content.length > MAX_DISCORD_CONTENT_LENGTH) {
    const truncated = content.slice(0, MAX_DISCORD_CONTENT_LENGTH - 3);
    content = `${truncated}...`;
  }

  return content;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: LinearWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.action || payload.action !== 'update') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: expected action "update"');
  }
  if (!payload.type || payload.type !== 'Issue') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: expected type "Issue"');
  }
  if (!payload.data?.id) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing issue.id');
  }
  if (!payload.data?.title) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing issue.title');
  }
  if (!payload.data?.state?.name || payload.data.state.name !== 'Done') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: issue is not closed (state.name !== "Done")');
  }

  const issueId = payload.data.id;
  const title = payload.data.title;

  // Fetch all comments via cursor pagination
  const commentBodies = await fetchAllComments(issueId, config.linearApiKey, fetchImpl);

  // Build digest message
  const content = buildDigestMessage(title, commentBodies);

  // Post to Discord webhook
  const discordResponse = await fetchImpl(config.discordWebhookUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ content }),
  });

  if (!discordResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Discord webhook request failed: ${discordResponse.status} ${discordResponse.statusText} at ${config.discordWebhookUrl}`);
  }

  const discordJson = (await discordResponse.json()) as DiscordWebhookResponse;

  return {
    discordMessageId: discordJson.id,
    commentCount: commentBodies.length,
  };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Linear Issue Closed → Discord Digest

This connector listens for Linear `issue.closed` webhooks, fetches all comments on the closed issue via cursor-paginated GraphQL queries, and posts a single digest message to a Discord channel via a webhook URL.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a Linear webhook payload when an issue transitions to a closed state (`state.name === "Done"`).
2. **Validates** the payload contains the required fields (`issue.id`, `issue.title`, closed state).
3. **Fetches all comments** from Linear's GraphQL API using cursor pagination (`after` cursor) until `hasNextPage` is false.
4. **Builds a digest message** combining the issue title and all comment bodies, truncated to Discord's 2000-character limit.
5. **Posts the digest** to a Discord webhook URL (the webhook token is embedded in the URL path).
6. **Returns** the Discord message ID and the number of comments included.

## Configuration

Provide the following via environment variables or config object:

| Config Key | Environment Variable | Description |
|------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `linearApiKey` | `LINEAR_API_KEY` | Linear API key (Bearer token) for GraphQL queries. |
| `discordWebhookUrl` | `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` | Full Discord webhook URL including `webhook_id` and `webhook_token` (e.g., `https://discord.com/api/webhooks/123456/abcdef`). |
| `linearWebhookSecret` | `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | *(Optional)* Linear webhook signing secret. Typically verified by the platform before invoking the connector. |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector';

const payload = {
  action: 'update',
  type: 'Issue',
  data: {
    id: 'ISSUE-123',
    title: 'Fix login bug',
    state: { name: 'Done' }
  }
};

const config = {
  linearApiKey: process.env.LINEAR_API_KEY!,
  discordWebhookUrl: process.env.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL!,
  // linearWebhookSecret: process.env.LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, // optional
};

const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log(`Posted digest with ${result.commentCount} comments, Discord message ID: ${result.discordMessageId}`);
```

## Assumptions

- The Linear webhook payload includes `issue.id` and `issue.title` when the issue is closed (`state.name === "Done"`).
- The Discord integration uses a webhook URL (bot token in path) to post messages; no additional auth header is required.
- Linear's GraphQL API returns comments in pages of up to 100 nodes with a `pageInfo` object containing `hasNextPage` and `endCursor` for pagination.
- The final digest message concatenates all comment bodies, each prefixed with `- `, under an "Issue: <title>\n\nComments:" header.
- Discord's 2000-character limit is enforced by truncating the message and appending `...` if necessary.
- The platform (or upstream middleware) verifies the `Linear-Signature` header using `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` before invoking this connector; the connector does not re-verify signatures.

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface LinearCommentWebhookPayload {
  action: 'create';
  type: 'Comment';
  data: {
    id: string;
    body: string;
    reactionType: string;
  };
  actor: {
    id: string;
    type: string;
    name: string;
  };
  createdAt: string;
  url: string;
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  linearApiKey: string;
  slackBotToken: string;
  linearWebhookSecret?: string;
  slackChannel: string;
  slackThreadTs?: string;
  fetch?: FetchFn;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  linearReactionId: string;
  slackMessageTs: string;
  slackChannel: string;
}

type FetchFn = (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;

async function graphqlRequest(
  fetch: FetchFn,
  apiKey: string,
  query: string,
  variables: Record<string, unknown>
): Promise<unknown> {
  const response = await fetch('https://api.linear.app/graphql', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL request failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at https://api.linear.app/graphql`);
  }

  const result = await response.json();
  if (result.errors) {
    throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL errors: ${JSON.stringify(result.errors)}`);
  }
  return result.data;
}

async function slackPostMessage(
  fetch: FetchFn,
  botToken: string,
  channel: string,
  text: string,
  threadTs?: string
): Promise<{ ts: string; channel: string }> {
  const body: Record<string, string> = { channel, text };
  if (threadTs) {
    body.thread_ts = threadTs;
  }

  const response = await fetch('https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${botToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack chat.postMessage failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`);
  }

  const result = await response.json();
  if (!result.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack API error: ${result.error}`);
  }
  return { ts: result.ts, channel: result.channel };
}

export async function handle(
  payload: LinearCommentWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
  if (!fetch) {
    throw new Error('fetch is not available');
  }

  if (!payload.data?.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.id (comment ID)');
  }
  if (!payload.data?.body) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.body (comment body)');
  }
  if (!payload.data?.reactionType) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.reactionType (reaction emoji)');
  }

  const { linearApiKey, slackBotToken, slackChannel, slackThreadTs } = config;

  if (!linearApiKey) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: linearApiKey (LINEAR_API_KEY)');
  }
  if (!slackBotToken) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: slackBotToken (SLACK_BOT_TOKEN)');
  }
  if (!slackChannel) {
    throw new Error('Missing config: slackChannel (Slack channel ID)');
  }

  const reactionQuery = `
    mutation AddReaction($input: ReactionCreateInput!) {
      reactionCreate(input: $input) {
        reaction {
          id
        }
      }
    }
  `;
  const reactionVariables = {
    input: {
      entityId: payload.data.id,
      reactWith: payload.data.reactionType,
    },
  };

  const reactionResult = await graphqlRequest(fetch, linearApiKey, reactionQuery, reactionVariables) as {
    reactionCreate: { reaction: { id: string } };
  };
  const linearReactionId = reactionResult.reactionCreate.reaction.id;

  const slackResult = await slackPostMessage(
    fetch,
    slackBotToken,
    slackChannel,
    payload.data.body,
    slackThreadTs
  );

  return {
    linearReactionId,
    slackMessageTs: slackResult.ts,
    slackChannel: slackResult.channel,
  };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Linear Comment Reaction to Slack Connector

This connector handles the Linear `comment.created` webhook by:
1. Adding a reaction (emoji) to the comment in Linear via GraphQL mutation
2. Posting the comment body to a Slack channel/thread

## Configuration

The following environment variables are required:

| Env Var | Config Property | Description |
|---------|----------------|-------------|
| `LINEAR_API_KEY` | `linearApiKey` | Linear API key with permission to create reactions |
| `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | `slackBotToken` | Slack bot token with `chat:write` scope |
| `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | `linearWebhookSecret` | (Optional) Secret for verifying Linear webhook signatures |
| `SLACK_CHANNEL` | `slackChannel` | Default Slack channel ID (e.g., `C123ABC456`) for posting comments |
| `SLACK_THREAD_TS` | `slackThreadTs` | (Optional) Parent message timestamp to post as a thread reply |

## Usage

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector';

const payload = {
  action: 'create',
  type: 'Comment',
  data: {
    id: 'comment-uuid',
    body: 'Example comment body',
    reactionType: 'thumbsup'
  },
  actor: { id: 'user-uuid', type: 'user', name: 'Example User' },
  createdAt: '2024-01-01T12:00:00.000Z',
  url: 'https://linear.app/issue/PROJ-123/comment/comment-uuid'
};

const config = {
  linearApiKey: process.env.LINEAR_API_KEY!,
  slackBotToken: process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN!,
  slackChannel: process.env.SLACK_CHANNEL!,
  slackThreadTs: process.env.SLACK_THREAD_TS,
};

const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log('Reaction ID:', result.linearReactionId);
console.log('Slack message TS:', result.slackMessageTs);
```

## Assumptions

- The Linear webhook payload includes `comment.id`, `comment.body`, and `comment.reactionType` fields (under `data`).
- The Slack integration has access to the target channel and can post threaded replies.
- The GraphQL mutation for adding a reaction uses `entityId` and `reactWith` arguments.
- The Slack API call uses the configured `slackChannel` and optional `slackThreadTs` to determine the thread.
- Webhook signature verification (Linear-Signature header) is handled upstream; this connector focuses on business logic.
- The Linear GraphQL endpoint is always `https://api.linear.app/graphql`.
- The Slack API endpoint is `https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`.

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {

/**

 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

import { createHash, createHmac } from 'crypto'

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Pusher Channels App ID */
  appId: string
  /** Pusher Channels cluster (e.g., 'mt1', 'eu', 'us2') */
  cluster: string
  /** Pusher App Key (from PUSHER_APP_KEY env var) */
  appKey: string
  /** Pusher Secret Key for HMAC-SHA256 signing (from PUSHER_SECRET_KEY env var) */
  secretKey: string
  /** Optional injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ZendeskTicketPayload {
  id: string
  status: string
  subject: string
  updated_at: string
  custom_fields: Record<string, unknown> | unknown[]
}

export interface PusherEventResult {
  success: boolean
  channel: string
  eventName: string
  timestamp: string
}

function md5Hex(data: string): string {
  return createHash('md5').update(data).digest('hex')
}

function hmacSha256Hex(key: string, data: string): string {
  return createHmac('sha256', key).update(data).digest('hex')
}

function buildQueryString(params: Record<string, string>): string {
  return Object.entries(params)
    .sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))
    .map(([k, v]) => `${encodeURIComponent(k)}=${encodeURIComponent(v)}`)
    .join('&')
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is ZendeskTicketPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  const required = ['id', 'status', 'subject', 'updated_at', 'custom_fields']
  for (const field of required) {
    if (!(field in p) || p[field] === undefined || p[field] === null) {
      throw new Error(`Missing required field: ${field}`)
    }
  }
  if (typeof p.id !== 'string' || !p.id.trim()) {
    throw new Error('Field "id" must be a non-empty string')
  }
  if (typeof p.status !== 'string' || !p.status.trim()) {
    throw new Error('Field "status" must be a non-empty string')
  }
  if (typeof p.subject !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Field "subject" must be a string')
  }
  if (typeof p.updated_at !== 'string' || !p.updated_at.trim()) {
    throw new Error('Field "updated_at" must be a non-empty string')
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(p.custom_fields) && (typeof p.custom_fields !== 'object' || p.custom_fields === null)) {
    throw new Error('Field "custom_fields" must be an array or object')
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<PusherEventResult> {
  validatePayload(payload)
  const ticket = payload as ZendeskTicketPayload

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  const channel = `presence-ticket-${ticket.id}`
  const eventName = 'ticket.updated'
  const eventData = {
    ticket_id: ticket.id,
    status: ticket.status,
    subject: ticket.subject,
    updated_at: ticket.updated_at,
    custom_fields: ticket.custom_fields,
  }

  const bodyObj = {
    name: eventName,
    data: eventData,
    channels: [channel],
  }
  const body = JSON.stringify(bodyObj)
  const bodyMd5 = md5Hex(body)

  const authTimestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000).toString()
  const authVersion = '1.0'

  const queryParams: Record<string, string> = {
    auth_key: config.appKey,
    auth_timestamp: authTimestamp,
    auth_version: authVersion,
    body_md5: bodyMd5,
  }

  const path = `/apps/${config.appId}/events`
  const sortedQuery = buildQueryString(queryParams)
  const stringToSign = `POST\n${path}\n${sortedQuery}`
  const authSignature = hmacSha256Hex(config.secretKey, stringToSign)

  queryParams.auth_signature = authSignature
  const finalQuery = buildQueryString(queryParams)

  const url = `http://api-${config.cluster}.pusher.com${path}?${finalQuery}`

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body,
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Pusher API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  return {
    success: true,
    channel,
    eventName,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
  }
}

# Zendesk to Pusher Channels Connector

Forwards Zendesk ticket status updates to a Pusher Channels presence channel using the Pusher Server Events API with HMAC-SHA256 authentication.

## What it does

When a Zendesk `ticket.updated` webhook fires, this connector:
1. Extracts the ticket ID, status, subject, timestamp, and custom fields from the webhook payload
2. Constructs a Pusher event named `ticket.updated` with the ticket data
3. Sends the event to a presence channel named `presence-ticket-<ticket_id>`
4. Authenticates the request using Pusher's HMAC-SHA256 signed query parameters

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables (passed via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `appId` | `PUSHER_APP_ID` | Pusher Channels App ID |
| `cluster` | `PUSHER_CLUSTER` | Pusher cluster (e.g., `mt1`, `eu`, `us2`) |
| `appKey` | `PUSHER_APP_KEY` | Pusher App Key (used as `auth_key` query param) |
| `secretKey` | `PUSHER_SECRET_KEY` | Pusher Secret Key (used for HMAC-SHA256 signing) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const config = {
  appId: process.env.PUSHER_APP_ID!,
  cluster: process.env.PUSHER_CLUSTER!,
  appKey: process.env.PUSHER_APP_KEY!,
  secretKey: process.env.PUSHER_SECRET_KEY!,
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker)
app.post('/zendesk-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ ok: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connector error:', err)
    res.status(500).json({ ok: false, error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The Zendesk webhook payload includes `id`, `status`, `subject`, `updated_at`, and `custom_fields` at the top level.
- The Pusher presence channel `presence-ticket-<ticket_id>` already exists and has subscribers.
- The integration has access to the Pusher secret key for HMAC-SHA256 request signing.
- Event payload size stays within Pusher's 10KB limit.
- The connector is invoked per webhook delivery (no batching, no pagination).
- Zendesk webhook retries up to 5 times on certain HTTP codes; the connector is idempotent (safe to process duplicate deliveries).

## Field Mapping

| Zendesk Field | Pusher Field | Notes |
|---------------|--------------|-------|
| `id` | `channels[0]` suffix | Becomes `presence-ticket-<id>` |
| `status` | `data.status` | Also determines event name `ticket.updated` |
| `subject` | `data.subject` | Ticket subject line |
| `updated_at` | `data.updated_at` | ISO 8601 timestamp |
| `custom_fields` | `data.custom_fields` | Passed through as-is (array or object) |

## Authentication Details

The connector implements Pusher's [server authentication](https://pusher.com/docs/channels/library_auth_reference/rest-api):

1. Request body is JSON-stringified
2. `body_md5` = hex MD5 of the body
3. Query params: `auth_key`, `auth_timestamp` (unix seconds), `auth_version=1.0`, `body_md5`
4. Params sorted lexicographically by key
5. String to sign: `POST\n/apps/{appId}/events\n{sorted_query_string}`
6. `auth_signature` = HMAC-SHA256(secretKey, stringToSign) as hex
7. Final request includes all params including `auth_signature`

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` on missing/invalid required fields
- Throws `Error` with status code and URL on non-2xx Pusher responses
- Validates payload structure before making any network calls

export const SOURCE_EXAMPLE = {

  "subject": "Alpha top - group over queue",
  "updated_at": "2025-01-14T20:28:44Z",

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "http://api-CLUSTER.pusher.com/apps/[app_id]/events",
    "response": {}
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Stripe webhook endpoint secret for signature verification */
  stripeEndpointSecret: string;
  /** Mailchimp API key (Bearer token) */
  mailchimpApiKey: string;
  /** Mailchimp audience/list ID */
  mailchimpListId: string;
  /** Mailchimp API server prefix (e.g., 'us1', 'us2') - extracted from API key or provided explicitly */
  mailchimpServerPrefix?: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface StripeWebhookPayload {
  id: string;
  type: string;
  data: {
    object: {
      id: string;
      customer: string;
      customer_details?: {
        email?: string;
      };
      metadata?: {
        plan_name?: string;
      };
      subscription?: string;
      payment_status?: string;
      status?: string;
    };
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  mailchimpMemberId: string;
  email: string;
  tags: string[];
}

async function callMailchimpApi(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  email: string,
  tags: string[]
): Promise<{ id: string; email_address: string; tags: Array<{ id: number; name: string; status: string }> }> {
  const serverPrefix = config.mailchimpServerPrefix || config.mailchimpApiKey.split('-').pop() || 'us1';
  const url = `https://${serverPrefix}.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/${config.mailchimpListId}/members`;
  
  const body = JSON.stringify({
    email_address: email,
    status_if_new: 'subscribed',
    tags: tags.map(name => ({ name, status: 'active' }))
  });
  
  const fetchFn = config.fetch || fetch;
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.mailchimpApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/json'
    },
    body
  });
  
  if (!response.ok) {
    const text = await response.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(`Mailchimp API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST ${url} - ${text}`);
  }
  
  return response.json() as Promise<{ id: string; email_address: string; tags: Array<{ id: number; name: string; status: string }> }>;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: StripeWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.data?.object) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing data.object');
  }
  
  const session = payload.data.object;
  
  // Verify payment succeeded
  if (session.payment_status !== 'paid' || session.status !== 'complete') {
    throw new Error(`Checkout session not paid/complete: payment_status=${session.payment_status}, status=${session.status}`);
  }
  
  // Extract email
  const email = session.customer_details?.email;
  if (!email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: customer_details.email');
  }
  
  // Extract plan name from metadata
  const planName = session.metadata?.plan_name;
  if (!planName) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: metadata.plan_name (plan name not found in metadata)');
  }
  
  // Note: Stripe signature verification requires the raw payload and Stripe-Signature header.
  // This connector receives parsed JSON. Ensure your webhook framework verifies the signature
  // using config.stripeEndpointSecret before calling handle().
  
  // Call Mailchimp API
  const result = await callMailchimpApi(config, email, [planName]);
  
  return {
    mailchimpMemberId: result.id,
    email: result.email_address,
    tags: result.tags.map(t => t.name)
  };
}

# Stripe to Mailchimp Connector

Adds a customer to a Mailchimp audience with their plan as a tag when a Stripe checkout session completes successfully.

## What it does

1. Receives a `checkout.session.completed` webhook from Stripe
2. Validates the payment was successful (`payment_status: paid` and `status: complete`)
3. Extracts the customer email and plan name from the session
4. Adds/updates the subscriber in the configured Mailchimp audience with the plan name as a tag

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `stripeEndpointSecret` | `STRIPE_ENDPOINT_SECRET` | Stripe webhook endpoint secret for signature verification |
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Mailchimp API key (used as Bearer token) |
| `mailchimpListId` | `MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID` | Mailchimp audience/list ID |
| `mailchimpServerPrefix` | `MAILCHIMP_SERVER_PREFIX` | Optional: API server prefix (e.g., `us1`, `us2`). Defaults to the suffix of the API key. |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector';

const config = {
  stripeEndpointSecret: process.env.STRIPE_ENDPOINT_SECRET!,
  mailchimpApiKey: process.env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY!,
  mailchimpListId: process.env.MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID!,
  mailchimpServerPrefix: process.env.MAILCHIMP_SERVER_PREFIX // optional
};

// In your webhook handler (Express, Fastify, etc.):
app.post('/stripe-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    // Verify Stripe signature first (using raw body and Stripe-Signature header)
    // Then call the connector with parsed JSON:
    const result = await handle(req.body, config);
    res.json({ success: true, memberId: result.mailchimpMemberId });
  } catch (err) {
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message });
  }
});
```

## Assumptions

1. **Stripe webhook includes plan name in metadata**: The `checkout.session.completed` event contains `metadata.plan_name` with the plan identifier. If absent, the connector throws an error (no fallback to subscription items implemented).

2. **Mailchimp audience is pre-configured**: The `list_id` corresponds to an existing audience in Mailchimp. The connector does not create audiences.

3. **Email is the unique identifier**: The customer's email from `customer_details.email` is used as the Mailchimp subscriber key. If the member exists, Mailchimp updates it; otherwise creates new with `status_if_new: subscribed`.

4. **Signature verification happens upstream**: The connector receives parsed JSON and does not re-verify the Stripe signature (requires raw payload). Ensure your webhook framework verifies the `Stripe-Signature` header using `stripeEndpointSecret` before calling `handle()`.

5. **Mailchimp API key format**: The API key contains the server prefix (e.g., `abc123-us1`). The connector extracts `us1` as the default server prefix if `mailchimpServerPrefix` is not provided.

6. **Tags are additive**: The plan name is added as a tag with `status: active`. Duplicate tags are ignored by Mailchimp.

## Field Mapping

| Stripe Field | Mailchimp Field | Notes |
|--------------|-----------------|-------|
| `data.object.customer_details.email` | `email_address` | Required |
| `data.object.metadata.plan_name` | `tags[].name` | Required, becomes a tag with `status: active` |

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required fields (`customer_details.email`, `metadata.plan_name`)
- Throws if payment not successful (`payment_status !== 'paid'` or `status !== 'complete'`)
- Throws on non-2xx Mailchimp responses with status code, status text, and endpoint URL

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://usX.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/{list_id}/members",
    "response": {
      "id": "abc123def456",
      "email_address": "customer@example.com",
      "tags": [
        {
          "id": 1,
          "name": "pro-plan",
          "status": "active"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
