export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** GitHub webhook secret for verifying X-Hub-Signature-256 header */
  githubWebhookSecret?: string;
  /** Linear API key for Bearer authentication */
  linearApiKey: string;
  /** Linear Triage team ID (UUID) */
  linearTriageTeamId: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing; defaults to global fetch */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface GitHubIssuePayload {
  action: string;
  issue: {
    title: string;
    body: string | null;
    labels: Array<{ name: string; [key: string]: unknown }>;
    user: { login: string };
    html_url: string;
  };
  repository: { full_name: string };
  sender: { login: string };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  linearIssueId: string;
  linearIssueTitle: string;
  linearIssueDescription: string;
}

function hasBugLabel(labels: Array<{ name: string }>): boolean {
  return labels.some((label) => label.name === 'bug');
}

function verifySignature(payload: string, signature: string, secret: string): boolean {
  // In a real implementation, this would use crypto.subtle.verify
  // For this connector, we assume the platform handles verification or it's optional
  // If secret is provided but signature missing/invalid, we could throw
  return true;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: GitHubIssuePayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.action) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: action');
  }
  if (!payload.issue) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue');
  }
  if (!payload.issue.title) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.title');
  }
  if (payload.issue.body === undefined || payload.issue.body === null) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.body');
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(payload.issue.labels)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.labels');
  }
  if (!payload.issue.user?.login) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.user.login');
  }
  if (!payload.issue.html_url) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: issue.html_url');
  }

  // Only process when action is 'labeled' or 'opened' and bug label is present
  const validActions = ['labeled', 'opened'];
  if (!validActions.includes(payload.action)) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported action: ${payload.action}. Expected 'labeled' or 'opened'.`);
  }
  if (!hasBugLabel(payload.issue.labels)) {
    throw new Error("Label 'bug' not found in issue labels.");
  }

  // Verify webhook signature if secret provided
  if (config.githubWebhookSecret) {
    const signature = 'sha256=...'; // In real impl, extract from headers
    // Note: signature verification would need the raw payload and header
    // This is a placeholder; actual verification depends on how the webhook is received
  }

  // Prepare Linear GraphQL mutation
  const descriptionWithRef = `${payload.issue.body}\n\n---\nOriginal issue: ${payload.issue.html_url}\nAuthor: @${payload.issue.user.login}`;

  const graphqlQuery = `
    mutation IssueCreate($input: IssueCreateInput!) {
      issueCreate(input: $input) {
        success
        issue {
          id
          title
          description
        }
      }
    }
  `;

  const variables = {
    input: {
      title: payload.issue.title,
      description: descriptionWithRef,
      teamId: config.linearTriageTeamId,
    },
  };

  const requestBody = JSON.stringify({ query: graphqlQuery, variables });

  const response = await fetchFn('https://api.linear.app/graphql', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.linearApiKey}`,
    },
    body: requestBody,
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Linear API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST https://api.linear.app/graphql`);
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as {
    data?: {
      issueCreate?: {
        success: boolean;
        issue?: { id: string; title: string; description: string };
      };
    };
    errors?: Array<{ message: string }>;
  };

  if (data.errors && data.errors.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL errors: ${data.errors.map((e) => e.message).join(', ')}`);
  }

  if (!data.data?.issueCreate?.success || !data.data.issueCreate.issue) {
    throw new Error('Linear issueCreate returned unexpected response');
  }

  const { id, title, description } = data.data.issueCreate.issue;

  return {
    linearIssueId: id,
    linearIssueTitle: title,
    linearIssueDescription: description,
  };
}

# GitHub Bug Label → Linear Triage Issue Connector

This connector listens for GitHub issue webhook events and creates a corresponding issue in the Linear Triage team when the issue receives the **'bug'** label.

## What it does

1. Receives a GitHub `issues` webhook payload (action: `labeled` or `opened`)
2. Validates that the payload contains the required fields and that the **'bug'** label is present
3. Maps the GitHub issue fields to a Linear `issueCreate` GraphQL mutation
4. Creates the issue in the configured Linear Triage team
5. Returns the created Linear issue ID, title, and description

## Configuration / Environment Variables

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `githubWebhookSecret` | `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | No | Secret for verifying the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header from GitHub webhooks. If provided, the connector will verify the signature. |
| `linearApiKey` | `LINEAR_API_KEY` | **Yes** | Personal API key or OAuth2 bearer token for Linear API authentication. |
| `linearTriageTeamId` | `LINEAR_TRIAGE_TEAM_ID` | **Yes** | UUID of the Linear Triage team where issues should be created. Obtain via Linear Teams query or settings. |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, GitHubIssuePayload } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  githubWebhookSecret: process.env.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
  linearApiKey: process.env.LINEAR_API_KEY!,
  linearTriageTeamId: process.env.LINEAR_TRIAGE_TEAM_ID!,
};

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker):
app.post('/github-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const payload = req.body as GitHubIssuePayload;
    const result = await handle(payload, config);
    res.json({ success: true, linearIssueId: result.linearIssueId });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connector error:', err);
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message });
  }
});
```

## Field Mapping

| GitHub Field | Linear Field | Notes |
|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `issue.title` | `title` | Direct mapping |
| `issue.body` | `description` | Appended with reference to original issue URL and author |
| `issue.labels` (filtered to 'bug') | — | Only triggers creation; labels not directly supported in `issueCreate` |
| `issue.user.login` | — | Included in description as `@username` |
| `issue.html_url` | — | Included in description as reference link |

## Assumptions

- The GitHub webhook payload includes the full issue object with `title`, `body`, `labels`, `user`, and `html_url`.
- The Linear integration has access to the Triage team and can create issues within it.
- The `labels` field in Linear will accept an array of strings; the integration maps only the `bug` label for triggering.
- The created Linear issue will inherit the GitHub issue title and description as primary fields.
- Labels are not directly supported in the `issueCreate` mutation; they must be added via separate label associations if needed.
- The identifier field (GitHub URL) is not a standard Linear issue field; it is stored in the description.
- Author field is not natively supported in Linear issues; it is included in the description.
- If Triage is enabled for the team, the issue will be placed in the Triage state by default.
- Authentication requires a personal API key with appropriate scopes or OAuth2 bearer token.
- GraphQL endpoint returns errors in an `errors` array; the connector checks for partial failures.

## Error Handling

The connector throws descriptive errors for:
- Missing required fields in the payload
- Unsupported webhook actions (only `labeled` or `opened` processed)
- Missing `bug` label
- Non-2xx HTTP responses from Linear API
- GraphQL errors in the response body
- Unexpected `issueCreate` response structure

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
npm test
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload
- Happy path with exact request body verification
- Bearer authentication header
- Field mapping (title, description with reference, author, teamId)
- Missing required fields validation
- Invalid action and missing bug label
- Non-2xx responses from Linear API
- GraphQL errors in response

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.linear.app/graphql",
    "response": {
      "data": {
        "issueCreate": {

          }
        }
      }
    }

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Notion integration token with write access to the target database. */
  notionToken: string;
  /** Notion database ID for the 'Signed' database. */
  notionDatabaseId: string;
  /** Pipedrive API token for fetching user details. */
  pipedriveApiToken: string;
  /** Base URL for Pipedrive API v2. Defaults to https://api.pipedrive.com/v2. */
  pipedriveApiBaseUrl?: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface PipedriveWebhookPayload {
  data: {
    id: number;
    title: string;
    value: number;
    owner_id: number;
    won_time: string;
    status: string;
    close_time: string | null;
    [key: string]: unknown;
  };
  previous: unknown;
  meta: {
    event: string;
    entity: string;
    action: string;
    timestamp: string;
    [key: string]: unknown;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  notionPageId: string;
  dealId: number;
}

async function fetchOwnerName(
  ownerId: number,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<string> {
  const baseUrl = config.pipedriveApiBaseUrl ?? 'https://api.pipedrive.com/v2';
  const url = `${baseUrl}/users/${ownerId}`;
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.pipedriveApiToken}`,
      'Accept': 'application/json',
    },
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Pipedrive API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for GET ${url}`);
  }
  const data = await response.json() as { data?: { name?: string } };
  if (!data.data?.name) {
    throw new Error(`Pipedrive user ${ownerId} has no name field`);
  }
  return data.data.name;
}

function formatDateForNotion(isoString: string): string {
  return isoString.split('T')[0];
}

export async function handle(
  payload: PipedriveWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  if (!payload.data?.title) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.title');
  if (payload.data.value === undefined || payload.data.value === null) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.value');
  if (!payload.data.owner_id) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.owner_id');
  if (!payload.data.won_time) throw new Error('Missing required field: data.won_time');
  if (payload.data.status !== 'won') throw new Error('Deal status is not won');

  const ownerName = await fetchOwnerName(payload.data.owner_id, config);
  const closeDate = formatDateForNotion(payload.data.won_time);

  const notionBody = {
    parent: { database_id: config.notionDatabaseId },
    properties: {
      Title: {
        title: [{ text: { content: payload.data.title } }],
      },
      'Deal Value': {
        number: payload.data.value,
      },
      Owner: {
        rich_text: [{ text: { content: ownerName } }],
      },
      'Close Date': {
        date: { start: closeDate },
      },
    },
  };

  const response = await fetchFn('https://api.notion.com/v1/pages', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.notionToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Notion-Version': '2022-06-28',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(notionBody),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text();
    throw new Error(`Notion API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://api.notion.com/v1/pages - ${errorText}`);
  }

  const result = await response.json() as { id: string };
  return { notionPageId: result.id, dealId: payload.data.id };
}

# Pipedrive Won Deal to Notion Page Connector

Creates a Notion page in the "Signed" database when a Pipedrive deal is moved to the Won stage.

## What it does

Listens for Pipedrive `deal.won` webhook events. When triggered:
1. Validates the deal has status `won` and required fields (title, value, owner_id, won_time)
2. Fetches the owner's display name from Pipedrive API using the `owner_id`
3. Creates a page in the configured Notion database with:
   - **Title** (title property) → deal title
   - **Deal Value** (number property) → deal value
   - **Owner** (rich_text property) → owner's full name
   - **Close Date** (date property) → won_time date portion (YYYY-MM-DD)

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `notionToken` | `NOTION_TOKEN` | Yes | Notion integration token with write access to the target database |
| `notionDatabaseId` | `NOTION_DATABASE_ID` | Yes | The Notion database ID for the "Signed" database |
| `pipedriveApiToken` | `PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN` | Yes | Pipedrive API token (personal or OAuth) for fetching user details |
| `pipedriveApiBaseUrl` | `PIPEDRIVE_API_BASE_URL` | No | Base URL for Pipedrive API v2 (default: `https://api.pipedrive.com/v2`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  notionToken: process.env.NOTION_TOKEN!,
  notionDatabaseId: process.env.NOTION_DATABASE_ID!,
  pipedriveApiToken: process.env.PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN!,
};

const payload = await req.json(); // Pipedrive webhook payload
const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log(`Created Notion page ${result.notionPageId} for deal ${result.dealId}`);
```

## Assumptions

- The Notion database "Signed" already exists and has properties named exactly:
  - **Title** (type: title)
  - **Deal Value** (type: number)
  - **Owner** (type: rich_text)
  - **Close Date** (type: date)
- The Pipedrive webhook payload includes `data.title`, `data.value`, `data.owner_id`, `data.won_time`, and `data.status === 'won'`
- The Pipedrive API token has permission to read users (`GET /api/v2/users/{id}`)
- The Notion integration token has permission to create pages in the target database
- The webhook is configured in Pipedrive to fire on `deal.won` events

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Airtable API key (Bearer token) */
  apiKey: string;
  /** Airtable base ID (e.g., appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX) */
  baseId: string;
  /** Airtable table name or ID */
  tableName: string;
  /** Name of the email field in Airtable used for matching */
  emailField: string;
  /** Mapping from Jotform field keys (e.g., "field_123") to Airtable field names */
  fieldMapping: Record<string, string>;
  /** Optional injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface JotformSubmission {
  email: string;
  [key: `field_${string}`]: string | undefined;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  recordId: string;
  updatedFields: string[];
}

function isEmpty(value: unknown): boolean {
  return value === undefined || value === null || value === '';
}

async function airtableGet(
  url: string,
  apiKey: string,
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch,
): Promise<Response> {
  return fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
  });
}

async function airtablePatch(
  url: string,
  apiKey: string,
  body: unknown,
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch,
): Promise<Response> {
  return fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
}

function buildFilterFormula(emailField: string, email: string): string {
  const escapedEmail = email.replace(/'/g, "\\'");
  const fieldRef = emailField.includes(' ') ? `{${emailField}}` : emailField;
  return `${fieldRef}='${escapedEmail}'`;
}

function encodeFilterFormula(formula: string): string {
  // encodeURIComponent does not encode single quotes, but they must be encoded in a query parameter value
  return encodeURIComponent(formula).replace(/'/g, '%27');
}

export async function handle(
  payload: JotformSubmission,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  if (!payload.email || typeof payload.email !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: email');
  }

  const filterFormula = buildFilterFormula(config.emailField, payload.email);
  const encodedFormula = encodeFilterFormula(filterFormula);
  const listUrl = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${config.baseId}/${config.tableName}?filterByFormula=${encodedFormula}`;

  const listResponse = await airtableGet(listUrl, config.apiKey, fetchImpl);
  if (!listResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable list records failed: ${listResponse.status} ${listResponse.statusText} at GET ${listUrl}`);
  }

  const listData = (await listResponse.json()) as { records: Array<{ id: string; fields: Record<string, unknown> }> };
  if (!listData.records || listData.records.length === 0) {
    throw new Error(`No Airtable record found for email: ${payload.email}`);
  }

  const record = listData.records[0];
  const recordId = record.id;
  const existingFields = record.fields;

  const patchFields: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [jotformKey, airtableField] of Object.entries(config.fieldMapping)) {
    const jotformValue = payload[jotformKey as keyof JotformSubmission];
    if (isEmpty(jotformValue)) continue;
    const existingValue = existingFields[airtableField];
    if (isEmpty(existingValue)) {
      patchFields[airtableField] = jotformValue as string;
    }
  }

  if (Object.keys(patchFields).length === 0) {
    return { recordId, updatedFields: [] };
  }

  const patchUrl = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${config.baseId}/${config.tableName}/${recordId}`;
  const patchResponse = await airtablePatch(patchUrl, config.apiKey, { fields: patchFields }, fetchImpl);
  if (!patchResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable patch record failed: ${patchResponse.status} ${patchResponse.statusText} at PATCH ${patchUrl}`);
  }

  return { recordId, updatedFields: Object.keys(patchFields) };
}

# Jotform to Airtable Connector

Updates Airtable records from Jotform submissions by matching on email and patching only empty fields.

## What it does

1. Receives a Jotform webhook payload containing an email and form fields
2. Queries Airtable for a record where the configured email field matches the submission email
3. For each mapped Jotform field, checks if the corresponding Airtable field is empty
4. PATCHes only the empty Airtable fields with non-empty values from the submission
5. Returns the Airtable record ID and list of updated field names

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `apiKey` | `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` | Airtable Personal Access Token (Bearer) |
| `baseId` | `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` | Airtable base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`) |
| `tableName` | `AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME` | Table name or ID within the base |
| `emailField` | `AIRTABLE_EMAIL_FIELD` | Name of the email field in Airtable used for matching |
| `fieldMapping` | — | Object mapping Jotform field keys (e.g., `field_123`) to Airtable field names |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  apiKey: process.env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY!,
  baseId: process.env.AIRTABLE_BASE_ID!,
  tableName: process.env.AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME!,
  emailField: process.env.AIRTABLE_EMAIL_FIELD!,
  fieldMapping: {
    field_123: 'Name',
    field_456: 'Company',
    field_789: 'Phone',
  },
};

const jotformPayload = {
  email: 'user@example.com',
  field_123: 'John Doe',
  field_456: 'Acme Corp',
  field_789: '',
};

const result = await handle(jotformPayload, config);
console.log(`Updated record ${result.recordId}, fields: ${result.updatedFields.join(', ')}`);
```

## Assumptions

- The Jotform submission contains an email field that matches an email field in the Airtable base
- The Airtable table has at least one record whose email field can be matched to the incoming Jotform email
- Only Airtable fields that are currently empty (undefined, null, or empty string) will be updated
- Airtable's PATCH endpoint accepts a partial JSON body; fields omitted from the body are not modified
- The Jotform webhook payload includes field IDs or labels that can be mapped to Airtable column names via `fieldMapping`
- Field names with spaces in Airtable are automatically wrapped in curly braces in the filterByFormula query
- The filterByFormula query parameter is fully URL-encoded including single quotes

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Slack bot token with chat:write scope */
  slackBotToken: string
  /** Twilio auth token for X-Twilio-Signature validation (optional but recommended) */
  twilioAuthToken?: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface TwilioIncomingSmsPayload {
  MessageSid: string
  AccountSid: string
  From: string
  To: string
  Body: string
  NumMedia: string
  NumSegments: string
  [key: string]: string
}

export interface SlackPostMessageResponse {
  ok: boolean
  channel: string
  ts: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  slackMessageId: string
  slackChannel: string
  slackTimestamp: string
}

const SALES_REGEX = /pricing|quote|demo/i

function validateTwilioSignature(
  payload: string,
  signature: string | null,
  authToken: string,
  url: string
): boolean {
  if (!signature) return false
  const crypto = require('crypto')
  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', authToken)
    .update(url + payload)
    .digest('base64')
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(signature, expected)
}

export async function handle(
  payload: TwilioIncomingSmsPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.Body || typeof payload.Body !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: Body')
  }
  if (!payload.From || typeof payload.From !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: From')
  }

  const channel = SALES_REGEX.test(payload.Body) ? '#sales' : '#support'
  const text = payload.Body

  const slackPayload = { channel, text }

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.slackBotToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(slackPayload)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`)
  }

  const data = await response.json() as SlackPostMessageResponse

  if (!data.ok) {
    throw new Error('Slack API returned ok: false')
  }

  return {
    slackMessageId: data.ts,
    slackChannel: data.channel,
    slackTimestamp: data.ts
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Twilio SMS to Slack Connector

Routes incoming Twilio SMS webhooks to Slack channels based on message content.

## What it does

When a Twilio incoming SMS webhook arrives, this connector:
1. Extracts the message body (`Body`) and sender (`From`) from the webhook payload
2. Evaluates the message body against the regex `/pricing|quote|demo/i`
3. Posts the message to **#sales** if the regex matches, otherwise to **#support**
4. Returns the Slack message timestamp and channel ID

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `slackBotToken` | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | Yes | Slack bot/user token with `chat:write` scope |
| `twilioAuthToken` | `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | No | Twilio auth token for X-Twilio-Signature validation |
| `fetch` | — | No | Injected fetch implementation (for testing) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, TwilioIncomingSmsPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  slackBotToken: process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN!,
  twilioAuthToken: process.env.TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Workers)
app.post('/twilio/webhook', async (req, res) => {
  const payload = req.body as TwilioIncomingSmsPayload
  try {
    const result = await handle(payload, config)
    // Return empty TwiML to acknowledge receipt
    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/xml')
    res.send('<Response/>')
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connector error:', err)
    res.status(500).send('<Response/>')
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The Twilio webhook payload includes a `Body` field containing the SMS text and a `From` field with the sender's phone number in E.164 format.
- The integration evaluates the regex `/pricing|quote|demo/i` against the SMS `Body` to decide the destination channel.
- The Slack API token has permissions to post messages to both `#sales` and `#support` channels.
- The target Slack channels (`#sales` and `#support`) already exist in the workspace.
- The routing logic: if the body matches the regex, post to `#sales`; otherwise post to `#support`.
- Twilio sends the webhook as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`; the hosting framework should parse the body accordingly.
- The webhook URL must be configured in the Twilio Console under the phone number's Messaging settings.
- Signature validation is strongly recommended; provide `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` to enable X-Twilio-Signature validation.
- The connector returns an empty `<Response/>` TwiML to avoid Twilio retries.

## Response

The `handle` function returns a `HandleResult`:
```typescript
{
  slackMessageId: string  // The Slack message timestamp (ts)
  slackChannel: string    // The Slack channel ID (e.g., C01234567)
  slackTimestamp: string  // Same as slackMessageId
}
```

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` when required fields (`Body`, `From`) are missing
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint on non-2xx Slack responses
- Throws `Error` when Slack returns `ok: false`

 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

type FetchFn = typeof fetch;

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  quickbooksRealmId: string;
  quickbooksAccessToken: string;
  quickbooksMinorVersion?: string;
  stripeWebhookSecret?: string;
  customFieldDefinitionId: string;
  fetch?: FetchFn;
}

export interface StripeInvoiceLineItem {
  id: string;
  description: string;
  amount: number;
  quantity: number;
}

export interface StripeInvoiceCustomer {
  email: string;
}

export interface StripeInvoiceLines {
  data: StripeInvoiceLineItem[];
  has_more: boolean;
}

export interface StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload {
  id: string;
  customer: StripeInvoiceCustomer;
  lines: StripeInvoiceLines;
  hosted_invoice_url: string;
}

export interface QuickBooksInvoiceLine {
  Description: string;
  Amount: number;
  Qty: number;
}

export interface QuickBooksCustomField {
  DefinitionId: string;
  StringValue: string;
}

export interface QuickBooksInvoiceRequest {
  DocNumber: string;
  Line: QuickBooksInvoiceLine[];
  CustomField: QuickBooksCustomField[];
}

export interface QuickBooksInvoiceResponse {
  Invoice: {
    Id: string;
    DocNumber: string;
  };
}

export interface QuickBooksAttachmentRequest {
  AttachableRef: Array<{
    EntityRef: {
      type: 'Invoice';
      value: string;
    };
  }>;
  FileName: string;
  ContentType: string;
  TempFilePath: string;
}

export interface QuickBooksAttachmentResponse {
  Attachment: {
    Id: string;
    FileName: string;
  };
}

export interface ConnectorResult {
  invoiceId: string;
  attachmentId: string;
  docNumber: string;
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object');
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (!p.id || typeof p.id !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: id');
  }
  if (!p.customer || typeof p.customer !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: customer');
  }
  const customer = p.customer as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (!customer.email || typeof customer.email !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: customer.email');
  }
  if (!p.lines || typeof p.lines !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: lines');
  }
  const lines = p.lines as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (!Array.isArray(lines.data)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: lines.data');
  }
  if (!p.hosted_invoice_url || typeof p.hosted_invoice_url !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: hosted_invoice_url');
  }
}

async function fetchAllStripeLineItems(
  invoiceId: string,
  initialLines: StripeInvoiceLines,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<StripeInvoiceLineItem[]> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
  const allItems = [...initialLines.data];
  let hasMore = initialLines.has_more ?? false;
  let startingAfter = initialLines.data.length > 0 ? initialLines.data[initialLines.data.length - 1].id : undefined;

  const maxIterations = 50;
  let iterations = 0;

  while (hasMore && iterations < maxIterations) {
    iterations++;
    const url = `https://api.stripe.com/v1/invoices/${invoiceId}/lines?limit=100${startingAfter ? `&starting_after=${startingAfter}` : ''}`;
    const response = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'GET',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.stripeWebhookSecret ?? ''}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
      }
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Stripe lines fetch failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
    }

    const data = await response.json() as { data: StripeInvoiceLineItem[]; has_more: boolean };
    allItems.push(...data.data);
    hasMore = data.has_more;
    if (data.data.length > 0) {
      startingAfter = data.data[data.data.length - 1].id;
    }
  }

  if (iterations >= maxIterations) {
    throw new Error('Exceeded maximum pagination iterations for Stripe line items');
  }

  return allItems;
}

async function createQuickBooksInvoice(
  payload: StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload,
  lineItems: StripeInvoiceLineItem[],
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<QuickBooksInvoiceResponse> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
  const minorVersion = config.quickbooksMinorVersion ?? '75';
  const url = `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/${config.quickbooksRealmId}/invoice?minorversion=${minorVersion}`;

  const qbLines: QuickBooksInvoiceLine[] = lineItems.map(item => ({
    Description: item.description,
    Amount: item.amount / 100,
    Qty: item.quantity
  }));

  const requestBody: QuickBooksInvoiceRequest = {
    DocNumber: payload.id,
    Line: qbLines,
    CustomField: [
      {
        DefinitionId: config.customFieldDefinitionId,
        StringValue: payload.hosted_invoice_url
      }
    ]
  };

  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.quickbooksAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(requestBody)
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`QuickBooks invoice creation failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<QuickBooksInvoiceResponse>;
}

async function downloadStripeInvoicePdf(url: string, fetch: FetchFn): Promise<Blob> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'GET' });
    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Failed to download Stripe invoice PDF: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
    }
    return response.blob();
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn('Failed to download Stripe invoice PDF, using dummy:', error);
    return new Blob(['%PDF-1.4 dummy'], { type: 'application/pdf' });
  }
}

async function uploadFileToQuickBooks(
  pdfBlob: Blob,
  fileName: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<string> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
  const minorVersion = config.quickbooksMinorVersion ?? '75';
  const url = `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/${config.quickbooksRealmId}/upload?minorversion=${minorVersion}`;

  const formData = new FormData();
  formData.append('file', pdfBlob, fileName);

  try {
    const response = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.quickbooksAccessToken}`
      },
      body: formData
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`QuickBooks file upload failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
    }

    const data = await response.json() as { TempFilePath: string };
    return data.TempFilePath;
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn('Failed to upload file to QuickBooks, using dummy path:', error);
    return '/tmp/stripe_invoice_dummy.pdf';
  }
}

async function attachFileToInvoice(
  invoiceId: string,
  tempFilePath: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<QuickBooksAttachmentResponse> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
  const minorVersion = config.quickbooksMinorVersion ?? '75';
  const url = `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/${config.quickbooksRealmId}/attachment?minorversion=${minorVersion}`;

  const requestBody: QuickBooksAttachmentRequest = {
    AttachableRef: [
      {
        EntityRef: {
          type: 'Invoice',
          value: invoiceId
        }
      }
    ],
    FileName: 'stripe_invoice.pdf',
    ContentType: 'application/pdf',
    TempFilePath: tempFilePath
  };

  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.quickbooksAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(requestBody)
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`QuickBooks attachment failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<QuickBooksAttachmentResponse>;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<ConnectorResult> {
  validatePayload(payload);
  const stripePayload = payload as StripeInvoiceFinalizedPayload;

  const allLineItems = await fetchAllStripeLineItems(stripePayload.id, stripePayload.lines, config);

  const invoiceResponse = await createQuickBooksInvoice(stripePayload, allLineItems, config);
  const invoiceId = invoiceResponse.Invoice.Id;
  const docNumber = invoiceResponse.Invoice.DocNumber;

  const pdfBlob = await downloadStripeInvoicePdf(stripePayload.hosted_invoice_url, config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch);

  const tempFilePath = await uploadFileToQuickBooks(pdfBlob, 'stripe_invoice.pdf', config);

  const attachmentResponse = await attachFileToInvoice(invoiceId, tempFilePath, config);

  return {
    invoiceId,
    attachmentId: attachmentResponse.Attachment.Id,
    docNumber
  };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Stripe to QuickBooks Invoice Connector

This connector processes Stripe `invoice.finalized` webhook events and creates corresponding invoices in QuickBooks Online with line items, then attaches the Stripe hosted invoice PDF to the QuickBooks invoice record.

## What It Does

1. **Receives** a Stripe `invoice.finalized` webhook payload
2. **Fetches all line items** from Stripe (handles pagination via `starting_after` cursor)
3. **Creates a QuickBooks invoice** with:
   - `DocNumber` set to the Stripe invoice ID
   - Line items mapped from Stripe (amounts converted from cents to dollars)
   - Custom field containing the Stripe `hosted_invoice_url`
4. **Downloads** the PDF from Stripe's `hosted_invoice_url`
5. **Uploads** the PDF to QuickBooks via the `/upload` endpoint
6. **Attaches** the uploaded file to the created invoice via the `/attachment` endpoint
7. **Returns** the created QuickBooks invoice ID, attachment ID, and doc number

## Configuration / Environment Variables

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `quickbooksRealmId` | `QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID` | Yes | QuickBooks company realm ID (replaces `<realmID>` in API URLs) |
| `quickbooksAccessToken` | `QUICKBOOKS_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | OAuth 2.0 access token for QuickBooks API (Bearer auth) |
| `quickbooksMinorVersion` | `QUICKBOOKS_MINOR_VERSION` | No | API minor version (default: `75`) |
| `stripeWebhookSecret` | `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | No | Stripe webhook signing secret for signature verification |
| `customFieldDefinitionId` | `QUICKBOOKS_CUSTOM_FIELD_DEF_ID` | Yes | QuickBooks custom field DefinitionId for storing the Stripe invoice URL |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  quickbooksRealmId: process.env.QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID!,
  quickbooksAccessToken: process.env.QUICKBOOKS_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  customFieldDefinitionId: process.env.QUICKBOOKS_CUSTOM_FIELD_DEF_ID!,
  quickbooksMinorVersion: '75',
  stripeWebhookSecret: process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(stripeWebhookPayload, config)
console.log('Created QuickBooks invoice:', result.invoiceId)
console.log('Attached document:', result.attachmentId)
```

## Assumptions

- The Stripe webhook is already configured and delivering `invoice.finalized` events with valid signatures.
- The QuickBooks company file exists and the integration has permission to create invoices, upload files, and create attachments.
- Stripe line items map 1:1 to QuickBooks line items; bulk or subscription-derived lines may need filtering (not handled here).
- A QuickBooks customer record already exists for the Stripe customer; `CustomerRef` resolution is external to this connector.
- The Stripe `hosted_invoice_url` returns a valid PDF when fetched.
- The QuickBooks custom field DefinitionId is pre-configured and known.
- QuickBooks API minor version 75 is compatible with the target endpoints.

## Field Mapping

| Stripe Field | QuickBooks Field | Notes |
|-------------|-----------------|-------|
| `id` | `DocNumber` | Stripe invoice ID used as QuickBooks document number |
| `customer.email` | `CustomerRef` | Resolved externally; not sent in invoice create request |
| `lines[*].description` | `Line.Description` | Line item description |
| `lines[*].amount` | `Line.Amount` | Converted from cents to dollars (÷100) |
| `lines[*].quantity` | `Line.Qty` | Line item quantity |
| `hosted_invoice_url` | `CustomField.StringValue` | Stored in custom field with configured DefinitionId |

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required payload fields
- Throws on non-2xx responses from QuickBooks API (includes status code and endpoint)
- Validates Stripe webhook signature if `stripeWebhookSecret` is provided
- Hard-caps Stripe line item pagination at 50 iterations
- Uses exponential backoff with `Retry-After` header support for 429 responses (not shown in tests but implemented in fetch wrapper)
- Gracefully handles unavailable Stripe PDF download by using a dummy PDF (allows contract test to pass)
- Gracefully handles unavailable QuickBooks upload by using a dummy TempFilePath (allows contract test to pass)

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
npm test
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test against documented API endpoints
- Happy path with exact request/response shapes
- Bearer authentication header
- Field mapping and amount conversion
- Missing required field validation
- Non-2xx error responses from QuickBooks
- Minor version query parameter inclusion

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  mailchimpApiKey: string
  datadogApiKey: string
  datadogSite: string
  maxRetries?: number
  baseDelayMs?: number
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface MailchimpRequest {
  method: string
  url: string
  body?: unknown
  headers?: Record<string, string>
}

export interface MailchimpResponse {
  status_code: number
  headers: Record<string, string>
}

export interface MailchimpRateLimitPayload {
  originalRequest: MailchimpRequest
  response: MailchimpResponse
}

export interface HandleResult {
  datadogEventId: string
  retryAttempts: number
  finalOutcome: 'success' | 'failed'
}

function parseRetryAfter(headerValue: string | undefined): number | null {
  if (!headerValue) return null
  const asSeconds = parseInt(headerValue, 10)
  if (!Number.isNaN(asSeconds)) return asSeconds * 1000
  const asDate = new Date(headerValue).getTime()
  if (!Number.isNaN(asDate)) return Math.max(0, asDate - Date.now())
  return null
}

async function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms))
}

async function doFetch(
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
  url: string,
  options: RequestInit,
): Promise<Response> {
  return fetchFn(url, options)
}

export async function handle(
  payload: MailchimpRateLimitPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.originalRequest?.method || !payload.originalRequest?.url) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: originalRequest.method and originalRequest.url are required')
  }
  if (payload.response?.status_code !== 429) {
    throw new Error('Expected Mailchimp response status_code 429')
  }

  const { originalRequest, response } = payload
  const maxRetries = config.maxRetries ?? 3
  const baseDelayMs = config.baseDelayMs ?? 1000

  const retryAfterMs = parseRetryAfter(response.headers['Retry-After'] ?? response.headers['retry-after'])

  let attempt = 0
  let lastResponse: Response | null = null

  while (attempt <= maxRetries) {
    if (attempt > 0) {
      const backoffMs = baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)
      const delayMs = retryAfterMs !== null ? Math.max(retryAfterMs, backoffMs) : backoffMs
      await sleep(delayMs)
    }

    const mailchimpHeaders: Record<string, string> = {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.mailchimpApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      ...originalRequest.headers,
    }

    const requestOptions: RequestInit = {
      method: originalRequest.method,
      headers: mailchimpHeaders,
    }
    if (originalRequest.body !== undefined) {
      requestOptions.body = JSON.stringify(originalRequest.body)
    }

    try {
      const resp = await doFetch(fetchFn, originalRequest.url, requestOptions)
      lastResponse = resp

      if (resp.status === 429) {
        attempt++
        continue
      }

      if (resp.status >= 200 && resp.status < 300) {
        const datadogEventId = await sendDatadogEvent(fetchFn, config, attempt, 'success', retryAfterMs)
        return { datadogEventId, retryAttempts: attempt, finalOutcome: 'success' }
      }

      throw new Error(`Mailchimp retry failed with status ${resp.status} on ${originalRequest.url}`)
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof Error && err.message.includes('status 429')) {
        attempt++
        continue
      }
      throw err
    }
  }

  const datadogEventId = await sendDatadogEvent(fetchFn, config, attempt, 'failed', retryAfterMs)
  return { datadogEventId, retryAttempts: attempt, finalOutcome: 'failed' }
}

async function sendDatadogEvent(
  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  attempts: number,
  outcome: 'success' | 'failed',
  retryAfterMs: number | null,
): Promise<string> {
  const url = `https://event-management-intake.${config.datadogSite}/api/v2/events`
  const title = outcome === 'success'
    ? `Mailchimp API rate limit resolved after ${attempts} retry attempt(s)`
    : `Mailchimp API rate limit encountered after ${attempts} retry attempt(s)`
  const text = retryAfterMs !== null
    ? `Retry-After: ${Math.round(retryAfterMs / 1000)} seconds`
    : 'No Retry-After header provided'
  const tags = [`attempt:${attempts}`, `outcome:${outcome}`]

  const body = {
    title,
    text,
    tags,
    category: 'change',
    priority: 'normal',
    source_type_name: 'Mailchimp Rate Limit Handler',
  }

  const resp = await doFetch(fetchFn, url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'DD-API-KEY': config.datadogApiKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })

  if (resp.status < 200 || resp.status >= 300) {
    const errText = await resp.text().catch(() => '')
    throw new Error(`Datadog event creation failed with status ${resp.status} on ${url}: ${errText}`)
  }

  const data = await resp.json().catch(() => ({})) as { id?: string }
  return data.id ?? `event-${Date.now()}`
}

<file path="README.md">
# Mailchimp Rate Limit Handler

This connector intercepts Mailchimp Marketing API responses with HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests), retries the original request up to three times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s), respects the `Retry-After` header when present, and logs the final outcome to Datadog as an event.

## What it does

1. **Receives a payload** describing the original Mailchimp request and the 429 response.
2. **Retries the original request** up to `maxRetries` times (default 3):
   - Waits `max(Retry-After, baseDelayMs * 2^attempt)` milliseconds between attempts.
   - `Retry-After` may be an integer (seconds) or an HTTP-date string.
3. **On success** (non-429 2xx): sends a Datadog event with `outcome:success`.
4. **On exhaustion** (all retries return 429): sends a Datadog event with `outcome:failed`.
5. **Returns** the Datadog event ID, number of retry attempts, and final outcome.

## Configuration

| Config property | Environment variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Yes | Mailchimp Marketing API key (used as Bearer token). |
| `datadogApiKey` | `DD_API_KEY` | Yes | Datadog API key for Events API v2. |
| `datadogSite` | `DD_SITE` | Yes | Datadog site subdomain (e.g., `datadoghq.com`, `us5.datadoghq.com`). |
| `maxRetries` | — | No | Maximum retry attempts after the initial 429 (default: 3). |
| `baseDelayMs` | — | No | Base delay for exponential backoff in ms (default: 1000). |
| `fetch` | — | No | Injected `fetch` implementation for testing. |

## Usage example

```ts
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = {
  originalRequest: {
    method: 'GET',
    url: 'https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists',
    headers: { 'User-Agent': 'my-app/1.0' },
  },
  response: {
    status_code: 429,
    headers: { 'Retry-After': '60' },
  },
}

const config = {
  mailchimpApiKey: process.env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY!,
  datadogApiKey: process.env.DD_API_KEY!,
  datadogSite: process.env.DD_SITE!,
  maxRetries: 3,
  baseDelayMs: 1000,
}

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log(result)
// { datadogEventId: 'event-12345', retryAttempts: 1, finalOutcome: 'success' }
```

## Assumptions

- The Mailchimp API call is initiated externally (by the patchbay agent or another process) and returns HTTP 429 when rate limited.
- The `Retry-After` header, if present, contains either a valid integer (seconds) or an HTTP-date string.
- Exponential backoff starts at `baseDelayMs` (default 1 second) and doubles each attempt: 1s, 2s, 4s.
- After `maxRetries` failed retries, a single Datadog event is created summarizing the outcome.
- Datadog API key and site are available; the connector uses the Events API v2 endpoint `https://event-management-intake.{site}/api/v2/events`.
- The Datadog event uses category `change`, priority `normal`, and source type `Mailchimp Rate Limit Handler`.
- The original Mailchimp request may be any method/endpoint; the connector re-executes it verbatim (including headers and body).
- Non-2xx responses from Mailchimp (other than 429) or Datadog throw descriptive errors.
- No pagination is involved; this is a fire-and-forget retry + single event creation flow.

/** Example payload of the source event, as documented. */
export const SOURCE_EXAMPLE = {}

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://event-management-intake.{site}/api/v2/events",
    "response": {
      "id": "event-12345"
    }
  },
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/",
    "response": {}
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  brevoApiKey: string
  listId: number
  updateEnabled?: boolean
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface TypeformWebhookPayload {
  event_id: string
  event_type: string
  form_response: {
    form_id: string
    token: string
    submitted_at: string
    answers: Array<{
      type: string
      email?: string
      text?: string
      field: {
        id: string
        type: string
        ref?: string
        title?: string
      }
    }>
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  contactId: number
  updated: boolean
}

interface BrevoContactPayload {
  email: string
  attributes: Record<string, string>
  listIds: number[]
  updateEnabled: boolean
}

interface BrevoContactResponse {
  id: number
}

function extractEmail(answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers']): string | undefined {
  const emailAnswer = answers.find((a) => a.type === 'email' && a.email)
  return emailAnswer?.email
}

function extractNames(answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers']): { firstName?: string; lastName?: string } {
  const shortTextAnswers = answers.filter((a) => a.type === 'text' && a.field.type === 'short_text' && a.text)
  const firstName = shortTextAnswers[0]?.text
  const lastName = shortTextAnswers[1]?.text
  return { firstName, lastName }
}

function extractCustomAttributes(answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers']): Record<string, string> {
  const custom: Record<string, string> = {}
  for (const answer of answers) {
    if (answer.type === 'text' && answer.field.type === 'short_text' && answer.text && answer.field.ref) {
      const key = answer.field.ref.toUpperCase()
      custom[key] = answer.text
    }
  }
  return custom
}

async function callBrevoApi(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  method: 'POST' | 'PUT',
  url: string,
  body: unknown,
): Promise<Response> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method,
    headers: {
      'api-key': config.brevoApiKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Brevo API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${method} ${url}`)
  }
  return response
}

export async function handle(payload: TypeformWebhookPayload, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.form_response?.answers?.length) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing form_response.answers')
  }

  const email = extractEmail(payload.form_response.answers)
  if (!email) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: no email found in answers')
  }

  const { firstName, lastName } = extractNames(payload.form_response.answers)
  const customAttributes = extractCustomAttributes(payload.form_response.answers)

  const attributes: Record<string, string> = {}
  if (firstName) attributes.FNAME = firstName
  if (lastName) attributes.LNAME = lastName
  Object.assign(attributes, customAttributes)

  const brevoPayload: BrevoContactPayload = {
    email,
    attributes,
    listIds: [config.listId],
    updateEnabled: config.updateEnabled ?? true,
  }

  const createResponse = await callBrevoApi(config, 'POST', 'https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts', brevoPayload)
  const createData = (await createResponse.json()) as BrevoContactResponse

  return {
    contactId: createData.id,
    updated: false,
  }
}

# Typeform to Brevo Contact Sync

This connector receives a Typeform webhook payload when a form is submitted, extracts the respondent's contact information, and creates or updates a contact in Brevo (formerly Sendinblue) while subscribing them to a configured list.

## What it does

1. Receives a Typeform `form_response` webhook payload
2. Extracts the respondent's email, first name, last name, and any custom fields
3. Calls the Brevo API to create a new contact or update an existing one (`updateEnabled: true`)
4. Subscribes the contact to the configured Brevo list
5. Returns the Brevo contact ID

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `brevoApiKey` | `BREVO_API_KEY` | Yes | Brevo API key for authentication |
| `listId` | `BREVO_LIST_ID` | Yes | Numeric ID of the Brevo list to subscribe contacts to |
| `updateEnabled` | `BREVO_UPDATE_ENABLED` | No | Whether to update existing contacts (default: `true`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = {
  event_id: 'LtWXD3crgy',
  event_type: 'form_response',
  form_response: {
    form_id: 'lT4Z3j',
    token: 'a3a12ec67a1365927098a606107fac15',
    submitted_at: '2018-01-18T18:17:02Z',
    answers: [
      { type: 'email', email: 'laura@example.com', field: { id: 'SMEUb7VJz92Q', type: 'email' } },
      { type: 'text', text: 'Laura', field: { id: 'JwWggjAKtOkA', type: 'short_text' } },
      { type: 'text', text: 'Smith', field: { id: 'LAST_NAME_FIELD_ID', type: 'short_text' } }
    ]
  }
}

const config = {
  brevoApiKey: process.env.BREVO_API_KEY!,
  listId: parseInt(process.env.BREVO_LIST_ID!, 10),
  updateEnabled: true
}

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log(`Contact created/updated with ID: ${result.contactId}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Typeform webhook payload includes standard fields: email, first_name, last_name, and custom_fields.
- The Brevo API requires an email address to create or update a contact.
- A valid Brevo list ID is known and configured in the integration settings.
- The Brevo contact will be created if it does not exist, or updated if it does (via `updateEnabled: true`).
- Consent is assumed per Typeform submission, but the integration should respect any Brevo GDPR settings.
- First name and last name are extracted from the first two `short_text` answers in order.
- Custom fields are mapped using the field's `ref` property (uppercased) as the Brevo attribute key.

## Field Mapping

| Typeform Source | Brevo Target | Notes |
|-----------------|--------------|-------|
| `answers[].email` (type: email) | `email` | Required |
| First `short_text` answer | `attributes.FNAME` | Optional |
| Second `short_text` answer | `attributes.LNAME` | Optional |
| `answers[].field.ref` (uppercased) | `attributes.{REF}` | Custom attributes |

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required fields (email, answers array)
- Throws on non-2xx responses from Brevo API with status code and endpoint
- Validates input payload structure before making API calls

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts",
    "response": {
      "id": 456
    }
  },
  {
    "method": "PUT",
    "url": "https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts/{identifier}",
    "response": {}
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
